<a id="page-base"></a>
# Codelessly: the base

You write Codelessly user interfaces directly as JSON files: screens, their layout, their look, their data and their
behavior. This file is the **base**: read it in full first; it is enough to build most pages. Everything else is on
a page of its own in this folder, linked from here and listed in the [index](#base-index) at the end (the same
index, with an A–Z of every name, is `index.md`). Open a page when you need what it covers; do not read the folder
end to end. On a page, *Patterns* is usually what you need; *Reference* holds the generated tables to look one prop
up. This describes `codelessly_api` 30.1.0; every example here is checked by a test.

<a id="base-the-model-in-one-table"></a>
## The model in one table

Each node is a Flutter widget as data. The base types and what they correspond to:

| Node type | Flutter |
|---|---|
| `canvas` | a screen (`Scaffold`: slots `body`, `appBar`, `bottomNavigationBar`, `floatingActionButton`) |
| `row`, `column` | `Row`, `Column`, which also carry their own padding and decoration (a `Container` around them) |
| `flex` | `Flex`: a row or column whose `direction` can change at a width |
| `stack` | `Stack` with `Positioned` / `Align` children |
| `box` | a `Container` with no child (a shape, a rule, an image) |
| `text`, `icon` | `Text` / `Text.rich`, `Icon` |
| `spacer` | `Spacer` (with no size) / `SizedBox` (with one) |
| buttons, inputs, `listView`, `gridView` | Material's buttons and inputs, `ListView.builder`, `GridView.builder` |

Single-child wrapper widgets are fields of the node they would wrap: `Padding`, `SizedBox`, `Expanded`,
`Flexible`, `Positioned`, `Align`, `ConstrainedBox` and `AspectRatio` are in its `layout`; `DecoratedBox`,
`ClipRRect` and shadows in its `decoration`; `Opacity` and `Visibility` are `opacity` and `visible`. A "card" is
one `column` with a fill, a radius and padding, not three nested widgets.

<a id="base-the-document"></a>
## The document

A layout document is one JSON object holding one or more **canvases** (screens) and all their nodes in a single
flat map:

| Key | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `schema` | Always 3 (`kSchemaVersion`). A schema-2 document (or one with none) loads, migrated in memory (`migrate2to3`). |
| `id` | The layout's id (optional). |
| `roots` | Canvas ids, in order: the screens of this page. |
| `nodes` | Every node, by id: `{"<id>": {"type": ..., ...}}`. A node's id is its key here. |
| `variables` | Variables per scope: `{"<canvas id>" \| "page_variables": [variable, ...]}`. |
| `conditions` | Conditions per canvas: `{"<canvas id>": [condition, ...]}`. |
| `scripts` | The layout's scripts (JavaScript), a list of script objects. |
| `breakpoints` | The project's breakpoints: `[{"id", "name", "minWidth", "width", "height"}]`; absent: the defaults. |

The smallest useful document: a canvas whose `body` slot holds a column with two texts. Every key not written takes
its default.

```json
{
  "schema": 3,
  "roots": ["home"],
  "nodes": {
    "home": {
      "type": "canvas",
      "name": "Home",
      "slots": {"body": "page"},
      "layout": {"width": 390, "height": 844},
      "decoration": {"fills": [{"color": "#FFFFFFFF"}]}
    },
    "page": {
      "type": "column",
      "children": ["title", "body"],
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 390}, "height": {"fill": 844}, "padding": 24},
      "props": {"crossAxisAlignment": "start", "spacing": 12}
    },
    "title": {
      "type": "text",
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 342}, "height": {"hug": 34}},
      "props": {"text": "Hello", "style": {"fontSize": 28, "fontWeight": 700, "color": "#FF111827"}}
    },
    "body": {
      "type": "text",
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 342}, "height": {"hug": 40}},
      "props": {
        "text": "A column with two texts, filling the screen's width.",
        "style": {"fontSize": 15, "height": 1.4, "color": "#FF4B5563"}
      }
    }
  }
}
```

A page is one file. A **site** is a folder with a `site.json` (its pages, components, theme and shared variables);
see [checking your work](#base-checking-your-work) and [components](#page-components).

<a id="base-theme-first-named-colours-and-text-styles"></a>
## Theme first: named colours and text styles

Declare a palette and a type scale once and name them everywhere, as a Flutter app declares `ThemeData` and its
widgets read `Theme.of(context)`. **Write the theme before the first node**: a name per colour the design uses, a
name per kind of text (display, title, body, label, eyebrow...).

The theme is the `theme` of the site manifest, `site.json`, next to the pages:

```json
{
  "schema": 3,
  "pages": ["home.json"],
  "theme": {
    "colors": {"ink": "#FF1B1B1B", "ember": "#FFE4572E", "paper": "#FFF6F1E9"},
    "textStyles": {
      "body": {"fontSize": 16, "height": 1.5, "color": "ink"},
      "title": {"from": "body", "fontSize": 32, "fontWeight": 700, "height": 1.2},
      "eyebrow": {"from": "body", "fontSize": 12, "letterSpacing": 2, "color": "ember"}
    },
    "media": [{"minWidth": 1024, "patch": {"textStyles": {"title": {"fontSize": 56}}}}]
  }
}
```

- `colors` maps a name to `"#AARRGGBB"` (or another colour's name). Wherever a colour is accepted (a fill, a
  stroke, a text's colour, a shadow, an input's border), write its name: `"color": "ember"`.
- `textStyles` maps a name to a [TextStyle](#type-TextStyle); a style may start `from` another (`"title": {"from":
  "body", "fontSize": 32}`). A text names its style: `"style": "title"`; to change a few fields of it,
  `"style": {"from": "title", "color": "ember"}`.
- In a binding a name is not read: bind the value, `"${theme.colors.ember}"`.
- Validation reports a name the theme does not have (`unknown_theme_name`, with the nearest name).

Controls (buttons, chips, fields, switches, pickers, tabs) take the colours and fonts their props leave unset
from the theme's roles (`primary`, `onPrimary`, `surface`, `onSurface`, `error`, `fontFamily`, `buttonRadius`...).
Without a theme they are neutral: ink on paper and the greys between. Nothing comes from Material's defaults or
from the app the layout is shown in.

**Light and dark.** `"dark": {"colors": {...}}` in the theme gives the colours that differ in dark mode, and
`"mode"` which one the site starts in (Flutter's `ThemeMode`: `system`, the default, follows the device; `light`;
`dark`). A theme switch is one action, `{"type": "setThemeMode", "mode": "${= theme.isDark ? 'light' : 'dark'}"}`:
every named colour, named text style and control of every screen follows, and the choice is kept for the next
visit. Read the mode as `${theme.mode}` and `${theme.isDark}`. Name colours in your text styles (`"color": "ink"`)
so they change with it: [dark mode](#theme-dark-mode).

**Fonts.** Declare the site's fonts in `site.json` as a pubspec does, files beside it: `"fonts": [{"family":
"Fraunces", "fonts": [{"asset": "fonts/Fraunces-Regular.ttf"}, {"asset": "fonts/Fraunces-Bold.ttf", "weight":
700}]}]` (`.ttf`, `.otf` or `.woff`; not `.woff2`). Text styles name the family; the render command and the app
load the files, and a family nobody declared is reported (`font_fallback`, naming the nodes): [fonts](#theme-fonts).

**Images.** A photo or illustration is an image fill naming a file beside `site.json` by its relative path:
`{"type": "image", "image": {"url": "images/hero.jpg", "fit": "cover"}}` (PNG, JPEG, WebP, GIF or SVG); a file
that is not there is reported (`image_failed`). Drawn art is a `customPaint`: [images and
illustration](#decoration-images).

A theme that changes with the screen size, every theme key: [theme](#page-theme).

<a id="base-nodes-ids-children-and-slots"></a>
## Nodes, ids, children and slots

`nodes` maps each node's **id** (the map key; do not repeat it inside the node) to the node. A parent lists its
children's ids in `children`, or names them in `slots`; a child does not name its parent. Every node except a
canvas has exactly one parent; `roots` lists the canvases, and a canvas is never a child. Ids are any text, and
**per document**: a page's actions and conditions name its own nodes, a component's ids are its own, and two pages
may both have a `title`. **Canvas ids are site-wide** (links name screens by them): never repeat one. A node's main keys: `type`, `layout`, `decoration`, `props` (the type's own parameters),
`children` / `slots`, `bind`, `actions`, `media`, `visible`, `opacity`, `name`.

Which types take children, which take named slots, which take neither:

| takes | types |
|---|---|
| `children` (a list of ids) | `stack`, `row`, `column`, `flex`, `variance`, `listView` (and slots loading, error, end, sectionHeader, reorderPlaceholder), `gridView` (and slots loading, error, end, reorderPlaceholder), `pageView`, `tabs`, `accordion`, `expansionTile` (and slots tile), `singlePlaceholder`, `slot` |
| `slots` (name → id) | `canvas` (body, appBar, floatingActionButton, bottomNavigationBar), `tableView` (cell, columnHeader, rowHeader, corner), `badge` (child), `listTile` (leading, title, subtitle, trailing), `modal` (trigger, content) |
| nothing | `box`, `text`, `icon`, `spacer`, `tabBar`, `pagination`, `textField`, `checkbox`, `switch`, `radio`, `slider`, `dropdown`, `datePicker`, `timePicker`, `dateTimeInput`, `segmentedButton`, `signature`, `elevatedButton`, `filledButton`, `textButton`, `outlinedButton`, `iconButton`, `floatingActionButton`, `chip`, `actionChip`, `choiceChip`, `filterChip`, `inputChip`, `appBar`, `navigationBar`, `bottomNavigationBar`, `divider`, `verticalDivider`, `circularProgressIndicator`, `activityIndicator`, `progressBar`, `radialGauge`, `gaugeMeter`, `chart`, `plotChart`, `barChart`, `lineChart`, `barcode`, `path`, `external`, `placeholder`, `video`, `embeddedVideo`, `audioPlayer`, `webView` |

A type with "no decoration" draws no box: put it inside a `box`, `row`, `column` or `stack` that has the fill or
border.

<a id="base-layout"></a>
## Layout

`layout` says how big a node is and where it sits in its parent. Every field: [layout fields](#layout-layout-fields).

<a id="base-width-and-height"></a>
### Width and height

Each axis has a **mode** and a **number**:

| JSON | Mode | Size |
|---|---|---|
| `120` | fixed | Exactly 120. |
| `{"hug": 120}` | hug | The size of the content (a text's lines, a row's children plus padding). |
| `{"fill": 120}` | fill | All the room the parent gives: the free space along a row's or column's main axis (shared by `flex`), the whole cross axis, the whole box of a stack or canvas slot. |
| `{"flexible": 120}` | flexible | Up to 120, less if a row or column runs out of room (main axis only). |

The number is the **design size**: the size of a fixed node, and the size used where a mode cannot apply (a fill
inside something that scrolls on that axis, or inside a parent that hugs that axis: `fill_fallback`). For `hug` and
`fill` it does not limit the size: cap a fill with `"constraints": {"maxWidth": 760}`. **A node without `width` or
`height` is 0 × 0 and draws nothing** (`zero_size`); give every node both, except a `canvas` and a `spacer`.

<a id="base-rows-columns-and-flex"></a>
### Rows, columns and flex

`row` and `column` lay their children along their **main axis**; `flex` is the same with a `direction`
(`horizontal` | `vertical`) a media rule can change. Props: `mainAxisAlignment` (default `start`;
`spaceBetween`...), `crossAxisAlignment` (default **`center`**: write `start` for left-aligned content, `stretch` to
fill), `spacing` (the gap), `wrap` (flow onto new lines, like `Wrap`; `runSpacing` between lines). A child of a row
or column may set in its own `layout`:

- `flex`: its share of the free space when its main-axis size is `fill` or `flexible` (default 1);
- `align`: its alignment in its slot, `[x, y]` from -1 to 1 or a name (`"centerRight"`);
- `order` (CSS `order`): children are laid out by ascending order, equal orders as listed;
- `basis` (CSS `flex-basis`, in a **wrapping** row): the size the child counts when lines break; with a `fill`
  main size it then grows by its `flex` share of its line. `"width": {"fill": 300}, "basis": 280` is CSS
  `flex: 1 1 280px`: three across at 1000 px, two at 700, one at 390.

A child hidden by a binding or a media rule takes no room (CSS `display: none`). A `spacer` takes the free space
only in a row or column that has some (a fill or fixed main size).

<a id="base-padding-margin-constraints-a-capped-width"></a>
### Padding, margin, constraints, a capped width

- `padding` is space inside the node's box, `margin` outside it: a number (all sides) or **four** numbers
  `[left, top, right, bottom]` (two numbers are not read).
- `constraints`: `{"minWidth", "maxWidth", "minHeight", "maxHeight"}`. `aspectRatio`: width / height.
- **A full-width band with capped, centered content** (CSS `max-width: 1200px; margin: 0 auto`): the band fills
  the width and holds the background; its one child fills with `"constraints": {"maxWidth": 1200}`, centered by the
  band's `crossAxisAlignment` (`center`, the default). [The capped band, with an example](#layout-a-capped-band).
- A negative margin does not overlap a neighbour: to overlap, move what the node paints with `"motion":
  {"translateY": -36}` (layout unchanged), or use a stack. [Overlap and bleed](#layout-overlap-and-bleed).

<a id="base-stacks"></a>
### Stacks

A `stack` places each child by its `layout.x` and `layout.y`: `16` or `{"start": 16}` from the left/top,
`{"end": 16}` from the right/bottom, `{"start": 16, "end": 16}` stretched between, `{"align": 0}` aligned (-1 start,
0 center, 1 end). Later children paint on top. `x`/`y` mean nothing under a row or column, `flex`/`align` nothing
under a stack (`layout_field_ignored`).

```json
{
  "schema": 3,
  "roots": ["board"],
  "nodes": {
    "board": {"type": "canvas", "slots": {"body": "stage"}, "layout": {"width": 400, "height": 300}},
    "stage": {
      "type": "stack",
      "children": ["photo", "badge", "caption"],
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 400}, "height": {"fill": 300}},
      "decoration": {"fills": [{"color": "#FFE5E7EB"}]}
    },
    "photo": {
      "type": "box",
      "layout": {"width": 200, "height": 120, "x": {"align": 0}, "y": {"align": 0}},
      "decoration": {
        "fills": [
          {
            "type": "linear",
            "stops": [{"position": 0, "color": "#FF6366F1"}, {"position": 1, "color": "#FFEC4899"}]
          }
        ],
        "radius": 16
      }
    },
    "badge": {
      "type": "box",
      "layout": {"width": 48, "height": 48, "x": {"end": 16}, "y": {"start": 16}},
      "decoration": {"fills": [{"color": "#FFF59E0B"}], "shape": "circle"}
    },
    "caption": {
      "type": "text",
      "layout": {"width": {"hug": 100}, "height": {"hug": 20}, "x": {"start": 16, "end": 16}, "y": {"end": 16}},
      "props": {
        "text": "Pinned 16 px from the left, right and bottom",
        "textAlign": "center",
        "style": {"fontSize": 14, "color": "#FF374151"}
      }
    }
  }
}
```

<a id="base-decoration"></a>
## Decoration

`decoration` paints the node's box:

- `fills`: paints, bottom to top. `{"color": "#FF2563EB"}` is solid; a gradient is `{"type": "linear", "stops":
  [{"position": 0, "color": ...}, {"position": 1, "color": ...}]}` (`"begin"`/`"end"` alignments; also `radial`,
  `sweep`); an image is `{"type": "image", "image": {"url": "...", "fit": "cover"}}` (give the box the image's size
  or an `aspectRatio`).
- `strokes` with `strokeWidth` (default 1): the border. `radius`: a number or `[topLeft, topRight, bottomRight,
  bottomLeft]`. `shape: "circle"`.
- `effects`: `{"type": "dropShadow", "color": "#1F000000", "offset": [0, 4], "blurRadius": 12}`; an effect needs
  its `type`.
- `clip: "antiAlias"` clips the children to the rounded box.

Colours are `"#AARRGGBB"` (alpha first: `#FF` opaque, `#80` half), `"#RRGGBB"` or a theme colour's name; `"#FFF"`,
`rgb()` and CSS names are not read. Patterns in pixels, grain, foreground scrims, icons, paths and custom drawing:
[decoration](#page-decoration).

```json
{
  "schema": 3,
  "roots": ["deco"],
  "nodes": {
    "deco": {
      "type": "canvas",
      "slots": {"body": "row"},
      "layout": {"width": 520, "height": 200},
      "decoration": {"fills": [{"color": "#FFF9FAFB"}]}
    },
    "row": {
      "type": "row",
      "children": ["card", "gradient", "outlined"],
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 520}, "height": {"fill": 200}, "padding": 24},
      "props": {"spacing": 24, "mainAxisAlignment": "center"}
    },
    "card": {
      "type": "box",
      "layout": {"width": 140, "height": 120},
      "decoration": {
        "fills": [{"color": "#FFFFFFFF"}],
        "radius": 12,
        "effects": [{"type": "dropShadow", "color": "#33000000", "offset": [0, 4], "blurRadius": 16}]
      }
    },
    "gradient": {
      "type": "box",
      "layout": {"width": 140, "height": 120},
      "decoration": {
        "fills": [
          {
            "type": "radial",
            "stops": [{"position": 0, "color": "#FFFDE68A"}, {"position": 1, "color": "#FFF97316"}]
          }
        ],
        "radius": [24, 4, 24, 4]
      }
    },
    "outlined": {
      "type": "box",
      "layout": {"width": 140, "height": 120},
      "decoration": {"strokes": [{"color": "#FF2563EB"}], "strokeWidth": 2, "dashPattern": [6, 4], "radius": 12}
    }
  }
}
```

<a id="base-text"></a>
## Text

A `text` node has `props.text` and `props.style`: a theme style's name (`"style": "body"`) or a TextStyle
(`fontSize`, `fontWeight` 100–900, `fontFamily`, `color`, `height` as a multiple of the size, `letterSpacing`,
`decoration`, `fontStyle`), plus `textAlign`, `maxLines` and `overflow` (`ellipsis`).

- **No `color`: the text is painted white.** Always set it (in the style or the named style).
- No `fontSize`: 12. No `fontWeight`: 400. No `fontFamily`: the platform's default (Roboto). No `height`: the
  nearest `defaultTextStyle`'s, else the font's own line height ([text](#theme-text)).
- Size: one line `{"hug": n}` × `{"hug": n}`; a paragraph `{"fill": n}` wide (it wraps) × `{"hug": n}` high.
- `text` may hold expressions: `"Hello, ${user.name}"`; `"$${price}"` shows `$47`.
- Symbols the font has no glyph for (✦, ✓, →) draw as empty boxes (`missing_glyph`): use an `icon` node.

Runs (parts in another style), superscripts, links in text: [text](#theme-text).

<a id="base-the-base-node-types"></a>
## The base node types

The props that matter most; each type's page lists all of them.

| type | takes | props (the base ones; all of them on its page) |
|---|---|---|
| [`canvas`](#node-canvas) | slots body, appBar, floatingActionButton, bottomNavigationBar |  |
| [`column`](#node-column) | children | `mainAxisAlignment` start|end|center|spaceBetween|spaceAround|spaceEvenly, `crossAxisAlignment` start|end|center|stretch|baseline, `spacing` number, `scrollable` bool |
| [`row`](#node-row) | children | `mainAxisAlignment` start|end|center|spaceBetween|spaceAround|spaceEvenly, `crossAxisAlignment` start|end|center|stretch|baseline, `spacing` number, `wrap` bool, `runSpacing` number |
| [`flex`](#node-flex) | children | `direction` horizontal|vertical, `mainAxisAlignment` start|end|center|spaceBetween|spaceAround|spaceEvenly, `crossAxisAlignment` start|end|center|stretch|baseline, `spacing` number, `wrap` bool |
| [`stack`](#node-stack) | children |  |
| [`box`](#node-box) | none |  |
| [`text`](#node-text) | none; no decoration | `text` text, `style` TextStyle {from, fontFamily, fontWeight, fontStyle, fontSize, color, foreground, letterSpacing}, `textAlign` left|right|center|justify|start|end, `maxLines` int, `overflow` clip|fade|ellipsis|visible |
| [`icon`](#node-icon) | none; no decoration | `icon` icon name, `color` "#AARRGGBB", `size` number |
| [`spacer`](#node-spacer) | none; no decoration |  |
| [`divider`](#node-divider) | none; no decoration | `thickness` number, `color` "#AARRGGBB" |
| [`filledButton`](#node-filledButton) | none; no decoration | `label` text, `icon` icon name, `style` ButtonStyle {backgroundColor, foregroundColor, shadowColor, elevation, textStyle, side, shape, iconSize}, `enabled` bool |
| [`elevatedButton`](#node-elevatedButton) | none; no decoration | `label` text, `icon` icon name, `style` ButtonStyle {backgroundColor, foregroundColor, shadowColor, elevation, textStyle, side, shape, iconSize} |
| [`outlinedButton`](#node-outlinedButton) | none; no decoration | `label` text, `icon` icon name, `style` ButtonStyle {backgroundColor, foregroundColor, shadowColor, elevation, textStyle, side, shape, iconSize} |
| [`textButton`](#node-textButton) | none; no decoration | `label` text, `icon` icon name, `style` ButtonStyle {backgroundColor, foregroundColor, shadowColor, elevation, textStyle, side, shape, iconSize} |
| [`iconButton`](#node-iconButton) | none; no decoration | `icon` icon name, `style` ButtonStyle {backgroundColor, foregroundColor, shadowColor, elevation, textStyle, side, shape, iconSize} |
| [`textField`](#node-textField) | none; no decoration | `initialValue` text, `decoration` InputDecoration {icon, labelText, labelStyle, floatingLabelStyle, helperText, helperStyle, helperMaxLines, hintText}, `keyboardType` text|multiline|number|phone|datetime|emailAddress|url|visiblePassword|..., `obscureText` bool, `maxLines` int |
| [`checkbox`](#node-checkbox) | none; no decoration | `value` bool, `activeColor` "#AARRGGBB" |
| [`switch`](#node-switch) | none; no decoration | `value` bool, `activeTrackColor` "#AARRGGBB" |
| [`radio`](#node-radio) | none; no decoration | `value` text, `groupValue` text, `activeColor` "#AARRGGBB" |
| [`slider`](#node-slider) | none; no decoration | `value` number, `min` number, `max` number, `divisions` int, `activeTrackColor` "#AARRGGBB" |
| [`dropdown`](#node-dropdown) | none | `items` [text], `value` Object, `hint` text |
| [`segmentedButton`](#node-segmentedButton) | none; no decoration | `segments` [ButtonSegment {value, label, icon, tooltip, enabled}], `selected` [text] |
| [`listView`](#node-listView) | children; slots loading, error, end, sectionHeader, reorderPlaceholder; no decoration | `scrollDirection` horizontal|vertical, `spacing` number, `scrollable` bool |
| [`gridView`](#node-gridView) | children; slots loading, error, end, reorderPlaceholder; no decoration | `crossAxisCount` int, `minCrossAxisExtent` number, `mainAxisSpacing` number, `crossAxisSpacing` number, `shrinkWrapRows` bool |

- **Buttons**: the text is `label` (not `text`); colours, corners and the label's style are in `style` (a
  [ButtonStyle](#type-ButtonStyle): `backgroundColor`, `foregroundColor`, `textStyle`, `shape`), not in
  `decoration`. Give a button a fixed width or a fill: a hugging button is only as wide as its label. For full
  control, use a `row` with a fill, padding, a text child and a `click` reaction.
- **Inputs** (`textField`, `checkbox`, `switch`, `radio`, `slider`, `dropdown`, `segmentedButton`) report a new
  value through their `changed` trigger as `${result}`: store it with `setVariable`. **Two-way**: bind the value
  prop to the variable (`"bind": {"props.initialValue": "${query}"}` for a text field, `"props.value"` for the
  others). A text field's label, hint, border and fill are in `props.decoration` (an
  [InputDecoration](#type-InputDecoration)). Styling every control, validation: [forms](#page-forms).
- **Lists**: a `listView` or `gridView` repeats its **first child** once per item of its `data` binding:
  `"bind": {"data": "${plans}"}`; inside, `${item.name}` and `${index}`. An item fills the list across (its
  cross-axis size is `fill`). In a page that scrolls, give the list
  `"scrollable": false` (a gridView: `"physics": "never"`). A grid of as many equal columns as fit:
  `minCrossAxisExtent` (CSS `repeat(auto-fit, minmax(280px, 1fr))`); equal-height cards: `"shrinkWrapRows": true`.
  Nested lists, tables, pagination: [lists](#page-lists).
- **Icons**: `props.icon` is a Material icon name (`"arrow_forward"`, `"check_circle"`; `_outlined`, `_rounded`
  suffixes), with `color` and `size`.
- **Images**: an image fill on a `box` (see Decoration). **Divider**: `divider` with `thickness` and `color`, or a
  `box` 1 high with a fill.

<a id="base-variables-bindings-and-expressions"></a>
## Variables, bindings and expressions

**Variables** hold state. Declare them in the document's `variables` under a canvas id (that screen) or
`"page_variables"` (every canvas of the document):

```json
"variables": {"page_variables": [
  {"name": "annual", "type": "boolean", "value": false},
  {"name": "plans", "type": "list", "value": [{"name": "Team", "monthly": 39}]},
  {"name": "price", "type": "number", "formula": "annual ? plans[0].monthly * 0.8 : plans[0].monthly"},
  {"name": "usd", "type": "text", "parameters": ["n"], "formula": "'$' + round(n)"}
]}
```

Types: `integer`, `text`, `decimal`, `boolean`, `color`, `list`, `map`, `image`, `choice`. A variable with a `formula` is **computed**: read-only, it follows what it reads. With
`parameters` it is a **function** any formula calls (`${= usd(price * 12)}`). Write a rule once, not in every
binding.

**Expressions**: `${name}` or `${path}` reads a value (`${user.name}`, `${items[0].price}`, `${item.title}`);
`${= formula}` computes one (`${= count * price}`, `${= annual ? 'Yearly' : 'Monthly'}`, a list
`${= popular ? [0, 0, 0, 0] : [0, 28, 0, 0]}`). A text that is exactly one expression keeps the value's type. `${false}` reads a variable called `false`: a literal is `${= false}`.
Every formula function, grouped (text, numbers, money, lists, dates): [formula functions](#state-formula-functions).

**Bindings** put an expression on a field: `"bind": {path: expression}`, updated whenever what it reads changes.

```json
"bind": {"props.text": "${= 'Total: ' + money(count * price, '$')}", "visible": "${= count > 0}",
         "decoration.fills[0].color": "${= selected ? '#FFDBEAFE' : '#FFFFFFFF'}"}
```

Paths: `visible`, `opacity`, `layout.<field>`, `decoration.<field>` (`fills[0].color`), `props.<prop>` and
`props.<prop>.<field>`, `data`, `selected`, `disabled`, behavior keys. Other fields are literal: `"opacity":
"${x}"` is an error; bind it. What each path expects: [binding paths](#state-binding-paths).

<a id="base-reactions"></a>
## Reactions

A node's `actions` is a list of **reactions**: a trigger and the actions it runs, in order:

```json
"actions": [{"trigger": {"type": "click"},
             "actions": [{"type": "setVariable", "variable": "count", "op": "add", "value": "1"},
                         {"type": "navigate", "to": "thanks"}]}]
```

- Triggers: `click`, `hover`, `changed` (an input's value), `submitted`, `load` (on a canvas), `valueChanged`,
  `timer`... (all of them: [triggers](#interaction-triggers)).
- `setVariable` (`op`: `set` (default), `toggle`, `add`, `subtract`, `insert`, `removeAt`...; `value` is an
  expression), `navigate` (`to`: a canvas id; `"mode": "pop"` goes back), `openModal` / `closeModal`, `showToast`,
  `if` (`"condition"`: a predicate, `{"left": "${count}", "op": "greaterThan", "right": "5"}` or `{"left":
  "${= valid}", "op": "isTrue"}`; `then` and `else`: action lists), `scrollTo`, `componentEvent` (a component's event, or at run time the event
  to the host app). Action types here: `navigate`, `openModal`, `closeModal`, `retryFailed`, `openLink`, `setValue`, `setVariant`, `setVariable`, `callFunction`, `if`, `forEach`, `showToast`, `confirm`, `delay`, `copyToClipboard`, `setThemeMode`, `editText`, `focus`, `controlTrack`, `controlDismissible`, `controlTransform`, `scrollTo`, `animate`, `haptic`, `runScript`, `paginate`, `componentEvent`, `callApi`, `setStorage`, `cloudDocuments`, `loadCloudData`, `reloadCloudData`, `cloudFiles`, `cloudData`, `cloudBatch`, `submitForm`, `auth`, `paywall`, `print`, `preloadImages`, `speak`, `playSound`, `captureScreenshot`, `downloadFile`, `emitEvent`.
- Keys are exact; validation names the one meant: `{"type": "scrollTo", "node": "faq"}`, `{"type":
  "copyToClipboard", "text": "${address}"}`, `{"type": "downloadFile", "fileName": "trip.txt", "text": "${brief}"}`;
  a list appends with `"op": "add"` (`insert` takes an `index`).
- In a chain `${result}` is the trigger's event (a text field's text) until an action gives another value.
- A tap on a control inside a tappable row runs the control's reaction only: to toggle from the whole row, give the
  control `"ignorePointer": true` and bind its value.

Hover and pressed styles (`states`), drag, gestures: [interaction](#page-interaction). Screens and modals:
[navigation](#page-navigation).

<a id="base-screen-sizes-media-rules"></a>
## Screen sizes: media rules

1. Prefer layout that fits any width: wrapping rows with `basis`, a `gridView` with `minCrossAxisExtent`, a capped
   band.
2. A node's `media` is a list of CSS media queries over the node: `[{"minWidth": 600, "patch": {"props": {"style":
   {"fontSize": 40}}}}]`. `minWidth`/`maxWidth` are px (inclusive) or a breakpoint name (`"tablet"`).
3. The `patch` is shaped like the node (`props`, `layout`, `decoration`, `visible`, `motion`, `bind`) and merged
   over it; later rules win (the cascade). Write for phones, add `minWidth` rules (mobile first).
4. A row that becomes a column: a `flex` with a rule patching `"direction": "vertical"`; another order: patch
   `layout.order`; hidden: `"visible": false`.
5. A field both patched and bound shows the binding (`media_overridden`): put the binding in the rule's patch.

Breakpoints, sticky headers, scrolling, a canvas per breakpoint: [responsive layout](#page-layout).

<a id="base-rules-that-are-easy-to-get-wrong"></a>
## Rules that are easy to get wrong

1. Every node needs `layout.width` and `layout.height`; without them it is 0 × 0.
2. Every text needs a colour; without one it is white.
3. Padding and margin are a number or four numbers, never two.
4. Colours are `#AARRGGBB`, `#RRGGBB` or a theme colour's name; define the theme first and name its colours and
   styles.
5. Columns center their children across by default: `"crossAxisAlignment": "start"` for left-aligned content.
6. A screen taller than the window needs a scrolling body column (`"scrollable": true`, `fill` both ways).
7. Values in `props`, `layout` and `decoration` are literal; expressions go in `bind` (except `props.text`).
8. `x`/`y` only work under a `stack`; `flex`/`align` only under a `row`, `column` or `flex`.
9. Ids are map keys; a child is listed in exactly one parent; canvases are only in `roots`.
10. `fill` takes all the room it is given: cap it with `constraints.maxWidth`. Under a parent that hugs that
    axis, a fill is its design number (`fill_fallback`).
11. A backslash in a formula is written twice in JSON: `"${= matches(code, '^\\d{4}$')}"`.
12. Buttons: `label`, colours in `style`. Inputs: `changed` + `setVariable`, two-way by binding the value prop.
13. Repeated content comes from data: one template in a `listView` / `gridView`, not copies.

<a id="base-checking-your-work"></a>
## Checking your work

Decoding is lenient: a misspelled key or a value of the wrong shape is silently dropped. Never trust a document
that has not been checked. Run the render command from the SDK repository:

```sh
tool/render/render.sh site/ --out shots/ --sizes 390x844,834x1112,1440x900 --full-page
```

It validates every document strictly, renders each screen at each size (`shots/<screen>@<w>x<h>.png`,
`shots/diagnostics.json`) and prints one line per problem: a code, the JSON pointer
(`/nodes/hero-title/props/style/fontSize`) and what to do. It exits 1 on errors. Steps before the capture:
`--tap <id>` (`<id>#<n>` for the n-th list item), `--hover`, `--focus`, `--type <id>=<text>`,
`--set <variable>=<json>`, `--scroll <id>=<px>`, `--drag <id>=<dx>,<dy>`, `--navigate <canvas>?<param>=<value>`,
`--label <name>`. Look at the
screenshots: validation cannot tell you a page is ugly. Every option and diagnostic code: [render](#page-render).

<a id="base-sites-and-components-as-files"></a>
## Sites and components as files

A page longer than a screen or two is easier to write, fix and reuse as parts, each a file: a **component** is a
document with one root and a `widget` declaration of its parameters, slots and events, read inside as
`${props.price}`; a page **calls** it with one node of that type (`{"type": "PlanCard", "props": {"price": 47}}`),
as Flutter builds `PlanCard(price: 47)`. A component never reads its page's variables: pass what it needs as
parameters, and shared state as a `variable` parameter. A folder with `site.json` (pages, components, theme,
project variables) is a site. **Write `site.json` first, with every page listed in `pages`**, before the pages
that link to them: a link to a page not listed yet is an `unknown_screen` error.

- **List template**: one shape repeated from data in one parent.
- **Component**: the same structure in two or more places with different values (a card, a chip).
- **Section**: a top-level band of a page (header, hero, pricing, FAQ, footer), in its own file when it is more
  than about 15 nodes.

Parameter kinds, slots, events, the manifest, rendering one part: [components](#page-components). A whole site
(manifest, shared header and footer, route parameters, storage, a modal): [a complete site](#components-a-complete-multi-page-site).

<a id="index-the-pages"></a>
## The pages

| Page | What it covers | Words |
|---|---|---|
| [STARTER.md](#page-base) | The base (give it up front): the document, layout, decoration, text, the base node types, state, reactions, the rules. | 4603 |
| [layout.md](#page-layout) | Sizes, rows and columns, stacks, scrolling and screen sizes beyond the base: every layout field, which sizing modes each parent allows, media rules and breakpoints, and the web layouts agents ask for (a capped band, cards that wrap, a row that becomes a column, overlap and bleed, a sticky header or column). | 7037 |
| [theme.md](#page-theme) | A site's palette and type scale, declared once and named everywhere; dark mode and a type scale that changes with the screen size; and the `text` node in depth (runs, links, superscripts, fonts, text direction). | 2632 |
| [decoration.md](#page-decoration) | What a node's box paints beyond the base: gradients, pixel patterns and grain, borders on some sides, shadows and blurs, scrims over children, images, icons, SVG-like paths and custom drawing. | 4097 |
| [forms.md](#page-forms) | Buttons, text fields, checkboxes, switches, radios, sliders, dropdowns, segmented buttons, date and time pickers, chips and signatures: every control's props, **how to style each one (in one place, below)**, two-way binding to a variable, validation and error states, focus and the keyboard. | 10159 |
| [lists.md](#page-lists) | Anything repeated from data: lists and grids from one item template, nested lists (`item`, `index`, `parent`), equal-height card grids, tables, carousels (`pageView`), list tiles, pagination, pull to refresh, swipe actions and reordering. | 6101 |
| [navigation.md](#page-navigation) | Several screens and moving between them, a page's URL path, passing values to a screen, dialogs, bottom sheets and popovers, confirmations and toasts, app bars, navigation bars, tabs and disclosure (accordions). | 4166 |
| [state.md](#page-state) | Variables and where they live, computed and function variables, expressions and every binding path with the value it expects, conditions, the formula functions (grouped: text, numbers, money, lists, objects, dates, colours), the actions that change state, and sandboxed scripts. | 6398 |
| [interaction.md](#page-interaction) | What a node does when it is tapped, hovered, pressed, dragged or swiped: reactions and every trigger, hover and pressed styles (`states`), ink ripples, tooltips, letting taps through, drag and drop, values set by dragging (`track`), swipe to dismiss, pan, pinch and rotate, keys, the clipboard and haptics. | 5162 |
| [animation.md](#page-animation) | Anything that moves: a change that animates (implicit transitions), keyframe animations and presets, moving, scaling and turning a node without changing layout (`motion`), shared-element flights (`hero`), reveal on scroll, shimmer, typewriter text, particles, flip cards and tilt, and the timer and frame triggers for clocks and games. | 4610 |
| [components.md](#page-components) | Splitting a page into parts, each a file: a component used in several places with different values (a card, a chip, a row), a section used once (a header, a hero, an FAQ), their parameters (every kind, `variable` included), slots and events, the site manifest, and when to use a component, a list template or a section. | 3706 |
| [charts.md](#page-charts) | Showing numbers as pictures: progress bars and rings, activity spinners, badges, gauges, bar, line and series charts, scatter plots and barcodes. | 6561 |
| [data.md](#page-data) | The `data` feature library: calling HTTP APIs, reading and writing the project's cloud documents and files, storing values on the device, and submitting forms. | 2308 |
| [auth.md](#page-auth) | The `auth` feature library: signing app users in, up and out, and managing their account, with `${auth}` to show who is signed in. | 468 |
| [commerce.md](#page-commerce) | The `commerce` feature library: a paywall screen's interactions (buy, restore, select a product, close, open a legal link). | 439 |
| [media.md](#page-media) | The `media` feature library: video players, embedded videos, an audio player, web views, reading text aloud, playing sounds, printing, capturing a screenshot, downloading a file and preloading images. | 1998 |
| [engage.md](#page-engage) | The `engage` feature library: firing app events that the project's automations listen for (a popup after a lesson, a review prompt after the third order), and the `${usage}` counters they read. | 311 |
| [publish.md](#page-publish) | What happens to documents after they are written: a published app's model (its layouts, components, theme and identity), page paths and titles, components published by reference, managed component releases and hosted plugins. | 672 |
| [edit-ops.md](#page-edit-ops) | Building and changing a document with edit operations: what a model sends in a `ui_apply` tool call, what an app's `UiSession` applies while the model streams, the retry protocol for rejected ops, the tools' schemas and the trust profiles that limit what a model may use. | 3297 |
| [render.md](#page-render) | Checking a document or a site before trusting it: strict validation, screenshots at each size, the states after taps, typing and scrolling, and a diagnostic for every problem with a code, a JSON pointer and what to do. | 2881 |
| [values.md](#page-values) | Looking up how one value is written: a value type (a colour, an alignment, insets), a model no feature page shows (its fields) or an enum (its names). | 13107 |

<a id="page-layout"></a>
# Responsive layout

<a id="layout-when-to-use"></a>
## When to use

Sizes, rows and columns, stacks, scrolling and screen sizes beyond the base: every layout field, which sizing
modes each parent allows, media rules and breakpoints, and the web layouts agents ask for (a capped band, cards that
wrap, a row that becomes a column, overlap and bleed, a sticky header or column).

<a id="layout-minimal-example"></a>
## Minimal example

The text hugs its content, the red box fills the column's width, and in the row the green and blue boxes share the
free space 1 : 2 (`flex`) beside a fixed grey box.

```json
{
  "schema": 3,
  "roots": ["sizing"],
  "nodes": {
    "sizing": {
      "type": "canvas",
      "slots": {"body": "col"},
      "layout": {"width": 400, "height": 400},
      "decoration": {"fills": [{"color": "#FFFFFFFF"}]}
    },
    "col": {
      "type": "column",
      "children": ["hugText", "fillBox", "bar"],
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 400}, "height": {"fill": 400}, "padding": 10},
      "props": {"crossAxisAlignment": "start", "spacing": 8}
    },
    "hugText": {
      "type": "text",
      "layout": {"width": {"hug": 80}, "height": {"hug": 20}},
      "props": {"text": "As wide as its text", "style": {"fontSize": 16, "color": "#FF000000"}}
    },
    "fillBox": {
      "type": "box",
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 380}, "height": 24},
      "decoration": {"fills": [{"color": "#FFEF4444"}]}
    },
    "bar": {
      "type": "row",
      "children": ["one", "two", "fixed"],
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 380}, "height": 40},
      "props": {"spacing": 10}
    },
    "one": {
      "type": "box",
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 100}, "height": {"fill": 40}},
      "decoration": {"fills": [{"color": "#FF22C55E"}]}
    },
    "two": {
      "type": "box",
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 200}, "height": {"fill": 40}, "flex": 2},
      "decoration": {"fills": [{"color": "#FF3B82F6"}]}
    },
    "fixed": {"type": "box", "layout": {"width": 60, "height": 20}, "decoration": {"fills": [{"color": "#FF9CA3AF"}]}}
  }
}
```

<a id="layout-reference"></a>
## Reference

<a id="layout-layout-fields"></a>
### Layout fields

A node's `"layout"`: its size, spacing and placement in its parent. `width` and `height` are an
[AxisSize](#type-AxisSize): a number (fixed) or `{"fill" | "hug" | "flexible" | "fixed": number}`; `x` and `y` an
[AxisPosition](#type-AxisPosition).

<a id="layout-width"></a>
<a id="layout-height"></a>
<a id="layout-constraints"></a>
<a id="layout-margin"></a>
<a id="layout-padding"></a>
<a id="layout-aspectRatio"></a>
<a id="layout-flex"></a>
<a id="layout-squeezable"></a>
<a id="layout-x"></a>
<a id="layout-y"></a>
<a id="layout-align"></a>
<a id="layout-order"></a>
<a id="layout-basis"></a>
| Key | Type | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `width` | [AxisSize](#type-AxisSize) | `0` |  | The node's width: a number (fixed), `{"hug": n}` (its content), `{"fill": n}` (the room its parent gives) or `{"flexible": n}` (up to n). n is the design size. Without one the node is 0 wide. |
| `height` | [AxisSize](#type-AxisSize) | `0` |  | The node's height: a number (fixed), `{"hug": n}`, `{"fill": n}` or `{"flexible": n}`, as `width`. Without one the node is 0 high. |
| `constraints` | [BoxConstraints](#type-BoxConstraints) | `{}` |  |  |
| `margin` | [EdgeInsets](#type-EdgeInsets) | `0` |  | Space around the node, outside its box. |
| `padding` | [EdgeInsets](#type-EdgeInsets) | `0` |  | Space between the node's box and its content (Flutter's `Padding`). A text's padding sits around its lines, as `Padding(child: Text(...))`: a hugging text grows by it (schema 3; schema 2 ignored it on a text, and the migration drops it there). |
| `aspectRatio` | double | unset | ≥ 0 | Width / height the node keeps when its parent resizes it. |
| `flex` | int | `1` | ≥ 0 | Under a row/column: share of the free space (`Expanded.flex`). |
| `squeezable` | bool | `false` |  | Under a row/column: a hugging child that may shrink (`Flexible`). |
| `x` | [AxisPosition](#type-AxisPosition) | `{"start":0}` |  | Under a freeform parent (`Positioned` / `Align`). |
| `y` | [AxisPosition](#type-AxisPosition) | `{"start":0}` |  | Position under a freeform parent. |
| `align` | [Alignment](#type-Alignment) | unset |  | Under a row/column: alignment in its slot (`Align`). |
| `order` | int | `0` |  | CSS `order`: under a row, column or flex, children are laid out and painted by ascending order (equal orders as listed). Patch it per screen size (`media`) to reorder at a width. |
| `basis` | double | unset | ≥ 0 | CSS `flex-basis`, under a wrapping row, column or flex: the main size the child counts when lines are broken; a child that fills the main axis (`{"fill": n}`) then grows by its `flex` share of the room left on its line (`flex: 1 1 280px`). Cards with `basis: 280` sit three across at 900 px, two at 600, one at 390, with no breakpoints. |

Read by decoding but not declared as fields: `widthFactor`, `heightFactor`. A share (0–1 and up) of the room its parent gives it on that axis (`FractionallySizedBox`): a progress bar's fill is `widthFactor: 0.6` of its track. Null: sized by `width` / `height`. Bindable (`layout.widthFactor`).

<a id="layout-which-sizing-modes-each-parent-allows"></a>
### Which sizing modes each parent allows

From the parents' own rules; "fill (with `basis`)": a child of a wrapping row may fill its line's share when it sets
`layout.basis`.

| Parent | Width may be | Height may be |
|---|---|---|
| `row` | fixed, fill, flexible, hug | fixed, fill, hug |
| `column` | fixed, fill, hug | fixed, fill, flexible, hug |
| `row` with {"wrap":true} | fixed, fill (with `basis`), hug | fixed, fill, hug |
| `column` with {"scrollable":true} | fixed, fill, hug | fixed, hug |
| `row` with {"scrollable":true,"scrollDirection":"horizontal"} | fixed, hug | fixed, fill, hug |
| `stack` | fixed, fill, hug | fixed, fill, hug |
| `canvas` | fixed, fill, hug | fixed, fill, hug |
| `listView` | fill | fixed, hug |
| `listView` with {"itemExtent":80} | fill | fill |
| `gridView` | fill | fill |
| `pageView` | fill | fill |

Why a mode is not allowed, as the declarations say it:

- Flexible only applies in a row or column, along its main axis.
- A wrapping row lays its children out in runs: they keep their own size along it, unless they set layout.basis (CSS flex-basis): then a filling child grows to share its line.
- The column scrolls: its content has no end to fill to.
- The row scrolls: its content has no end to fill to.
- Items in a list always fill across it.
- A list is unbounded along its scroll axis: items cannot fill it. Set an item extent.
- The list gives every item its item extent: they fill it.
- Grid cells size their children: they fill them.
- Pages size their children: they fill them.

<a id="layout-media-rules"></a>
### Media rules

A node's `media` (and the theme's) is a list of rules, each a CSS media query over the node:

| Key | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `minWidth` | CSS `min-width`: a width in px (inclusive), or a breakpoint name (from its min width). |
| `maxWidth` | CSS `max-width`: a width in px (inclusive), or a breakpoint name (up to the next breakpoint's min width, exclusive). |
| `orientation` | CSS `orientation`. |
| `patch` | A JSON merge patch over the node (maps merge, `null` removes, anything else replaces): `props`, `layout`, `decoration`, `visible`, `opacity`, `motion` (a transform that moves what is painted, not the layout: `Transform.translate`), and `bind`: bindings that hold at these sizes only (`"bind": {"visible": "${= !open}"}`), or `null` to drop one of the node's own here, so its patched value shows. |

<a id="layout-breakpoints"></a>
### Breakpoints

The project's breakpoints name size classes by minimum width. Unless a document's `breakpoints` key says otherwise
they are:

| id | name | minWidth | design width × height |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mobile` | Mobile | 0 | 390 × 844 |
| `tablet` | Tablet | 600 | 834 × 1112 |
| `desktop` | Desktop | 1024 | 1440 × 900 |

A breakpoint's fields:

| Key | Type | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | String | `""` |  | Stable id. |
| `name` | String | `""` |  | Name. |
| `minWidth` | double | `0` | ≥ 0 | From this width (inclusive). |
| `width` | double | `0` | ≥ 0 | Design width of its canvases. |
| `height` | double | `0` | ≥ 0 | Design height of its canvases. |

<a id="node-canvas"></a>
### `canvas`

Flutter `Scaffold`.

A screen (`Scaffold`): its `body` slot is the page content.

- Children: slots: `body`, `appBar`, `floatingActionButton`, `bottomNavigationBar`.
- Decoration: box decoration (fills, strokes, radius, shadows, clip).

| Key | Type | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `scaleMode` | [ScaleMode](#enum-ScaleMode) | `"responsive"` | `responsive`, `autoScale` | How the canvas fits a screen of another size than its design size: lays out at the screen's size, or scales the design. |
| `blockBack` | bool | `false` |  | While true, going back (the system or browser back button, a back gesture) keeps the user on this screen and runs its `backPressed` reactions instead. Usually bound (`${= dirty}`). A navigate pop from the screen's own actions is never blocked. |
| `breakpoint` | String | `""` |  | The breakpoint it is the design for. |
| `screen` | String | `""` |  | The screen it is a breakpoint of. |
| `breakpointMinWidth` | double | unset | ≥ 0 | Its own switch point. |
| `overlay` | bool | `false` |  | Shown above every screen, outside navigation. |
| `backdrop` | bool | `false` |  | Drawn beneath every screen, outside navigation. |

<a id="node-row"></a>
### `row`

Flutter `Row`.

`Row` and `Column`: the same props, different main axis.

- Children: `children`.
- Decoration: box decoration (fills, strokes, radius, shadows, clip).
- Reads from each child's layout: [`flex`](#layout-flex), [`squeezable`](#layout-squeezable), [`align`](#layout-align), [`order`](#layout-order), [`basis`](#layout-basis).

| Key | Type | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `mainAxisAlignment` | [MainAxisAlignment](#enum-MainAxisAlignment) | `"start"` | `start`, `end`, `center`, `spaceBetween`, `spaceAround`, `spaceEvenly` | How the children are placed along the main axis (horizontal in a row, vertical in a column), Flutter's `MainAxisAlignment`: `start`, `end`, `center`, `spaceBetween`, `spaceAround`, `spaceEvenly`. |
| `crossAxisAlignment` | [CrossAxisAlignment](#enum-CrossAxisAlignment) | `"center"` | `start`, `end`, `center`, `stretch`, `baseline` | How the children are placed across the main axis, Flutter's `CrossAxisAlignment`. The default `center` centers them: write `start` for left-aligned (or top-aligned) content, `stretch` to make every child as wide (or tall) as the node. |
| `spacing` | double | `0` | ≥ 0 | Space between children along the main axis. |
| `wrap` | bool | `false` |  | Wraps children onto new runs when they overflow (`Wrap`). |
| `runSpacing` | double | `0` | ≥ 0 | Space between runs when wrapping. |
| `squeezeChildren` | bool | `true` |  | Children that overflow a bounded main axis shrink to fit it (by how far each can, never below its content), as the editor lays them out; false lays them out at their own sizes and lets them run past the end, as Flutter's `Row`/`Column` does. |
| `scrollable` | bool | `false` |  | Scrolls its content. |
| `scrollDirection` | [Axis](#enum-Axis) | `"vertical"` | `horizontal`, `vertical` | The axis it scrolls along. |
| `reverse` | bool | `false` |  |  |
| `physics` | [ScrollPhysicsType](#enum-ScrollPhysicsType) | `"platform"` | `platform`, `bouncing`, `clamping`, `never`, `rangeMaintaining` |  |
| `alwaysScroll` | bool | `false` |  | Scrolls even when the content fits. |
| `clipBehavior` | [Clip](#enum-Clip) | `"hardEdge"` | `none`, `hardEdge`, `antiAlias`, `antiAliasWithSaveLayer` |  |
| `fillViewport` | bool | `false` |  | A scrolling row/column's content is at least as long as its viewport (`ConstrainedBox(minHeight: viewport)` in a `SingleChildScrollView`): alignment and expanded children use the whole viewport while it fits. Already so when it centers or spreads its children or has a flex child; this makes it so in every case. |

<a id="node-box"></a>
### `box`

Flutter `Container`.

A leaf box: Flutter `Container` with a decoration and no child.

- Children: none.
- Decoration: box decoration (fills, strokes, radius, shadows, clip).

_No props._

<a id="node-spacer"></a>
### `spacer`

Flutter `Spacer`.

Flexible empty space in a row/column (`Spacer`), or a fixed gap. With no size along its parent's main axis it is Flutter's `Spacer()`: it takes the free space by its `layout.flex`; a fixed size there makes it a gap.

- Children: none.
- Decoration: none: only blur effects in `decoration.effects` apply.

_No props._

Flutter `Divider`.

`Divider` and `VerticalDivider`: a line across the node's box.

- Children: none.
- Decoration: none: only blur effects in `decoration.effects` apply.

| Key | Type | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `thickness` | double | `1` | ≥ 0 | The line's thickness in pixels, drawn centered in the node's height (Flutter's `Divider.thickness`). |
| `color` | [Color](#type-Color) | unset |  | Null is the theme's outline variant. |
| `indent` | double | `0` | ≥ 0 |  |
| `endIndent` | double | `0` | ≥ 0 |  |

| Key | Type | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `thickness` | double | `1` | ≥ 0 | The line's thickness in pixels, drawn centered in the node's height (Flutter's `Divider.thickness`). |
| `color` | [Color](#type-Color) | unset |  | Null is the theme's outline variant. |
