<a id="node-variance"></a>
### `variance`

Variant switcher.

Shows one of several variants of its content (by id, or by breakpoint).

- Children: `children`.
- Decoration: box decoration (fills, strokes, radius, shadows, clip).
- Reads from each child's layout: [`x`](#layout-x), [`y`](#layout-y).

| Key | Type | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `variants` | List<Object> | `[]` |  | `[{"id", "name", "children": `ids`, "breakpoint"?, "overrides"?}]`; `breakpoint` is a project `Breakpoint.id` (DESIGN.md §5.3): a variance with any is responsive. |
| `current` | String | `""` |  |  |
| `minWidths` | Map<String, double> | `{}` |  | Its own switch points, by breakpoint. |

<a id="behavior-sticky"></a>
### `sticky` (behavior)

A node key (beside `layout` and `props`). Type: [Sticky](#type-Sticky). Default: unset.

Pinned in its scrolling view while its parent is in view.

<a id="type-Sticky"></a>
#### Sticky

Pins the node inside the scrolling row or column it scrolls in, as CSS `position: sticky`: once its leading edge reaches `offset` from the view's leading edge it stays there, drawn above the content scrolling under it, until the end of its parent (the section it heads) pushes it on. `${sticky.stuck}` says whether it is pinned now (the node's own bindings and the nodes inside it read it). The design canvas, which doesn't scroll, draws it in place. JSON `true` or `{"offset": 8}`.

| Key | Type | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `offset` | double | `0` |  | Distance from the view's leading edge where it pins (px). |

<a id="behavior-floating"></a>
### `floating` (behavior)

A node key (beside `layout` and `props`). Type: bool. Default: `false`.

Drawn above everything else at runtime (a menu under a field), still taking its place in the layout. The design canvas draws it in place.

<a id="behavior-measure"></a>
### `measure` (behavior)

A node key (beside `layout` and `props`). Type: [Measure](#type-Measure). Default: unset.

Its laid-out box, written to a variable.

<a id="type-Measure"></a>
#### Measure

Writes where the node is laid out, `{x, y, width, height, centerX, centerY}` in pixels, to a variable as layout changes: in the coordinates of the ancestor node `relativeTo` (empty: the screen), under `key` when the variable is a map. Other nodes then follow it: a marker travelling to the chip of the reader's layer on a timeline whose chips are laid out by data. The design canvas measures too.

| Key | Type | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `variable` | String | `""` |  | The variable its box is written to. |
| `key` | String | `""` |  | The key it's written under, for a map variable. |
| `relativeTo` | String | `""` |  | An ancestor node whose box it's measured in; empty: the screen. |

<a id="layout-triggers"></a>
### Triggers

Written as `"trigger": {"type": "<trigger>", ...}` in a reaction ([trigger fields](#interaction-trigger-fields)).

| Trigger | When it fires |
|---|---|
| <a id="trigger-scroll"></a>`scroll` | The node (a scrolling row, column or canvas) scrolled (`${result.offset}`, `${result.max}`, `${result.fraction}`), or came near its end (load the next page). |
| <a id="trigger-scrollEnd"></a>`scrollEnd` |  |
| <a id="trigger-enterViewport"></a>`enterViewport` | At least `Trigger.visibleFraction` of the node became visible (and stayed so for `Trigger.visibleMs`), or it fell below that after being visible. With `Trigger.onceKey` (`${item.id}`), an impression: once per item per app session. |
| <a id="trigger-exitViewport"></a>`exitViewport` |  |

<a id="action-scrollTo"></a>
### `scrollTo` (action): Scroll to

Scrolls node `node` into view: `alignment` 0 puts it at the start of the view, 1 at the end; `offset` moves it further. `axis` limits it to the scroll views along one axis (a map in a sideways window centers a point without scrolling the page under it); null scrolls every one around it.

| Key | Type | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `node` | String | `""` |  | The node to reveal: its id, or an expression giving one (`"cmp-col-${cmpCol + 1}"`). A node that is not on screen when the action runs is reported as an action error, not skipped silently. |
| `item` | String | `""` |  | For a repeated node: the key (or index) of the list item whose copy to reveal. |
| `durationMs` | int | `400` |  |  |
| `curve` | String | `"easeInOut"` |  | A Curves name. |
| `alignment` | double | `0` |  | 0: at the start of the view, 1: at the end. |
| `offset` | double | `0` |  |  |
| `axis` | [ScrollAxis](#enum-ScrollAxis) | unset | `horizontal`, `vertical` | Only the scroll views along this axis; null: every one. |

<a id="layout-patterns"></a>
## Patterns

<a id="layout-responsive-design"></a>
### Responsive design

Responsive layout works as on the web: flexbox and grid lay content out so it fits any width, and media queries
change what must change at a width. Use these, in this order:

1. **Intrinsic layout, no breakpoints.** A wrapping row whose children set `layout.basis` and fill the main axis:
   lines break by the basis and the children on each line grow to share it. For repeated data, a `gridView` with
   `minCrossAxisExtent` makes as many equal columns as fit. A share of the parent (CSS `width: 60%`) is
   `layout.widthFactor: 0.6`.
2. **Media rules** for what must change at a width: direction, order, visibility, type size, padding. A rule's
   `patch` is merged over the node (objects merge, `null` removes a key), except that a value with several forms is
   **replaced**, as CSS replaces a declaration: `{"width": {"hug": 200}}` over `{"fill": 292}` is `{"hug": 200}`.
   Rules apply in order, a later one winning (the cascade). Validation checks every patched value and judges sizes
   at each range of widths with the rules that hold there.
3. **Bindings on `${screen}`** for values computed from the size: `"bind": {"layout.width": "${= min(screen.width -
   32, 760)}"}`. `${screen}` has `width`, `height`, `breakpoint`, `is.<name>`, `atLeast.<name>`
   (`${= screen.atLeast.tablet ? 3 : 1}`). Nothing can check such a formula's result: prefer media rules.
4. **A canvas per breakpoint**, only for screens that are genuinely different designs (below).

Precedence: the node's own values, then its media rules, then an active interaction state's patch, then its
bindings, then conditions.

This page uses the four web patterns: a header whose links collapse to a menu icon below desktop, a 3 → 2 → 1 card
grid from data (`minCrossAxisExtent`), a text-and-photo section that stacks with the photo first on phones (`basis`
in a wrapping row, the photo's `order` patched), and a title whose size steps up with the width, inside a content
column capped at 1200:

```json
{
  "schema": 3,
  "roots": ["home"],
  "nodes": {
    "home": {
      "type": "canvas",
      "slots": {"body": "page"},
      "layout": {"width": 1440, "height": 900},
      "decoration": {"fills": [{"color": "#FFFFFFFF"}]}
    },
    "page": {
      "type": "column",
      "children": ["header", "content"],
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 1440}, "height": {"fill": 900}},
      "props": {"scrollable": true}
    },
    "header": {
      "type": "row",
      "children": ["logo", "nav", "menu"],
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 1440}, "height": 64, "padding": [16, 0, 16, 0]},
      "props": {"mainAxisAlignment": "spaceBetween"},
      "decoration": {"fills": [{"color": "#FF111827"}]},
      "media": [{"minWidth": "desktop", "patch": {"layout": {"padding": [32, 0, 32, 0]}}}]
    },
    "logo": {
      "type": "text",
      "layout": {"width": {"hug": 80}, "height": {"hug": 24}},
      "props": {"text": "Relay", "style": {"fontSize": 20, "fontWeight": 700, "color": "#FFFFFFFF"}}
    },
    "nav": {
      "type": "row",
      "children": ["nav-1", "nav-2", "nav-3"],
      "visible": false,
      "layout": {"width": {"hug": 300}, "height": {"hug": 20}},
      "props": {"spacing": 32},
      "media": [{"minWidth": "desktop", "patch": {"visible": true}}]
    },
    "nav-1": {
      "type": "text",
      "layout": {"width": {"hug": 60}, "height": {"hug": 20}},
      "props": {"text": "Product", "style": {"fontSize": 15, "color": "#FFD1D5DB"}}
    },
    "nav-2": {
      "type": "text",
      "layout": {"width": {"hug": 60}, "height": {"hug": 20}},
      "props": {"text": "Pricing", "style": {"fontSize": 15, "color": "#FFFFFFFF"}}
    },
    "nav-3": {
      "type": "text",
      "layout": {"width": {"hug": 60}, "height": {"hug": 20}},
      "props": {"text": "Docs", "style": {"fontSize": 15, "color": "#FFD1D5DB"}}
    },
    "menu": {
      "type": "icon",
      "layout": {"width": 28, "height": 28},
      "props": {"icon": "menu", "color": "#FFFFFFFF"},
      "media": [{"minWidth": "desktop", "patch": {"visible": false}}]
    },
    "content": {
      "type": "column",
      "children": ["title", "plans", "split"],
      "layout": {
        "width": {"fill": 1440},
        "height": {"hug": 800},
        "padding": [16, 24, 16, 24],
        "constraints": {"maxWidth": 1200}
      },
      "props": {"crossAxisAlignment": "stretch", "spacing": 24},
      "media": [{"minWidth": "tablet", "patch": {"layout": {"padding": [32, 48, 32, 48]}, "props": {"spacing": 32}}}]
    },
    "title": {
      "type": "text",
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 1136}, "height": {"hug": 64}},
      "props": {
        "text": "Plans that scale with your team",
        "style": {"fontSize": 32, "fontWeight": 700, "height": 1.1, "color": "#FF111827"}
      },
      "media": [
        {"minWidth": "tablet", "patch": {"props": {"style": {"fontSize": 40}}}},
        {"minWidth": "desktop", "patch": {"props": {"style": {"fontSize": 56}}}}
      ]
    },
    "plans": {
      "type": "gridView",
      "children": ["plan"],
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 1136}, "height": {"hug": 200}},
      "props": {
        "physics": "never",
        "minCrossAxisExtent": 280,
        "shrinkWrapRows": true,
        "crossAxisSpacing": 24,
        "mainAxisSpacing": 24
      },
      "bind": {"data": "${plans}"}
    },
    "plan": {
      "type": "column",
      "children": ["plan-name", "plan-price"],
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 360}, "height": {"fill": 160}, "padding": 24},
      "props": {"crossAxisAlignment": "start", "spacing": 8},
      "decoration": {"fills": [{"color": "#FFF3F4F6"}], "radius": 12}
    },
    "plan-name": {
      "type": "text",
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 312}, "height": {"hug": 24}},
      "props": {"text": "${item.name}", "style": {"fontSize": 18, "fontWeight": 600, "color": "#FF111827"}}
    },
    "plan-price": {
      "type": "text",
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 312}, "height": {"hug": 40}},
      "props": {"text": "${item.price}", "style": {"fontSize": 32, "fontWeight": 700, "color": "#FF2563EB"}}
    },
    "split": {
      "type": "row",
      "children": ["split-text", "split-photo"],
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 1136}, "height": {"hug": 240}},
      "props": {"wrap": true, "spacing": 48, "runSpacing": 16, "crossAxisAlignment": "center"}
    },
    "split-text": {
      "type": "text",
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 544}, "height": {"hug": 60}, "basis": 320},
      "props": {
        "text": "Every plan includes on-call schedules, escalation policies and status pages.",
        "style": {"fontSize": 18, "height": 1.5, "color": "#FF374151"}
      }
    },
    "split-photo": {
      "type": "box",
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 544}, "height": 240, "basis": 320},
      "decoration": {"fills": [{"color": "#FF93C5FD"}], "radius": 12},
      "media": [{"maxWidth": "mobile", "patch": {"layout": {"order": -1}}}]
    }
  },
  "variables": {
    "home": [
      {
        "name": "plans",
        "type": "list",
        "value": [
          {"name": "Starter", "price": "$0"},
          {"name": "Team", "price": "$29"},
          {"name": "Enterprise", "price": "Talk to us"}
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

The same page in CSS:

```css
#nav { display: none } @media (min-width: 1024px) { #nav { display: flex } #menu { display: none } }
#plans { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(280px, 1fr)); gap: 24px }
#split { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 16px 48px } #split > * { flex: 1 1 320px }
@media (max-width: 599px) { #split-photo { order: -1 } }
#title { font-size: 32px } @media (min-width: 600px) { #title { font-size: 40px } }
@media (min-width: 1024px) { #title { font-size: 56px } }
#content { max-width: 1200px; margin: 0 auto }
```

<a id="layout-a-capped-band"></a>
### A capped band

A full-width band with capped, centered content (CSS `max-width: 1200px; margin: 0 auto` inside a coloured band):
the band fills the width and holds the background; its one child fills with `constraints.maxWidth`, centered by the
band's `crossAxisAlignment` (`center`, the default). Under `crossAxisAlignment: stretch` a cap holds too, as CSS
`max-width` does: the child sits at the start, or where its `layout.align` puts it (`[0, 0]` centers it). Below, a
comparison table built from one row template and one cell template:

```json
{
  "schema": 3,
  "roots": ["home"],
  "nodes": {
    "home": {
      "type": "canvas",
      "slots": {"body": "page"},
      "layout": {"width": 1440, "height": 900},
      "decoration": {"fills": [{"color": "#FFFFFFFF"}]}
    },
    "page": {
      "type": "column",
      "children": ["band"],
      "props": {"scrollable": true},
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 1440}, "height": {"fill": 900}}
    },
    "band": {
      "type": "column",
      "children": ["rail"],
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 1440}, "height": {"hug": 200}, "padding": [24, 48, 24, 48]},
      "decoration": {"fills": [{"color": "#FF1F2937"}]}
    },
    "rail": {
      "type": "column",
      "children": ["title", "table"],
      "props": {"spacing": 16, "crossAxisAlignment": "stretch"},
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 1200}, "height": {"hug": 160}, "constraints": {"maxWidth": 1200}}
    },
    "title": {
      "type": "text",
      "props": {"text": "Compare plans", "style": {"fontSize": 28, "fontWeight": 700, "color": "#FFFFFFFF"}},
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 1200}, "height": {"hug": 34}}
    },
    "table": {
      "type": "listView",
      "children": ["tr"],
      "bind": {"data": "${rows}"},
      "props": {"physics": "never"},
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 1200}, "height": {"hug": 120}}
    },
    "tr": {
      "type": "row",
      "children": ["label", "cells"],
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 1200}, "height": {"hug": 44}},
      "decoration": {"strokes": [{"color": "#FF374151"}], "strokeSides": "bottom"}
    },
    "label": {
      "type": "text",
      "bind": {"props.text": "${item.label}"},
      "props": {"text": "", "style": {"fontSize": 14, "color": "#FFD1D5DB"}},
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 180}, "height": {"hug": 20}, "flex": 2}
    },
    "cells": {
      "type": "gridView",
      "children": ["cell"],
      "bind": {"data": "${item.values}", "props.crossAxisCount": "${= length(item.values)}"},
      "props": {"physics": "never", "crossAxisCount": 3, "shrinkWrapRows": true},
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 600}, "height": {"hug": 44}, "flex": 3}
    },
    "cell": {
      "type": "text",
      "bind": {"props.text": "${item}"},
      "props": {"text": "", "textAlign": "center", "style": {"fontSize": 14, "color": "#FFFFFFFF"}},
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 200}, "height": {"hug": 20}, "margin": [0, 12, 0, 12]}
    }
  },
  "variables": {
    "home": [
      {
        "name": "rows",
        "type": "list",
        "value": [
          {"label": "Seats", "values": ["5", "25", "Unlimited"]},
          {"label": "SSO", "values": ["–", "Yes", "Yes"]},
          {"label": "Support", "values": ["Email", "Chat", "24/7"]}
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

Across a row or column, a child's width comes out as:

| Parent's `crossAxisAlignment` | child `fill` | child `hug` | child fixed `n` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `start`, `center`, `end` | the parent's inner width, at most its `maxWidth`, placed by the alignment | its content, at most `maxWidth` | `n`, clamped by its constraints |
| `stretch` | the parent's inner width, at most its `maxWidth` (then at the start, or at its `align`) | its content, at the start | the parent's inner width, at most its `maxWidth` |

<a id="layout-cards-that-wrap"></a>
### Cards that wrap

Three plan cards three across at desktop, two at tablet, one on phones, with no breakpoint: a wrapping `row`
(`"wrap": true`, `spacing`, `runSpacing`) whose cards are `"width": {"fill": 300}, "basis": 280`. With
`crossAxisAlignment: stretch` the cards of each line are as tall as its tallest (CSS `align-items: stretch`: equal
heights). From data, use a `gridView` with `minCrossAxisExtent` and `shrinkWrapRows` instead
([equal-height cards](#lists-equal-height-cards)).

<a id="layout-a-row-that-becomes-a-column"></a>
### A row that becomes a column

A `flex` node with `"direction": "horizontal"` and a rule patching `"direction": "vertical"` below a width. Its
children stay the same nodes, keeping their state. Another order at a width: each child's `layout.order`, patched in
the child's own rule (`{"maxWidth": "mobile", "patch": {"layout": {"order": -1}}}` puts it first). Hidden at a
width: `{"maxWidth": "tablet", "patch": {"visible": false}}`; a hidden node takes no room.

```json
"split": {"type": "flex", "children": ["copy", "photo"], "props": {"direction": "horizontal", "spacing": 32},
          "layout": {"width": {"fill": 1200}, "height": {"hug": 400}},
          "media": [{"maxWidth": 599, "patch": {"props": {"direction": "vertical"}}}]}
```

<a id="layout-a-media-rule-and-a-binding-on-one-field"></a>
### A media rule and a binding on one field

Shown on phones only, and there only while a panel is closed: a patch may set `bind`, bindings that hold at its
sizes only. Write the node for the other sizes and bind in the rule: `"visible": false, "media": [{"maxWidth": 599,
"patch": {"bind": {"visible": "${= !filtersOpen}"}}}]`. The breakpoint stays in the media rule. To show a patched
value where the node binds the field at other sizes, drop the binding in the rule: `"patch": {"visible": true,
"bind": {"visible": null}}`.

<a id="layout-overlap-and-bleed"></a>
### Overlap and bleed

**Overlapping a neighbour** (CSS `margin-top: -36px`, `transform: translateY(-36px)`): Flutter's answer is
`Transform.translate`: `"motion": {"translateY": -36}` moves what the node paints, not its layout, so the next node
does not move up; a node later in its parent paints over the ones before it. A media rule may patch it. A card
overlapping the bottom of a hero band: the card after the hero with `translateY: -36`, and 36 px of `margin` below it
if the next section should keep its distance. The render command reports a node translated past its parent's box as
`layout_overflow` (a warning naming the parent): expected for this pattern, and the only diagnostic it leaves. To
overlap by an amount that depends on the content, or with no warning, use a `stack`.

**Bleeding past the gutter** (a table or photo running to the screen's edge while the text keeps its padding): put
the padding on the children, not on the band, or let the one child that bleeds translate out of it (`"motion":
{"translateX": 18}` with a width 18 larger), and keep the band's `"decoration": {"clip": "none"}` (the default). A
photo frame that overhangs its photo: a `stack` with a fixed or fill size holding the frame at a negative `x`/`y`.

<a id="layout-scrolling"></a>
### Scrolling

A screen scrolls only if something in it scrolls. Make the canvas's body column scroll: `"props": {"scrollable":
true}` with `{"fill": n}` width and height. Without it, content past the bottom of the screen is cut off
(`offscreen`). Inside a scrolling column, a child cannot `fill` the scrolling axis. Rows scroll sideways with
`"scrollable": true, "scrollDirection": "horizontal"`. `scrollTo` reveals a node (`"node"`: an id, or an expression
giving one; `"axis": "horizontal"` moves only sideways scroll views): `{"type": "scrollTo", "node": "faq",
"durationMs": 400}` from a sub-navigation link (the key is `node`, not `target`).

```json
{
  "schema": 3,
  "roots": ["article"],
  "nodes": {
    "article": {
      "type": "canvas",
      "slots": {"body": "scroller"},
      "layout": {"width": 390, "height": 844},
      "decoration": {"fills": [{"color": "#FFFFFFFF"}]}
    },
    "scroller": {
      "type": "column",
      "children": ["header", "p1", "p2", "p3"],
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 390}, "height": {"fill": 844}, "padding": 24},
      "props": {"scrollable": true, "spacing": 16, "crossAxisAlignment": "start"}
    },
    "header": {
      "type": "box",
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 342}, "height": 400},
      "decoration": {"fills": [{"color": "#FFDBEAFE"}], "radius": 16}
    },
    "p1": {
      "type": "box",
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 342}, "height": 300},
      "decoration": {"fills": [{"color": "#FFFDE68A"}], "radius": 16}
    },
    "p2": {
      "type": "box",
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 342}, "height": 300},
      "decoration": {"fills": [{"color": "#FFBBF7D0"}], "radius": 16}
    },
    "p3": {
      "type": "text",
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 342}, "height": {"hug": 20}},
      "props": {"text": "The end of the page.", "style": {"fontSize": 16, "color": "#FF111827"}}
    }
  }
}
```

<a id="layout-scroll-progress"></a>
### Scroll progress

A reading-progress bar on an article or a long page: a `scroll` reaction on the page's scrolling column writes
`${result.fraction}` (0 at the top, 1 at the end) to a variable, and a `progressBar` (or a box's width factor) is
bound to it. Put the bar outside the scrolling column (a `stack` over it, or the canvas's `appBar`) so it stays in
view:

```json
"actions": [{"trigger": {"type": "scroll"},
             "actions": [{"type": "setVariable", "variable": "readFraction", "value": "${result.fraction}"}]}]
```

and on the bar `"bind": {"props.value": "${readFraction}"}`. Per section instead of per page: `viewProgress` on the
section ([view progress](#animation-reveal-on-scroll-view-progress-sticky-effects)).

<a id="layout-a-sticky-header-or-column"></a>
### A sticky header or column

A header that stays at the top while the page scrolls under it: the scrolling column's first child with
`"sticky": {"offset": 0}` (CSS `position: sticky`); it is drawn above the content and is pushed on by the end of
its parent. `${sticky.stuck}` is true while it is pinned (bind a shadow or a smaller height to it). A `--full-page`
capture draws it once, in its place in the page, as a reader sees it at the top; to see it pinned, capture a window
scrolled down (`--scroll <scrolling column id>=1200` without `--full-page`). A header fixed to the window instead (it never
scrolls, and a full-page capture draws it once, at the top): a `stack` filling the canvas body, the scrolling column
first (with a top spacer of the header's height) and the header after it at `"y": 0`.

A comparison table with a **sticky first column** on phones is two parts side by side: a fixed column of row
labels, and a row of plan columns that scrolls sideways (made to scroll only on phones by a media rule on its
`scrollable`); give each table row the same height in both. From data: [a table from one template](#lists-a-table-from-one-template).

<a id="layout-a-canvas-per-breakpoint"></a>
### A canvas per breakpoint

Canvases with the same `props.screen` are one screen; each sets `props.breakpoint` to the breakpoint it is for. At
a given width the screen shows the canvas whose breakpoint's `minWidth` is the highest at or below the width, else
its narrowest. Each canvas has its own nodes; share state with `page_variables`. A `variance` node does the same for
one part of a screen. Older documents use this:

```json
{
  "schema": 3,
  "roots": ["home-mobile", "home-desktop"],
  "nodes": {
    "home-mobile": {
      "type": "canvas",
      "name": "Home",
      "props": {"screen": "home", "breakpoint": "mobile"},
      "slots": {"body": "m-page"},
      "layout": {"width": 390, "height": 844},
      "decoration": {"fills": [{"color": "#FFFFFFFF"}]}
    },
    "m-page": {
      "type": "column",
      "children": ["m-title", "m-size"],
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 390}, "height": {"fill": 844}, "padding": 24},
      "props": {"crossAxisAlignment": "start", "spacing": 8}
    },
    "m-title": {
      "type": "text",
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 342}, "height": {"hug": 32}},
      "props": {"text": "Stacked for phones", "style": {"fontSize": 24, "fontWeight": 700, "color": "#FF111827"}}
    },
    "m-size": {
      "type": "text",
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 342}, "height": {"hug": 20}},
      "props": {
        "text": "${screen.breakpoint}: ${screen.width} px wide",
        "style": {"fontSize": 14, "color": "#FF6B7280"}
      }
    },
    "home-desktop": {
      "type": "canvas",
      "name": "Home",
      "props": {"screen": "home", "breakpoint": "desktop"},
      "slots": {"body": "d-page"},
      "layout": {"width": 1440, "height": 900},
      "decoration": {"fills": [{"color": "#FFF3F4F6"}]}
    },
    "d-page": {
      "type": "row",
      "children": ["d-title", "d-size"],
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 1440}, "height": {"hug": 120}, "padding": 48},
      "props": {"mainAxisAlignment": "spaceBetween"}
    },
    "d-title": {
      "type": "text",
      "layout": {"width": {"hug": 400}, "height": {"hug": 48}},
      "props": {"text": "Side by side on desktops", "style": {"fontSize": 40, "fontWeight": 700, "color": "#FF111827"}}
    },
    "d-size": {
      "type": "text",
      "layout": {"width": {"hug": 200}, "height": {"hug": 20}},
      "props": {
        "text": "${screen.breakpoint}: ${screen.width} px wide",
        "style": {"fontSize": 14, "color": "#FF6B7280"}
      }
    }
  }
}
```

```json
{
  "schema": 3,
  "roots": ["page"],
  "nodes": {
    "page": {
      "type": "canvas",
      "slots": {"body": "col"},
      "layout": {"width": 390, "height": 844},
      "decoration": {"fills": [{"color": "#FFFFFFFF"}]}
    },
    "col": {
      "type": "column",
      "children": ["features"],
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 390}, "height": {"fill": 844}, "padding": 24}
    },
    "features": {
      "type": "variance",
      "children": ["stacked", "sideBySide"],
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 342}, "height": {"hug": 200}},
      "props": {
        "variants": [
          {"id": "narrow", "name": "Narrow", "breakpoint": "mobile", "children": ["stacked"]},
          {"id": "wide", "name": "Wide", "breakpoint": "tablet", "children": ["sideBySide"]}
        ]
      }
    },
    "stacked": {
      "type": "column",
      "children": ["a1", "a2"],
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 342}, "height": {"hug": 100}},
      "props": {"spacing": 12}
    },
    "a1": {
      "type": "box",
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 342}, "height": 80},
      "decoration": {"fills": [{"color": "#FF6366F1"}], "radius": 8}
    },
    "a2": {
      "type": "box",
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 342}, "height": 80},
      "decoration": {"fills": [{"color": "#FF22C55E"}], "radius": 8}
    },
    "sideBySide": {
      "type": "row",
      "children": ["b1", "b2"],
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 342}, "height": {"hug": 80}},
      "props": {"spacing": 12}
    },
    "b1": {
      "type": "box",
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 100}, "height": 80},
      "decoration": {"fills": [{"color": "#FF6366F1"}], "radius": 8}
    },
    "b2": {
      "type": "box",
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 100}, "height": 80},
      "decoration": {"fills": [{"color": "#FF22C55E"}], "radius": 8}
    }
  }
```

<a id="layout-pitfalls"></a>
## Pitfalls

- `fill` takes all the room it is given: cap it with `constraints.maxWidth`. Where its parent gives no room on that
  axis (it hugs it, or scrolls), a fill is its design number (`fill_fallback`, naming the parent).
- `x`/`y` mean nothing under a row or column, `flex`/`align` nothing under a stack (`layout_field_ignored`).
- A stack that hugs its children grows to hold them, so there a negative offset is 0 (`layout_clamped`). A
  negative margin does not overlap a neighbour (`layout_clamped`): translate with `motion`.
- A media patch replaces a size of another mode: `{"hug": 200}` over `{"fill": 292}` is `{"hug": 200}`. A field
  both patched and bound shows the binding (`media_overridden`): bind in the rule instead.
- `squeezeChildren` (default true) shrinks children that do not fit toward their content, as CSS flex items
  shrink; false is Flutter's overflow (`layout_overflow`).
- A `spacer` takes the free space only in a row or column with room to spare.
- Without `basis`, children of a wrapping row keep their own size.
- `${screen.width}` prints a decimal (`390.0`); `${= screen.width}` prints `390`.

<a id="page-theme"></a>
# Theme and text

<a id="theme-when-to-use"></a>
## When to use

A site's palette and type scale, declared once and named everywhere; dark mode and a type scale that changes with
the screen size; and the `text` node in depth (runs, links, superscripts, fonts, text direction).

<a id="theme-minimal-example"></a>
## Minimal example

A site manifest (`site.json`) with a theme: a palette and a type scale. The page next to it names them.

```json
{
  "schema": 3,
  "pages": ["home.json"],
  "theme": {
    "colors": {"ink": "#FF1B1B1B", "ember": "#FFE4572E", "paper": "#FFF6F1E9"},
    "textStyles": {
      "body": {"fontSize": 16, "height": 1.5, "color": "ink"},
      "title": {"from": "body", "fontSize": 32, "fontWeight": 700, "height": 1.2},
      "eyebrow": {"from": "body", "fontSize": 12, "letterSpacing": 2, "color": "ember"}
    },
    "media": [{"minWidth": 1024, "patch": {"textStyles": {"title": {"fontSize": 56}}}}]
  }
}
```

A page using it (a fragment of `home.json`'s `nodes`):

```json
"eyebrow": {"type": "text", "props": {"text": "OUR MENU", "style": "eyebrow"}, "layout": {"width": {"fill": 342}, "height": {"hug": 18}}},
"title":   {"type": "text", "props": {"text": "Fire, smoke and season", "style": "title"}, "layout": {"width": {"fill": 342}, "height": {"hug": 40}}},
"note":    {"type": "text", "props": {"text": "Cooked over oak.", "style": {"from": "body", "color": "ember"}}, "layout": {"width": {"fill": 342}, "height": {"hug": 24}}},
"rule":    {"type": "box", "layout": {"width": 120, "height": 4}, "decoration": {"fills": [{"color": "ember"}]}}
```

<a id="theme-reference"></a>
## Reference

<a id="theme-theme-keys"></a>
### Theme keys

The theme (`site.json`'s `theme`, or the app's theme at run time):

| Key | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `colors` | Every named color of the project by key (`themeKey` of its name: "Brand Blue" is `brandBlue`), read as `${theme.colors.brandBlue}`. |
| `textStyles` | Every named text style by key, read as `${theme.text.title.fontSize}` and named by a text's style (`"style": "title"`, or `{"from": "title", ...}` to change some of its fields). A style may itself start `from` another and name `colors`; `textStyle` gives it resolved. |
| `dark` | The colors for dark mode: the tokens and `colors` that differ from the light ones (its other fields are not used). |
| `media` | The theme by screen size, as CSS media queries over custom properties: each rule's `patch` is a theme's JSON (`{"textStyles": {"display": {"fontSize": 40}}, "colors": {...}}`) merged over this one while the screen meets its conditions (`atScreen`). A type scale that changes at a breakpoint is written once here, not on every text. |
| `primary` | Primary buttons and info toasts. |
| `onPrimary` | Text on `primary`. |
| `surface` | Dialog backgrounds. |
| `onSurface` | Text on `surface`. |
| `error` | Destructive buttons and error toasts. |
| `success` | Success toasts. |
| `warning` | Warning toasts. |
| `fontFamily` | Font family of body text and buttons. |
| `titleFontFamily` | Font family of titles. |
| `radius` | Corner radius of dialogs. |
| `buttonRadius` | Corner radius of buttons. |

<a id="node-text"></a>
### `text`

Flutter `Text.rich`.

`Text.rich`: a string with styled runs.

- Children: none.
- Decoration: none: only blur effects in `decoration.effects` apply.

| Key | Type | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `text` | String | `""` |  | The text shown. May hold expressions: `"Hello, ${user.name}"`. |
| `style` | [TextStyle](#type-TextStyle) | `{}` |  | Base style for the whole text. |
| `runs` | List<[TextRun](#type-TextRun)> | `[]` |  | Styled ranges over `text`, merged over `style`. |
| `textAlign` | [TextAlign](#enum-TextAlign) | `"start"` | `left`, `right`, `center`, `justify`, `start`, `end` | How lines are aligned inside the node's width (Flutter's `TextAlign`). |
| `textAlignVertical` | [TextAlignVertical](#enum-TextAlignVertical) | `"top"` | `top`, `center`, `bottom` | Where the lines sit when the node is taller than they are. |
| `maxLines` | int | unset |  | At most this many lines; the rest is cut as `overflow` says. Null: no limit. |
| `overflow` | [TextOverflow](#enum-TextOverflow) | `"clip"` | `clip`, `fade`, `ellipsis`, `visible` | What shows where the text is cut by `maxLines` or the node's size (Flutter's `TextOverflow`): `clip`, `fade`, `ellipsis`, `visible`. |
| `selectable` | bool | `false` |  | The user can select and copy the text (Flutter's `SelectableText`). |
| `scaleDown` | bool | `false` |  | Shrinks the whole text to fit its width, keeping its lines (`FittedBox(fit: BoxFit.scaleDown)`). |
| `countUp` | bool | `false` |  | A number in the text (after binding: "1,204", "\$12.50", "87%") counts up to each new value in a running app, from the value on screen; the characters around it, its decimals and its thousands separators stay. A design canvas (or TickerMode off) shows the final text. |
| `countUpDuration` | int | `500` | ≥ 0 | Milliseconds of one count. |
| `countUpCurve` | [AnimationCurve](#enum-AnimationCurve) | `"linear"` |  | The curve a number in the text counts up along when it changes. |
| `countUpOnShow` | bool | `true` |  | The first value counts up from 0 when the text first shows; off, it shows at rest and only later changes count. |

<a id="behavior-textDirection"></a>
### `textDirection` (behavior)

A node key (beside `layout` and `props`). Type: [TextDirection](#enum-TextDirection). Default: unset. Allowed: `ltr`, `rtl`.

Null inherits.

<a id="behavior-defaultTextStyle"></a>
### `defaultTextStyle` (behavior)

A node key (beside `layout` and `props`). Type: [TextStyle](#type-TextStyle). Default: unset.

The text style every text style of this node and its descendants is merged over (Flutter's DefaultTextStyle); the nearest one wins ({} gives Flutter's defaults back). Unset everywhere: Flutter's defaults, the font's own line height.

<a id="type-TextStyle"></a>
#### TextStyle

Flutter's `TextStyle`. Every field is optional: a span's style is merged over its text's base style, as in `Text.rich`.

| Key | Type | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `from` | String | unset |  | The name of one of the project's text styles (the site manifest's `theme.textStyles`) this style starts from, as `Theme.of(context).textTheme.titleLarge.merge(...)`: the fields written here change it. `"style": "title"` is short for `{"from": "title"}`. |
| `fontFamily` | String | unset |  | The font family (`"Inter"`); `fontWeight` picks its file. Without one: the platform's default (Roboto). |
| `fontWeight` | [FontWeight](#type-FontWeight) | unset |  | Flutter's `FontWeight`: 100–900, in hundreds. |
| `fontStyle` | [FontStyle](#enum-FontStyle) | unset | `normal`, `italic` | `normal` or `italic`. |
| `fontSize` | double | unset | ≥ 0 | The font size in logical pixels. Without one: 12. |
| `color` | [Color](#type-Color) | unset |  | Solid text color. |
| `foreground` | [Paint](#type-Paint) | unset |  | A gradient or image paint for the glyphs, used instead of `color`. |
| `letterSpacing` | double | unset |  | Logical pixels between letters. |
| `height` | double | unset | ≥ 0 | Line height as a multiple of the font size. Unset: the inherited defaultTextStyle's, else the font's own (Flutter's height: null, CSS line-height: normal). |
| `decoration` | [TextDecoration](#enum-TextDecoration) | unset | `none`, `underline`, `overline`, `lineThrough` | A line through the text: `underline`, `overline`, `lineThrough` or `none`. |
| `decorationColor` | [Color](#type-Color) | unset |  | The colour of the `decoration` line; without one, the text's colour. |
| `backgroundColor` | [Color](#type-Color) | unset |  | Painted behind the glyphs. |
| `decorationStyle` | [TextDecorationStyle](#enum-TextDecorationStyle) | unset | `solid`, `double`, `dotted`, `dashed`, `wavy` | The `decoration` line's style: `solid`, `double`, `dotted`, `dashed`, `wavy`. |
| `decorationThickness` | double | unset |  | The `decoration` line's thickness, as a multiple of the font's default. |
| `tabularFigures` | bool | unset |  | Fixed-width digits (`OpenTypeFeature.tabularFigures`). |
| `fontFeatures` | List<[FontFeature](#type-FontFeature)> | `[]` |  | OpenType feature settings (`"lnum"`, `"ss01"`, `"liga=0"`). |
| `leadingDistribution` | [TextLeadingDistribution](#enum-TextLeadingDistribution) | unset | `proportional`, `even` | Where a line's extra (or missing) height goes (`TextStyle .leadingDistribution`); null is Flutter's default, proportional. |
| `shadows` | List<[Effect](#type-Effect)> | `[]` |  | Text shadows (drop shadows only). |

<a id="action-setThemeMode"></a>
### `setThemeMode` (action): Set theme mode

Sets the site's theme mode (Flutter's ThemeMode: system, light or dark), as an app sets MaterialApp.themeMode: every screen redraws its named colors, text styles and controls in it; with persist (the default) the choice survives a reload. JSON: {"type": "setThemeMode", "mode": "${= theme.isDark ? 'light' : 'dark'}"}.

| Key | Type | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `mode` | String | `"system"` |  | system (the device's setting), light or dark (Flutter's ThemeMode); an expression: "${= theme.isDark ? 'light' : 'dark'}" toggles. |
| `persist` | bool | `true` |  | Keep the choice in the site's local storage: a reload (and every page) starts in it. |

<a id="type-TextRun"></a>
### TextRun

A styled range of a text's characters, `[start, end)`.

| Key | Type | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `start` | int | `0` |  |  |
| `end` | int | `0` |  |  |
| `style` | [TextStyle](#type-TextStyle) | `{}` |  |  |
| `link` | String | unset |  | A URL the run opens when tapped. |

<a id="theme-patterns"></a>
## Patterns

<a id="theme-named-colours-and-styles"></a>
### Named colours and styles

- **Colours**: `colors` maps a name to `"#AARRGGBB"` (or to another colour's name: `"accent": "ember"`). Wherever a
  colour is accepted, write its name. The roles `primary`, `onPrimary`, `surface`, `onSurface`, `error`, `success`,
  `warning` (keys of the theme) are names too.
- **Text styles**: `textStyles` maps a name to a TextStyle. A style may start `from` another and name colours. A
  text names its style in one field, `"style": "title"`; to change some fields of it, `"style": {"from": "title",
  "color": "ember"}` (`textTheme.titleLarge.merge(...)`: the fields written win). Runs, a button's `textStyle` and
  an input's styles take the same two forms.
- Changing a colour or style in the theme changes every node that names it, and only those.
- In a binding a name is not read: bind the value, `"${theme.colors.ember}"` or `"${theme.text.title}"`; inside
  a formula, `${= done ? theme.colors.sage : theme.colors.mist}`.

<a id="theme-what-controls-take-from-the-theme"></a>
### What controls take from the theme

A control's colours, fonts and shapes that its props leave unset come from the theme: `primary` fills filled buttons
(labelled in `onPrimary`) and draws checks, thumbs, focus rings and text-button labels where it reads on `surface`
(else `onSurface` does); `fontFamily` is every control label's font (`titleFontFamily` titles'); `buttonRadius`
shapes every kind of button and chip, `radius` dialogs, menus and pickers. Without a theme, controls are neutral:
ink on paper (near-black on white; near-white on near-black in dark mode) and the greys between, in no font of
their own. Nothing comes from Material's defaults (no purple, ripples or elevation) or from the host app's theme.

<a id="theme-spacing-and-radius-scales"></a>
### Spacing and radius scales

The theme has no spacing or radius tokens for nodes: its `radius` and `buttonRadius` shape controls only. Write
padding, gaps and corner radii as numbers, or keep a scale as a project variable (`{"name": "space", "type": "map",
"value": {"sm": 8, "md": 16, "lg": 32}}` in `site.json`) and bind it where it varies: `"bind": {"layout.padding":
"${space.md}", "props.spacing": "${space.sm}"}`.

<a id="theme-a-type-scale-that-changes-with-the-screen-size"></a>
### A type scale that changes with the screen size

The theme's `media` rules patch the theme as a node's rules patch a node: `{"minWidth": 1024, "patch":
{"textStyles": {"title": {"fontSize": 56}}}}` makes every text using `title` grow at desktop width, written once. A
node's own media rule may switch its style (`"patch": {"props": {"style": "caption"}}`, which replaces the style)
or change some fields (`{"style": {"fontSize": 20}}`, merged over the named style).

<a id="theme-dark-mode"></a>
### Dark mode

`"dark": {"colors": {"ink": "#FFEEEEEE"}}` gives the colours (and roles: `surface`, `primary`...) that differ in
dark mode; everything naming `ink` follows the mode: fills, strokes, named text styles (a style whose `color` is
`"ink"`), and the controls, which take the theme's roles. A style with a literal colour (`"#FF111111"`) does not
change: name the colour.

Which mode shows is the theme's `mode` (Flutter's `ThemeMode`, as `MaterialApp.themeMode`): `system` (the default:
the device's setting), `light` or `dark`. A site's own switch is one action:

```json
{"type": "setThemeMode", "mode": "${= theme.isDark ? 'light' : 'dark'}"}
```

`mode` is an expression giving `system`, `light` or `dark`. Every screen of the site redraws at once, the next page
opens in the same mode, and with `persist` (the default) the choice is kept in the site's local storage, so a
reload starts in it; `"persist": false` keeps it for this visit only. `${theme.mode}` reads the mode chosen and
`${theme.isDark}` (also `${screen.isDark}`) whether the screen is dark; bind a switch's value to
`${theme.isDark}` to show it. A theme without `dark` stays as designed in dark mode (its colours and controls light),
while `${theme.isDark}` still says dark (`${theme.hasDark}` is false), so a page may choose its own colours.

The render command captures either: `--theme light` or `--theme dark` (the PNG names end `-light`, `-dark`), and a
`--tap` on the switch afterwards captures the other.

<a id="theme-text"></a>
### Text

A `text` node has `props.text` and `props.style`. What a text looks like when the style leaves something out: no
`color`, white; no `fontSize`, 12; no `fontWeight`, 400; no `fontFamily`, the platform's default (Roboto on Android
and the web); no `height`, the nearest `defaultTextStyle`'s (a node key, Flutter's `DefaultTextStyle`, for its
whole subtree), else the font's own line height. Sizing: one line `{"hug": n}` × `{"hug": n}`; a paragraph `{"fill": n}` wide × `{"hug": n}` high. A
fixed height shorter than the lines clips them (`text_clipped`).

`runs` style parts of the text: `[{"start": 0, "end": 5, "style": {"fontWeight": 700}}]` (character offsets, end
exclusive, `\n` counting as one), merged over `style`; a run may carry a `"link"` URL. A literal `$` right before an
expression is text: `"$${price}"` shows `$47`. There is no escape for a literal `${`: compute it.

<a id="theme-superscripts-and-a-raised-currency-sign"></a>
### Superscripts and a raised currency sign

A raised or lowered character (a price's "$", a footnote mark): a run with `"fontFeatures": ["sups"]` (or `"subs"`)
when the font has those OpenType features; otherwise a smaller `fontSize` in a row of texts aligned
`crossAxisAlignment: start` (or `baseline`) for the exact shift.

<a id="theme-fonts"></a>
### Fonts

`style.fontFamily` names a family (`"Inter"`), with `fontWeight` and `fontStyle` choosing the file. A site declares
the families it ships in `site.json`, in the shape of a Flutter pubspec's `fonts:` section, the files beside it:

```json
{
  "schema": 3,
  "pages": ["home.json"],
  "fonts": [
    {"family": "Fraunces", "fonts": [
      {"asset": "fonts/fraunces-latin-400-normal.woff"},
      {"asset": "fonts/fraunces-latin-700-normal.woff", "weight": 700},
      {"asset": "fonts/fraunces-latin-400-italic.woff", "style": "italic"}
    ]}
  ],
  "theme": {"fontFamily": "Fraunces", "textStyles": {"body": {"fontFamily": "Fraunces", "fontSize": 17}}}
}
```

- `family` is the name text styles use, whatever the file calls itself; each file has a `weight` (100–900, default
  400) and a `style` (`normal` or `italic`).
- Files are `.ttf`, `.otf` or `.woff` (an npm `@fontsource/<family>` package's `files/` folder has a `.woff` beside
  each `.woff2`). WOFF2 is not read (`font_format`); a declared file that is not there is `font_missing`.
- The render command loads them with no flag, before the page shows; a published site loads them from its files.
- A family a text style names that no file provides is `font_fallback`, naming the nodes that use it: declare it,
  or pass `--fonts <dir>` (`--fonts system` for the system's fonts). A family nobody declared is fetched by name
  from Google Fonts in an app.

Characters the font has no glyph for draw as empty boxes (`missing_glyph`): use an `icon`.

<a id="theme-pitfalls"></a>
## Pitfalls

- A text without a colour is white (`text_no_color` when rendered): set it in the style or the named style.
- A name the theme does not have is `unknown_theme_name` (with the nearest name); a theme of the wrong shape is
  `invalid_theme`. Without a `site.json`, put the page in a folder with one: `{"schema": 3, "pages": ["home.json"],
  "theme": {...}}`.
- A theme colour's name is not read from a formula: bind `${theme.colors.ember}`.
- Run offsets count characters, `\n` as one.

<a id="theme-see-also"></a>
## See also

[Decoration](#page-decoration) (paints that name theme colours) · [forms](#page-forms) (input and button text
styles) · [responsive layout](#layout-media-rules) (media rules).

<a id="page-decoration"></a>
# Decoration, images, icons and drawing

<a id="decoration-when-to-use"></a>
## When to use

What a node's box paints beyond the base: gradients, pixel patterns and grain, borders on some sides, shadows and
blurs, scrims over children, images, icons, SVG-like paths and custom drawing.

<a id="decoration-minimal-example"></a>
## Minimal example

A card with a solid fill, a border, rounded corners and a shadow, and a gradient band:

```json
{
  "schema": 3,
  "roots": ["deco"],
  "nodes": {
    "deco": {
      "type": "canvas",
      "slots": {"body": "row"},
      "layout": {"width": 520, "height": 200},
      "decoration": {"fills": [{"color": "#FFF9FAFB"}]}
    },
    "row": {
      "type": "row",
      "children": ["card", "gradient", "outlined"],
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 520}, "height": {"fill": 200}, "padding": 24},
      "props": {"spacing": 24, "mainAxisAlignment": "center"}
    },
    "card": {
      "type": "box",
      "layout": {"width": 140, "height": 120},
      "decoration": {
        "fills": [{"color": "#FFFFFFFF"}],
        "radius": 12,
        "effects": [{"type": "dropShadow", "color": "#33000000", "offset": [0, 4], "blurRadius": 16}]
      }
    },
    "gradient": {
      "type": "box",
      "layout": {"width": 140, "height": 120},
      "decoration": {
        "fills": [
          {
            "type": "radial",
            "stops": [{"position": 0, "color": "#FFFDE68A"}, {"position": 1, "color": "#FFF97316"}]
          }
        ],
        "radius": [24, 4, 24, 4]
      }
    },
    "outlined": {
      "type": "box",
      "layout": {"width": 140, "height": 120},
      "decoration": {"strokes": [{"color": "#FF2563EB"}], "strokeWidth": 2, "dashPattern": [6, 4], "radius": 12}
    }
  }
}
```

<a id="decoration-reference"></a>
## Reference

<a id="decoration-decoration-fields"></a>
### Decoration fields

A node's `"decoration"`: what its box paints. Types without a box decoration keep only blur effects. Fills paint
bottom to top under the node's content; `foregroundFills` paint over it, children included. Every colour may be a
theme colour's name.

| Key | Type | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `fills` | List<[Paint](#type-Paint)> | `[]` |  | Paints for the box, bottom to top: a colour, a gradient, an image or noise. |
| `strokes` | List<[Paint](#type-Paint)> | `[]` |  | Paints for the border, drawn `strokeWidth` wide. |
| `strokeWidth` | double | `1` | ≥ 0 | The border's width in pixels. Without `strokes` it draws nothing. |
| `strokeAlign` | [StrokeAlign](#enum-StrokeAlign) | `"inside"` | `inside`, `center`, `outside` |  |
| `strokeSides` | [StrokeSides](#enum-StrokeSides) | `"all"` |  | Which sides the border is drawn on: `all`, `top`, `bottom`, `left`, `right`, `topBottom`, `leftRight`... |
| `strokeCap` | [StrokeCap](#enum-StrokeCap) | `"butt"` | `butt`, `round`, `square` |  |
| `dashPattern` | List<double> | `[]` |  | Dash and gap lengths, alternating; empty is a solid stroke. |
| `radius` | [BorderRadius](#type-BorderRadius) | `0` |  |  |
| `effects` | List<[Effect](#type-Effect)> | `[]` |  | Shadows and blurs: each `{"type": "dropShadow" \| "innerShadow" \| "layerBlur" \| "backgroundBlur", ...}`. |
| `clip` | [Clip](#enum-Clip) | `"none"` | `none`, `hardEdge`, `antiAlias`, `antiAliasWithSaveLayer` | Clips the content to the box (rounded by `radius`). |
| `blendMode` | [BlendMode](#enum-BlendMode) | `"srcOver"` |  |  |
| `foregroundFills` | List<[Paint](#type-Paint)> | `[]` |  | Fills painted over the content. |
| `shape` | [DecorationShape](#enum-DecorationShape) | `"rectangle"` | `rectangle`, `circle` | A rectangle (rounded by `radius`) or a circle. |

<a id="node-icon"></a>
### `icon`

Flutter `Icon`.

Flutter `Icon` (font icons) or an SVG/image icon.

- Children: none.
- Decoration: none: only blur effects in `decoration.effects` apply.

| Key | Type | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `icon` | [IconData](#type-IconData) | `{}` |  | Which glyph: a Material icon name, `"check_circle"` (a style by suffix: `"search_rounded"`), the one form to write everywhere (an icon node, an input's `prefixIcon`). Also read: an image URL, and the object forms of older documents (`{"type": "MATERIAL_ICON", "name", "style"}`, `{"type": "CUPERTINO_ICON", "codepoint"}`). |
| `color` | [Color](#type-Color) | unset |  | The glyph's colour (`"#AARRGGBB"` or a theme colour's name). |
| `size` | double | unset | ≥ 0 | Flutter `Icon.size`: the glyph's width and height. Unset, the glyph fills the node's box (contained, centred), as before. Set, the glyph is drawn at this size, centred in the node's box (at most the box), and a hugging axis of the node takes it (`{"hug": 24}` with `"size": 18` is 18 wide). |

<a id="node-path"></a>
### `path`

Flutter `CustomPaint` of an SVG path.

An SVG path, filled and stroked with the node's decoration (Flutter `CustomPaint`).

- Children: none.
- Decoration: box decoration (fills, strokes, radius, shadows, clip).

| Key | Type | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `data` | String | `""` |  | SVG path data (`M0 0 L10 10 Z`). |
| `viewBox` | [Size](#type-Size) | unset |  | The coordinate space of `data`, `[width, height]`, scaled to the box. Null: `data` is in the box's own pixels. |
| `scaleStroke` | bool | `false` |  | Whether the stroke (its width and dash lengths) is in `viewBox` units, scaled with the drawing as in SVG, instead of the box's pixels (an icon's line keeps its weight at any size; a diagram's grows with it). |
| `trimStart` | double | `0` | ≥ 0, ≤ 1 | The stroked part of the path, as fractions of its length. |
| `trimEnd` | double | `1` | ≥ 0, ≤ 1 |  |
| `strokeJoin` | [StrokeJoin](#enum-StrokeJoin) | `"miter"` | `miter`, `round`, `bevel` | How segments meet when stroked (`Paint.strokeJoin`). |
| `strokeMiterLimit` | double | `4` | ≥ 0 | The miter limit of `StrokeJoin.miter` corners (`Paint.strokeMiterLimit`). |

<a id="behavior-customPaint"></a>
### `customPaint` (behavior)

A node key (beside `layout` and `props`). Type: [CustomPaint](#type-CustomPaint). Default: unset.

Flutter's `CustomPaint`: draw lists behind and over the content.

<a id="type-CustomPaint"></a>
#### CustomPaint

Flutter's `CustomPaint` on a node: `painter` drawn behind the node's content (its decoration and children) and `foregroundPainter` over it, both in the node's box (inside its transform and opacity, outside its clip). The node's layout is `CustomPaint.size`; its content is `child`.

`viewBox` is the ops' coordinate space, `[minX, minY, width, height]` (JSON also `[width, height]`), mapped onto the box by `fit` (`fill` stretches, as the `path` node's view box does); null: the box's own pixels. In expressions `size.width` and `size.height` are the view box's size when there is one, else the box's.

| Key | Type | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `painter` | List<DrawOp> | `[]` |  | Drawn behind the node's content (CustomPaint.painter). |
| `foregroundPainter` | List<DrawOp> | `[]` |  | Drawn over the node's content (CustomPaint.foregroundPainter). |
| `viewBox` | [Rect](#type-Rect) | unset |  | The ops' coordinates, [width, height] or [minX, minY, width, height], mapped onto the box by fit. Null: box pixels. |
| `fit` | [BoxFit](#enum-BoxFit) | `"fill"` | `fill`, `contain`, `cover`, `fitWidth`, `fitHeight`, `none`, `scaleDown` | How the view box maps onto the box. |
| `isComplex` | bool | `false` |  | Raster cache hint: the drawing is costly. |
| `willChange` | bool | `false` |  | Raster cache hint: the drawing changes often. |

<a id="decoration-triggers"></a>
### Triggers

Written as `"trigger": {"type": "<trigger>", ...}` in a reaction ([trigger fields](#interaction-trigger-fields)).

| Trigger | When it fires |
|---|---|
| <a id="trigger-imageLoading"></a>`imageLoading` | A node's image fill started loading, became ready, or failed. `${result.url}` identifies the image and `${result.status}` is `loading`, `loaded`, or `error`. Cached images can report loaded immediately without a loading event. |
| <a id="trigger-imageLoaded"></a>`imageLoaded` |  |
| <a id="trigger-imageError"></a>`imageError` |  |

<a id="type-Paint"></a>
### Paint

A fill or stroke paint: a solid color, a gradient or an image. Several paints stack, first at the bottom.

| Key | Type | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `type` | [PaintType](#enum-PaintType) | `"solid"` | `solid`, `linear`, `radial`, `sweep`, `diamond`, `image`, `noise` | What the paint is: `solid` (a colour), `linear`, `radial`, `sweep` or `diamond` (a gradient of `stops`), `image`, or `noise`. Without one: an image if it has `image`, a linear gradient if it has `stops`, else solid. |
| `id` | String | unset |  | Stable id, so a binding can target one paint (`fill-<id>`). |
| `visible` | bool | `true` |  | False keeps the paint but does not draw it. |
| `opacity` | double | `1` | ≥ 0, ≤ 1 | The paint's opacity, 0 to 1, multiplied with its colours' own alpha. |
| `blendMode` | [BlendMode](#enum-BlendMode) | `"srcOver"` |  | How the paint blends with what is under it (CSS `mix-blend-mode`). |
| `color` | [Color](#type-Color) | unset |  | Solid color (type `solid`). |
| `stops` | List<[ColorStop](#type-ColorStop)> | `[]` |  | Gradient stops (gradient types). |
| `transform` | List<double> | unset |  | Six numbers `[a, b, tx, c, d, ty]` mapping a point (x, y) of the box, in its unit square (0 to 1 each way), into the gradient's unit square: u = a·x + b·y + tx, v = c·x + d·y + ty. A linear gradient runs along u from 0 to 1; `[20, 0, 0, 0, 1, 0]` with `"tileMode": "repeated"` repeats it 20 times across the box. Simpler: `begin`/`end` (linear) or `center`/`radius` (radial). |
| `begin` | [Alignment](#type-Alignment) | unset |  | Linear: where the gradient starts, an alignment (`[-1, 0]` or `"centerLeft"`, Flutter `LinearGradient.begin`). Read into `transform`; default the left edge. |
| `end` | [Alignment](#type-Alignment) | unset |  | Linear: where the gradient ends (Flutter `LinearGradient.end`). `"begin": [0, -1], "end": [0, 1]` runs top to bottom; `"begin": [-1, 0], "end": [-0.9, 0]` with `"tileMode": "repeated"` repeats it every 5% of the width. |
| `center` | [Alignment](#type-Alignment) | unset |  | Radial: its center, an alignment (`[0, -1]`: the middle of the top edge; Flutter `RadialGradient.center`). Read into `transform`; default the box's center. |
| `tileMode` | [TileMode](#enum-TileMode) | `"clamp"` | `clamp`, `repeated`, `mirror`, `decal` | What a gradient does past `begin` and `end`: `clamp` (keeps the end colours), `repeated`, `mirror`, `decal`. |
| `image` | [ImagePaint](#type-ImagePaint) | unset |  | Image (type `image`). |
| `radius` | double | unset | ≥ 0 | Radial: the radius as a share of the box's shortest side (Flutter's RadialGradient); null: half the box's width (as the transform maps it). Past the last stop the gradient keeps the last stop's color (`tileMode` clamp): end a glow on a transparent stop, or it fills the rest of the box. |
| `length` | double | unset | ≥ 0 | A gradient's length in logical pixels, whatever the box's size: linear, from `begin` toward `end` (only their direction counts then); radial, its radius. With `"tileMode": "repeated"` the stops repeat every `length` px: CSS `repeating-linear-gradient(to bottom, #1F2937 0 1px, transparent 1px 80px)` is `{"type": "linear", "begin": "topCenter", "end": "bottomCenter", "length": 80, "tileMode": "repeated", "stops": [{"position": 0, "color": "#FF1F2937"}, {"position": 0.0125, "color": "#FF1F2937"}, {"position": 0.0125, "color": "#00000000"}, {"position": 1, "color": "#00000000"}]}`: a 1 px line every 80 px (a background grid is two such paints). |
| `noise` | [NoisePaint](#type-NoisePaint) | unset |  | Type `noise`: procedural grain, as SVG `<feTurbulence>`: `{"baseFrequency": 0.8, "numOctaves": 3, "seed": 0, "type": "fractalNoise"}`. With `color` the grain is that color, its alpha the noise; without, the four noise channels feTurbulence gives. Fade it with `opacity` (a film grain: 0.05 to 0.12) and set a `blendMode` (`overlay`, `softLight`) as CSS `mix-blend-mode`. Drawn as a seamless 256 px tile repeated over the box. |

<a id="type-ColorStop"></a>
### ColorStop

One gradient stop.

| Key | Type | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `position` | double | `0` | ≥ 0, ≤ 1 | Where the colour sits along the gradient, 0 (its start) to 1 (its end). |
| `color` | [Color](#type-Color) | `"#FF000000"` |  | The colour at `position`. |

<a id="type-ImagePaint"></a>
### ImagePaint

An image source and how it fills its box (Flutter's `DecorationImage`).

| Key | Type | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `url` | String | unset |  | The image's URL: `https://`, a `data:image/...` URL, or (for the render command's drafts) a path relative to the document. |
| `assetId` | String | unset |  | A project asset's id, for images uploaded to the project. |
| `fit` | [BoxFit](#enum-BoxFit) | `"cover"` | `fill`, `contain`, `cover`, `fitWidth`, `fitHeight`, `none`, `scaleDown` | How the image fills the box (Flutter's `BoxFit`): `cover`, `contain`, `fill`, `fitWidth`... |
| `alignment` | [Alignment](#type-Alignment) | `[0,0]` |  | Where the image sits in the box when it does not fill it, or which part shows when it is cropped. |
| `repeat` | [ImageRepeat](#enum-ImageRepeat) | `"noRepeat"` | `noRepeat`, `repeat`, `repeatX`, `repeatY` | Whether the image repeats to fill the box (Flutter's `ImageRepeat`). |
| `scale` | double | `1` | ≥ 0 | The image's pixel scale (`Image.scale`): 2 draws it at half its size. |
| `tint` | [Color](#type-Color) | unset |  | Draws every pixel in this color, keeping its alpha (`ColorFilter.mode(tint, BlendMode.srcIn)`). |
| `flipX` | bool | `false` |  | Mirrors the image horizontally / vertically. |
| `flipY` | bool | `false` |  | Mirrors the image horizontally / vertically. |
| `saturation` | double | `1` | ≥ 0 | Color saturation: 1 keeps the colors, 0 is grayscale. |
| `rect` | [Rect](#type-Rect) | unset |  | `[left, top, width, height]`, or null (placed by fit and alignment). |

<a id="type-NoisePaint"></a>
### NoisePaint

A `noise` paint's procedural noise, parameterised as SVG's `<feTurbulence>` (`baseFrequency`, `numOctaves`, `seed`, `type`): the texture a web page's grain overlay draws (`filter: url(#grain)`), here a paint, drawn as a seamless tile repeated over the box.

| Key | Type | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `baseFrequency` | double | `0.8` | ≥ 0, ≤ 4 | Lattice cells per pixel (feTurbulence `baseFrequency`): 0.8 a fine grain, 0.05 soft clouds. |
| `numOctaves` | int | `3` | ≥ 1 | Octaves summed, each twice the frequency at half the amplitude. |
| `seed` | int | `0` |  | The random seed: the same seed draws the same grain. |
| `type` | [NoiseType](#enum-NoiseType) | `"fractalNoise"` | `fractalNoise`, `turbulence` | `fractalNoise` (a soft grain) or `turbulence` (ridged). |

<a id="type-Effect"></a>
### Effect

A shadow or blur (Flutter's `BoxShadow`, `ImageFilter.blur`).

| Key | Type | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `type` | [EffectType](#enum-EffectType) | `"dropShadow"` | `dropShadow`, `innerShadow`, `layerBlur`, `backgroundBlur` | The effect: `dropShadow`, `innerShadow`, `layerBlur` (blurs the node) or `backgroundBlur` (blurs what is behind it: frosted glass). Required: an effect without a type is dropped. |
| `id` | String | unset |  | An id a binding can select the effect by (`decoration.effects.glow.color`). |
| `visible` | bool | `true` |  | False keeps the effect but does not draw it. |
| `color` | [Color](#type-Color) | `"#40000000"` |  | The shadow's colour. |
| `offset` | [Offset](#type-Offset) | `[0,0]` |  | The shadow's offset `[dx, dy]` in pixels. |
| `blurRadius` | double | `0` | ≥ 0 | How soft the shadow or blur is, in pixels. |
| `spreadRadius` | double | `0` |  | How far the shadow grows past the box before blurring, in pixels. |
| `blendMode` | [BlendMode](#enum-BlendMode) | `"srcOver"` |  | How the effect blends with what is under it. |

<a id="type-BorderSide"></a>
### BorderSide

Flutter's `BorderSide`. A null `color` is unset: the widget's theme default where it has one, else Flutter's black.

| Key | Type | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `color` | [Color](#type-Color) | unset |  | The line's colour. |
| `width` | double | `1` | ≥ 0 | The line's width in pixels. |
| `style` | [BorderStyle](#enum-BorderStyle) | `"solid"` | `none`, `solid` | `solid` or `none`. |
| `strokeAlign` | [StrokeAlign](#enum-StrokeAlign) | `"inside"` | `inside`, `center`, `outside` | Where the line sits on the edge: inside, centered on it, or outside. |

<a id="decoration-patterns"></a>
## Patterns

<a id="decoration-gradients"></a>
### Gradients

As Flutter's `LinearGradient`, a linear gradient runs from `"begin"` to `"end"` (alignments; default left to
right; `[0, -1]` to `[0, 1]` is top to bottom). As `RadialGradient`, a radial one has a `"center"` and a `"radius"`
(a share of the box's shortest side); past the last stop it keeps that stop's colour, so end a glow on a transparent
stop. `transform` is the general form. A paint without `type` is an image if it has `image`, a linear gradient if it
has `stops`, else a solid colour.

<a id="decoration-a-pattern-in-pixels-a-background-grid-grain"></a>
### A pattern in pixels, a background grid, grain

**A pattern in pixels** (CSS `repeating-linear-gradient(to bottom, #E5E7EB 0 1px, transparent 1px 80px)`): a
linear gradient with `"length": 80` (px from `begin` toward `end`) and `"tileMode": "repeated"`; a background grid is
two of them, one `topCenter` → `bottomCenter`, one `centerLeft` → `centerRight`.

```json
"fills": [
  {"type": "linear", "begin": "topCenter", "end": "bottomCenter", "length": 80, "tileMode": "repeated",
   "stops": [{"position": 0, "color": "#14FFFFFF"}, {"position": 0.0125, "color": "#14FFFFFF"}, {"position": 0.0125, "color": "#00FFFFFF"}, {"position": 1, "color": "#00FFFFFF"}]},
  {"type": "linear", "begin": "centerLeft", "end": "centerRight", "length": 80, "tileMode": "repeated",
   "stops": [{"position": 0, "color": "#14FFFFFF"}, {"position": 0.0125, "color": "#14FFFFFF"}, {"position": 0.0125, "color": "#00FFFFFF"}, {"position": 1, "color": "#00FFFFFF"}]}
]
```

**Grain**: `{"type": "noise", "noise": {"baseFrequency": 0.8, "numOctaves": 3, "seed": 1}, "color": "#FF000000",
"opacity": 0.08}`, SVG's `feTurbulence` as a paint (a seamless tile repeated over the box; `blendMode` as CSS
`mix-blend-mode`).

<a id="decoration-borders-rules-and-shadows"></a>
### Borders, rules and shadows

A node's border is painted with its own box, **under its children**: a child with a fill covers an `inside` border
(the default). Give the parent padding of the border's width, set `"strokeAlign": "outside"`, or put the border (or
the rule) on the filled child. `strokes` with `strokeWidth` (default 1), `strokeAlign` (`inside`, `center`, `outside`), `strokeSides` (`all`,
`bottom`, `topBottom`...) and `dashPattern` (`[6, 4]`). A rule under a text: the text inside a `row` or `column`
with `"strokes": [{"color": ...}], "strokeSides": "bottom"`, or a `box` 1 high. `strokeWidth` without `strokes`
draws nothing. Effects: `dropShadow`, `innerShadow`, `layerBlur`, `backgroundBlur` (frosted glass), each with
`color`, `offset`, `blurRadius`, `spreadRadius`.

<a id="decoration-a-scrim-over-a-photo"></a>
### A scrim over a photo

`foregroundFills` paint over the node **and its children**, as Flutter's `foregroundDecoration`: a scrim there
darkens a caption inside the node too. For a caption over a photo, paint the photo in `fills` and put the darkening
gradient on a child `box` before the caption (a stack: photo box, gradient box, caption text), or on the photo
box's `foregroundFills` when the caption is a sibling painted after it.

<a id="decoration-images"></a>
### Images

Images are image fills: `{"type": "image", "image": {"url": "...", "fit": "cover"}}` in `decoration.fills` of a box
(give the box the image's size or an `aspectRatio`), placed as Flutter's `DecorationImage` places them: `fit` is a
`BoxFit` (`cover`, `contain`, `fill`, `fitWidth`, `fitHeight`, `none`, `scaleDown`) and `alignment` an `Alignment`
(`[0, -0.3]` keeps a face in a cropped photo). The `url` is one of:

- **a file beside the site**, by its path relative to `site.json`'s folder (`"images/hero.jpg"`, as a Flutter app
  names an asset): PNG, JPEG, WebP, GIF, BMP or SVG. The render command reads it from the folder; a published site
  from its files. A path that names no file is `image_failed`, naming it. Use this for photos and illustrations.
- `https://...`: loaded by the app; the render command does not fetch it (`image_network`).
- `data:image/...` (an SVG may be written inline as `data:image/svg+xml;utf8,<svg ...>`, URL-encoded).

Fills stack, first at the bottom: a photo with a gradient scrim over it, so text reads on it, is two fills:

```json
{
  "schema": 3,
  "roots": ["story"],
  "nodes": {
    "story": {
      "type": "canvas",
      "slots": {"body": "page"},
      "layout": {"width": 390, "height": 320},
      "decoration": {"fills": [{"color": "#FFFFFFFF"}]}
    },
    "page": {
      "type": "column",
      "children": ["card"],
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 390}, "height": {"fill": 320}, "padding": 24}
    },
    "card": {
      "type": "column",
      "children": ["kicker", "headline"],
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 342}, "height": 240, "padding": 20},
      "props": {"mainAxisAlignment": "end", "crossAxisAlignment": "start", "spacing": 6},
      "decoration": {
        "radius": 16,
        "clip": "antiAlias",
        "fills": [
          {"type": "image", "image": {"url": "assets/photo.png", "fit": "cover", "alignment": [0, -0.3]}},
          {
            "type": "linear",
            "begin": [0, -1],
            "end": [0, 1],
            "stops": [{"color": "#00000000", "position": 0.35}, {"color": "#CC000000", "position": 1}]
          }
        ]
      }
    },
    "kicker": {
      "type": "text",
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 302}, "height": {"hug": 16}},
      "props": {
        "text": "TRAVEL",
        "style": {"fontSize": 12, "fontWeight": 700, "letterSpacing": 2, "color": "#FFFDE68A"}
      }
    },
    "headline": {
      "type": "text",
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 302}, "height": {"hug": 56}},
      "props": {
        "text": "A week on the salt marsh, by boat and on foot",
        "style": {"fontSize": 20, "fontWeight": 700, "height": 1.3, "color": "#FFFFFFFF"}
      }
    }
  }
}
```

<a id="decoration-illustration"></a>
### Illustration

Three ways to draw art without a photo, each scaled to its box:

- **An SVG file** (`images/hills.svg`) as an image fill: drawn as vectors at any size, `fit` and `alignment` as
  for a photo. For a single shape or mark, a `path` node with SVG path data and a `viewBox`.

```json
{
  "schema": 3,
  "roots": ["hero"],
  "nodes": {
    "hero": {
      "type": "canvas",
      "slots": {"body": "page"},
      "layout": {"width": 390, "height": 340},
      "decoration": {"fills": [{"color": "#FFFFFFFF"}]}
    },
    "page": {
      "type": "column",
      "children": ["art", "badge"],
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 390}, "height": {"fill": 340}, "padding": 24},
      "props": {"spacing": 12}
    },
    "art": {
      "type": "box",
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 342}, "height": 214},
      "decoration": {
        "radius": 12,
        "clip": "antiAlias",
        "fills": [{"type": "image", "image": {"url": "assets/hills.svg", "fit": "cover"}}]
      }
    },
    "badge": {
      "type": "path",
      "layout": {"width": 48, "height": 48},
      "props": {
        "data": "M12 2 L15 9 L22 9 L16.5 13.5 L18.5 21 L12 16.5 L5.5 21 L7.5 13.5 L2 9 L9 9 Z",
        "viewBox": [24, 24]
      },
      "decoration": {"fills": [{"color": "#FFF4B740"}]}
    }
  }
}
```

- **`customPaint`**: draw lists in a view box, Flutter's `Canvas` calls as data (`rect`, `circle`, `path` with SVG
  data, `line`, `repeat` over a count with `${index}`), behind (`painter`) or over (`foregroundPainter`) the node's
  content. Values may be expressions, so a drawing can follow data. It is not
  clipped by the box's `radius`: round a parent with `clip` for that.

```json
{
  "schema": 3,
  "roots": ["hero"],
  "nodes": {
    "hero": {
      "type": "canvas",
      "slots": {"body": "page"},
      "layout": {"width": 390, "height": 260},
      "decoration": {"fills": [{"color": "#FFFFFFFF"}]}
    },
    "page": {
      "type": "column",
      "children": ["scene"],
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 390}, "height": {"fill": 260}, "padding": 24}
    },
    "scene": {
      "type": "box",
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 342}, "height": 212},
      "customPaint": {
        "viewBox": [320, 200],
        "fit": "cover",
        "painter": [
          {"op": "rect", "rect": [0, 0, 320, 200], "paint": "#FFE8F1F8"},
          {"op": "circle", "c": [236, 62], "radius": 28, "paint": "#FFF4B740"},
          {
            "op": "repeat",
            "count": 3,
            "ops": [
              {
                "op": "circle",
                "c": ["${= 60 + index * 34}", "${= 48 + index * 6}"],
                "radius": 3,
                "paint": "#FF5D6D7E"
              }
            ]
          },
          {
            "op": "path",
            "d": "M0 150 C60 100 120 110 170 140 C220 170 270 120 320 130 L320 200 L0 200 Z",
            "paint": "#FF7FB685"
          },
          {
            "op": "path",
            "d": "M0 170 C80 140 160 160 220 175 C260 185 290 170 320 165 L320 200 L0 200 Z",
            "paint": "#FF3E7C59"
          },
          {
            "op": "line",
            "p1": [40, 196],
            "p2": [280, 196],
            "paint": {"color": "#33FFFFFF", "style": "stroke", "strokeWidth": 2}
          }
        ]
      }
    }
  }
}
```

<a id="decoration-icons"></a>
### Icons

An `icon` node with `props.icon` set to a Material icon name (`"check_circle"`, `"menu"`, `"north_east"`; any name
at fonts.google.com/icons; `_outlined`, `_rounded`, `_sharp` pick the style), `props.color` and `props.size` (the
glyph's size, centered in the node's box; without it the glyph fills the box). A text field's
`decoration.prefixIcon` is `{"icon": "search", "size": 18}`. A name the renderer does not know draws nothing
(`icon_not_drawn`).

<a id="decoration-small-marks-and-shapes"></a>
### Small marks and shapes

A mark the font lacks (✦, ✳): an `icon` (`"auto_awesome"`, `"star"`), or a `path` node with SVG path data and a
`viewBox` so it scales to its box: the one decorated shape (fills, strokes and shadows from its `decoration`). Custom
drawing beyond one path (several shapes, a line through points, shapes in different colors, text on a canvas): the
`customPaint` behavior's draw lists, behind or over the node's content. A line through points is a `path` op with
`points` (a formula of `${size.width}` for a share of the box), or with `commands` (Flutter's `Path` calls:
`moveTo`, `lineTo`, `quadraticBezierTo`, `cubicTo`, `close`) for curves; shapes in different colors are one `path`
op per color.

<a id="decoration-pitfalls"></a>
## Pitfalls

- An effect needs its `type`; without it the effect is dropped.
- Colours are `"#AARRGGBB"`, `"#RRGGBB"` or a theme name; `"#FFF"`, `rgb()` and CSS names are not read.
- A `path` node without a `viewBox` is drawn in its box's own pixels from the top left and is not clipped to the
  box (as Flutter's `CustomPaint`): give it a `viewBox` to scale it, or clip an ancestor (`path_overflow`).
- Decoration on a type that draws no box (a `text`, a `listView`) is ignored (`decoration_ignored`): wrap it.
- `clip` is needed for children to follow rounded corners.
- A child's fill covers its parent's inside border: pad the parent, stroke outside, or move the border to the child.

<a id="decoration-see-also"></a>
## See also

[Theme](#page-theme) (named colours) · [animation](#page-animation) (shimmer, motion) · [values](#page-values)
(Alignment, BorderRadius and the enums).

<a id="page-forms"></a>
# Buttons, forms and inputs

<a id="forms-when-to-use"></a>
## When to use

Buttons, text fields, checkboxes, switches, radios, sliders, dropdowns, segmented buttons, date and time pickers,
chips and signatures: every control's props, **how to style each one (in one place, below)**, two-way binding to a
variable, validation and error states, focus and the keyboard.

<a id="forms-minimal-example"></a>
## Minimal example

An email field stored in a variable on every change, an error shown after a failed send, and a thank-you after a
good one:

```json
{
  "schema": 3,
  "roots": ["contact"],
  "nodes": {
    "contact": {
      "type": "canvas",
      "slots": {"body": "col"},
      "layout": {"width": 390, "height": 500},
      "decoration": {"fills": [{"color": "#FFFFFFFF"}]}
    },
    "col": {
      "type": "column",
      "children": ["email", "emailError", "send", "thanks"],
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 390}, "height": {"fill": 500}, "padding": 24},
      "props": {"spacing": 8, "crossAxisAlignment": "start"}
    },
    "email": {
      "type": "textField",
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 342}, "height": 56},
      "props": {"decoration": {"labelText": "Email", "hintText": "you@example.com"}, "keyboardType": "emailAddress"},
      "actions": [
        {
          "trigger": {"type": "changed"},
          "actions": [{"type": "setVariable", "variable": "email", "value": "${result}"}]
        }
      ]
    },
    "emailError": {
      "type": "text",
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 342}, "height": {"hug": 18}},
      "props": {"text": "Enter a valid email address.", "style": {"fontSize": 13, "color": "#FFDC2626"}},
      "bind": {"visible": "${= tried && !contains(email, '@')}"}
    },
    "send": {
      "type": "elevatedButton",
      "layout": {"width": {"hug": 120}, "height": 44},
      "props": {"label": "Send"},
      "actions": [
        {
          "trigger": {"type": "click"},
          "actions": [
            {"type": "setVariable", "variable": "tried", "value": "true"},
            {
              "type": "if",
              "condition": {"left": "${= contains(email, '@')}", "op": "isTrue"},
              "then": [{"type": "setVariable", "variable": "sent", "value": "true"}]
            }
          ]
        }
      ]
    },
    "thanks": {
      "type": "text",
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 342}, "height": {"hug": 20}},
      "props": {"text": "Thanks! We'll reply within a day.", "style": {"fontSize": 15, "color": "#FF16A34A"}},
      "bind": {"visible": "${sent}"}
    }
  },
  "variables": {
    "contact": [
      {"name": "email", "type": "text", "value": ""},
      {"name": "tried", "type": "boolean", "value": false},
      {"name": "sent", "type": "boolean", "value": false}
    ]
  }
}
```

<a id="forms-reference"></a>
## Reference

Every control's props, then the models that style them ([InputDecoration](#type-InputDecoration),
[InputBorder](#type-InputBorder), [ButtonStyle](#type-ButtonStyle)...), then the input triggers.

<a id="node-filledButton"></a>
### `filledButton`

Flutter `FilledButton`.

`ElevatedButton`, `FilledButton`, `TextButton`, `OutlinedButton`: a label with an optional icon (their `.icon` constructors), styled by a `ButtonStyle`.

- Children: none.
- Decoration: none: only blur effects in `decoration.effects` apply.

| Key | Type | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `label` | String | `""` |  | The button's text (not `text`). Its colour, size and weight are in `style`. |
| `textAlign` | [TextAlign](#enum-TextAlign) | `"start"` | `left`, `right`, `center`, `justify`, `start`, `end` |  |
| `icon` | [IconData](#type-IconData) | `{}` |  | The icon beside the label; empty for none. |
| `iconAlignment` | [IconAlignment](#enum-IconAlignment) | `"start"` | `start`, `end` |  |
| `spacing` | double | `8` | ≥ 0 | Space between the icon and the label. |
| `enabled` | bool | `true` |  | False is a disabled button (`onPressed: null`). |
| `style` | [ButtonStyle](#type-ButtonStyle) | `{}` |  | The button's look (Flutter's `ButtonStyle`): `backgroundColor`, `foregroundColor` (the label and icon), `textStyle`, `shape`, `side`, `padding`. A button's colours are here, not in `decoration`. |
| `tonal` | bool | `false` |  | `FilledButton.tonal`. |
