<a id="forms-triggers"></a>
### Triggers

Written as `"trigger": {"type": "<trigger>", ...}` in a reaction ([trigger fields](#interaction-trigger-fields)).

| Trigger | When it fires |
|---|---|
| <a id="trigger-changed"></a>`changed` | An input's value changed (typed text, a toggled checkbox, a slider step, a picked item). `${result}` is the new value (a text field's: its text, word and selection). |
| <a id="trigger-changeEnd"></a>`changeEnd` | A slider was let go, with its final value. |
| <a id="trigger-submitted"></a>`submitted` | A text field was submitted from the keyboard. |
| <a id="trigger-editingComplete"></a>`editingComplete` | A text field lost focus after editing. |
| <a id="trigger-focusGained"></a>`focusGained` | A text field gained or lost focus. |
| <a id="trigger-focusLost"></a>`focusLost` |  |
| <a id="trigger-keyDown"></a>`keyDown` | A key went down (or up) while the screen shows; `Trigger.key` limits it to one key or combination, `Trigger.when` to while a formula holds. `${result.key}`, `${result.shift}`, `${result.alt}`, `${result.meta}`. |
| <a id="trigger-keyUp"></a>`keyUp` |  |

<a id="action-editText"></a>
### `editText` (action): Edit text

Edits text field `node`'s text at its cursor: wraps the selection in `before` / `after`, toggles a (numbered) list, inserts or sets `text`, replaces the word being typed, clears it or focuses it.

| Key | Type | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `node` | String | `""` |  | A text field. |
| `operation` | [EditTextOperation](#enum-EditTextOperation) | `"insert"` | `wrap`, `toggleList`, `insert`, `replaceWord`, `setText`, `clear`, `focus` |  |
| `text` | String | `""` |  |  |
| `before` | String | `""` |  |  |
| `after` | String | unset |  | Null: the same as before. |
| `numbered` | bool | `false` |  |  |

<a id="action-focus"></a>
### `focus` (action): Focus

Focuses text field `node` (selecting its text with `selectAll`), or takes the focus away (`unfocus`; from every field when `node` is empty).

| Key | Type | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `node` | String | `""` |  | A text field; empty with unfocus: every field. |
| `unfocus` | bool | `false` |  |  |
| `selectAll` | bool | `false` |  |  |

<a id="type-InputDecoration"></a>
### InputDecoration

Flutter's `InputDecoration`: a text field's border, label, hint, helper, error, prefix and suffix. Every field has Flutter's default (unset: the theme's).

| Key | Type | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `icon` | [InputIcon](#type-InputIcon) | unset |  | An icon before the field, outside its border. |
| `labelText` | String | unset |  | The label: inside the empty field, floating above it when focused or filled. |
| `labelStyle` | [TextStyle](#type-TextStyle) | `{}` |  | The label's style. |
| `floatingLabelStyle` | [TextStyle](#type-TextStyle) | `{}` |  | The label's style when it floats above the field. |
| `helperText` | String | unset |  | A line of help under the field. |
| `helperStyle` | [TextStyle](#type-TextStyle) | `{}` |  | The helper text's style. |
| `helperMaxLines` | int | unset |  | At most this many lines of helper text. |
| `hintText` | String | unset |  | Shown in the empty field (a placeholder). |
| `hintStyle` | [TextStyle](#type-TextStyle) | `{}` |  | The hint's style. |
| `hintMaxLines` | int | unset |  | At most this many lines of hint. |
| `errorText` | String | unset |  | The error under the field. Bound to a yes/no (SDK 8.x's error switch), `true` puts the field in error without a message (`kErrorWithoutMessage`: the error border only) and `false` clears it. |
| `errorStyle` | [TextStyle](#type-TextStyle) | `{}` |  | The error text's style. |
| `errorMaxLines` | int | unset |  | At most this many lines of error text. |
| `floatingLabelBehavior` | [FloatingLabelBehavior](#enum-FloatingLabelBehavior) | unset | `never`, `auto`, `always` | When the label floats above the field: `auto`, `always`, `never`. |
| `isCollapsed` | bool | `false` |  | No padding and no room for a label: the field is as small as its text. |
| `isDense` | bool | unset |  | Less vertical padding. |
| `contentPadding` | [EdgeInsets](#type-EdgeInsets) | unset |  | Space between the border and the text: a number or `[left, top, right, bottom]`. An outlined field needs some (`[14, 16, 14, 16]`) to keep the text off the border. |
| `prefixIcon` | [InputIcon](#type-InputIcon) | unset |  | An icon inside the border, before the text: `{"icon": "search", "size": 18}`; it may take reactions. |
| `prefixIconConstraints` | [BoxConstraints](#type-BoxConstraints) | `{}` |  | The prefix icon's size limits. |
| `prefixText` | String | unset |  | Text before the typed text (`$`). |
| `prefixStyle` | [TextStyle](#type-TextStyle) | `{}` |  | The prefix text's style. |
| `suffixIcon` | [InputIcon](#type-InputIcon) | unset |  | An icon inside the border, after the text: a clear (`close`) or show-password button; it may take reactions. |
| `suffixIconConstraints` | [BoxConstraints](#type-BoxConstraints) | `{}` |  | The suffix icon's size limits. |
| `suffixText` | String | unset |  | Text after the typed text (`kg`). |
| `suffixStyle` | [TextStyle](#type-TextStyle) | `{}` |  | The suffix text's style. |
| `counterText` | String | unset |  | Replaces the character counter; `""` hides it. |
| `counterStyle` | [TextStyle](#type-TextStyle) | `{}` |  | The character counter's style. |
| `filled` | bool | unset |  | Paints `fillColor` behind the field. |
| `fillColor` | [Color](#type-Color) | unset |  | The field's background, drawn when `filled` is true. |
| `focusColor` | [Color](#type-Color) | unset |  | The fill while the field has the focus. |
| `hoverColor` | [Color](#type-Color) | unset |  | The fill while a mouse is over the field. |
| `errorBorder` | [InputBorder](#type-InputBorder) | unset |  | The border while the field shows an error (`errorText` set). |
| `focusedBorder` | [InputBorder](#type-InputBorder) | unset |  | The border while the field has the focus. |
| `focusedErrorBorder` | [InputBorder](#type-InputBorder) | unset |  | The border while the field has the focus and shows an error. |
| `disabledBorder` | [InputBorder](#type-InputBorder) | unset |  | The border while the field is disabled. |
| `enabledBorder` | [InputBorder](#type-InputBorder) | unset |  | The border while the field is enabled and not focused. |
| `border` | [InputBorder](#type-InputBorder) | unset |  | The border used for any state without its own (`{"type": "outline", "borderSide": {...}, "borderRadius": 8}`, `underline` or `none`). |
| `enabled` | bool | `true` |  | False draws the field disabled. |
| `semanticCounterText` | String | unset |  | What a screen reader says for the counter. |
| `alignLabelWithHint` | bool | unset |  | Aligns the label with the hint in a multi-line field. |
| `constraints` | [BoxConstraints](#type-BoxConstraints) | `{}` |  | Size limits for the decorated field. |
| `prefixIconPadding` | [EdgeInsets](#type-EdgeInsets) | unset |  | Space around the prefix icon inside its box: places it at a set inset instead of Material's centered 48 px box; null keeps Material's layout. |
| `suffixIconPadding` | [EdgeInsets](#type-EdgeInsets) | unset |  | Space around the suffix icon inside its box; see `prefixIconPadding`. |
| `affixesAlwaysVisible` | bool | `false` |  | Shows `prefixText` and `suffixText` all the time, not only once the field is focused or has text (a unit such as "kWh"). |
| `paddingIncludesBorder` | bool | `false` |  | The active border's width adds to `contentPadding`, as a container's border adds to its padding (Flutter draws an outline over the padding). |

<a id="type-InputBorder"></a>
### InputBorder

Flutter's `InputBorder`: an `OutlineInputBorder` (the default here), an `UnderlineInputBorder` or `InputBorder.none`.

| Key | Type | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `type` | [InputBorderType](#enum-InputBorderType) | `"outline"` | `none`, `outline`, `underline` | `outline` (a box), `underline` (a line under the text) or `none`. |
| `borderSide` | [BorderSide](#type-BorderSide) | `{}` |  | The line: its colour and width. |
| `borderRadius` | [BorderRadius](#type-BorderRadius) | `4` |  | The corners' radius. |
| `gapPadding` | double | `4` | ≥ 0 | The gap around a floating label in an outline border. |

<a id="type-InputIcon"></a>
### InputIcon

An icon an input shows (`Icon`): a glyph as the icon node's `icon` prop (`{"source", "name", "codepoint", ...}` or an image), its size and color, and the actions a tap on it runs.

| Key | Type | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `icon` | [IconData](#type-IconData) | `{}` |  | The glyph, written as the `icon` node's `props.icon`: a Material icon name (`"search"`) or `{"type": "MATERIAL_ICON", "name": "search"}`. |
| `size` | double | `24` | ≥ 0 | The glyph's size. |
| `color` | [Color](#type-Color) | unset |  | The glyph's colour. |
| `actions` | List<Reaction> | `[]` |  | Reactions, as a node's: a tap on the icon (`{"trigger": {"type": "click"}, "actions": [...]}`). |

| `shape` | [ShapeBorder](#type-ShapeBorder) | unset |  | The button's shape: `{"type": "roundedRectangle", "borderRadius": 10}`, `stadium`, `circle`... |

<a id="forms-patterns"></a>
## Patterns

<a id="forms-styling-the-controls-in-one-place"></a>
### Styling the controls, in one place

| Control | Its look | Where |
|---|---|---|
| `textField` | label, hint, helper and error texts and their styles; border (`"border": {"type": "outline", "borderSide": {"color": ..., "width": 1}, "borderRadius": 8}`), `enabledBorder`, `focusedBorder`, `errorBorder`, `focusedErrorBorder`; `fillColor` + `filled`; `contentPadding`; `prefixIcon` / `suffixIcon`, `prefixText` / `suffixText` | `props.decoration` ([InputDecoration](#type-InputDecoration), [InputBorder](#type-InputBorder), [InputIcon](#type-InputIcon)) |
| `textField` | the typed text's style (`style`), alignment, the caret (`cursorColor`, `showCursor`), the focus ring (`focusRingColor`, `focusRingWidth`) | `props` ([textField](#node-textField)) |
| buttons | `backgroundColor`, `foregroundColor`, `textStyle` (the label's size and weight), `shape` (`{"type": "roundedRectangle", "borderRadius": 10}`), `side` (border), `padding`, `elevation` | `props.style` ([ButtonStyle](#type-ButtonStyle)) |
| `checkbox` | `activeColor`, `checkColor`, `fillColor`, `side` / `activeSide` (the box's border), `borderRadius`, `compact` | `props` ([checkbox](#node-checkbox)) |
| `switch` | `activeTrackColor`, `inactiveTrackColor`, `activeThumbColor`, `inactiveThumbColor`, `fillTrack`, `thumbInset`, `trackOutlineWidth`, `trackRadius` | `props` ([switch](#node-switch)) |
| `radio`, `slider`, `dropdown`, `segmentedButton` | their colours, track and thumb shapes | `props` ([radio](#node-radio), [slider](#node-slider), [dropdown](#node-dropdown), [segmentedButton](#node-segmentedButton)) |
| a labelled row | a `row` holding the control (with `"ignorePointer": true` and its value bound) and a text, with the row's `click` reaction | [a labelled checkbox](#forms-a-labelled-checkbox-or-switch) |

Every colour there may be a theme colour's name; every text style may name a theme style. An outlined field needs
`"contentPadding": [14, 16, 14, 16]` in its decoration to keep its text off the border.

<a id="forms-a-text-field-bound-to-a-variable-two-way"></a>
### A text field bound to a variable (two-way)

Bind its `props.initialValue` to the variable: `"bind": {"props.initialValue": "${query}"}`. Typing sets the
variable (its `changed` reaction also runs), and setting the variable elsewhere (a clear button, a stepper,
`--set`) changes the text, keeping the caret, as a `TextEditingController` held in state. The other inputs show
their bound value prop (`"bind": {"props.value": "${agree}"}` for a checkbox, switch, slider or dropdown,
`props.selected` for a segmented button, `props.groupValue` for radios) and report a change through `changed`:
store `${result}` in the same variable and the control follows it.

<a id="forms-validation-and-an-error-state"></a>
### Validation and an error state

Keep the values in variables, set a `tried` flag on submit, and show errors from computed variables: bind
`props.decoration.errorText` (the field turns to its `errorBorder` and shows the text) or a separate text's
`visible`. An empty `errorText` shows no error. The `validator` prop is declared but not applied by the SDK; `inputFormatter` applies only
`{"type": "regex", "pattern": ..., "allow": true}`.

```json
"variables": {"page_variables": [
  {"name": "seats", "type": "text", "value": "10"},
  {"name": "seatsError", "type": "text", "formula": "seats == '' || number(seats) < 1 ? 'Enter at least 1 seat.' : ''"}
]}
```

```json
"seatsField": {"type": "textField", "layout": {"width": 160, "height": 72},
  "bind": {"props.initialValue": "${seats}", "props.decoration.errorText": "${seatsError}"},
  "props": {"keyboardType": "number", "decoration": {"labelText": "Seats",
    "border": {"type": "outline", "borderRadius": 8}, "errorBorder": {"type": "outline", "borderRadius": 8, "borderSide": {"color": "#FFDC2626"}}}}}
```

Give a field that may show an error a hug height (`{"hug": 56}`): it grows by the error line, and the form with it;
a fixed height keeps the field that tall. A form submitted to a service: `submitForm` ([data](#page-data)).

<a id="forms-a-stepper-around-a-field"></a>
### A stepper around a field

Two icon buttons that `setVariable` with `"op": "add"` / `"subtract"` on a number, and a field bound two-way to the
same variable. Keep the last valid value in a second variable when the typed text may be invalid.

<a id="forms-a-clear-button-in-the-field"></a>
### A clear button in the field

Its `decoration.suffixIcon` with a tap reaction (`actions` is a list of reactions, as a node's), shown only while
there is text by binding the icon:

```json
"search": {"type": "textField", "layout": {"width": {"fill": 280}, "height": 44},
  "bind": {"props.initialValue": "${query}", "props.decoration.suffixIcon.icon": "${= query == '' ? '' : 'close'}"},
  "props": {"decoration": {"hintText": "Search dishes", "prefixIcon": {"icon": "search", "size": 18}, "suffixIcon": {"icon": "close", "size": 18,
    "actions": [{"trigger": {"type": "click"}, "actions": [{"type": "setVariable", "variable": "query", "value": ""}]}]}}}}
```

<a id="forms-a-labelled-checkbox-or-switch"></a>
### A labelled checkbox or switch

The whole row toggles: the control ignores the pointer and shows the variable; the row's reaction toggles it. A tap
on a control inside a tappable row otherwise runs the control's own reaction only (the innermost wins).

```json
"agreeRow": {"type": "row", "children": ["agreeBox", "agreeText"], "props": {"spacing": 8},
  "layout": {"width": {"hug": 240}, "height": 40},
  "actions": [{"trigger": {"type": "click"}, "actions": [{"type": "setVariable", "variable": "agree", "op": "toggle"}]}]},
"agreeBox": {"type": "checkbox", "ignorePointer": true, "layout": {"width": 24, "height": 24}, "bind": {"props.value": "${agree}"}},
"agreeText": {"type": "text", "props": {"text": "I agree", "style": {"fontSize": 15, "color": "#FF111827"}},
  "layout": {"width": {"hug": 60}, "height": {"hug": 20}}}
```

<a id="forms-buttons"></a>
### Buttons

Buttons (`filledButton`, `elevatedButton`, `outlinedButton`, `textButton`, `iconButton`) take `label` and `style`.
Their label text is 12 px unless `style.textStyle.fontSize` says otherwise. Give buttons a fixed or fill width. For
full control of a button's look (two lines, an icon after the label), use a `row` with a decoration, padding, text
children, a `click` reaction and [hover and pressed states](#interaction-hover-press-and-other-states).

<a id="forms-add-and-remove-items-a-list-editor"></a>
### Add and remove items (a list editor)

Add: `setVariable` on the list with `"op": "add"` (appends; a list value appends each item) and
`"value": "${= object('name', draft, 'done', false)}"`, then clear the draft; guard it with the action's `when` (or
an `if`) on the draft not being empty. Remove: in the item template, `"op": "removeAt"` with `"index": "${index}"`.
Change one item: `"op": "update"` with `index`, or a formula (`${= updateWhere(habits, 'id', item.id, h => set(h,
'done', !h.done))}`). Give items an id (`newId('habit')`) when they can be reordered or removed.

<a id="forms-focus-and-the-keyboard"></a>
### Focus and the keyboard

`focus` moves the focus to a field (or away), `editText` changes its text or selection. `submitted` fires on the
keyboard's done key; `textInputAction` picks the key. A canvas's `keyDown` reaction (`{"trigger": {"type":
"keyDown", "key": "ArrowRight"}, ...}`) runs while no text field has the focus: arrow keys between tabs, Escape to
close. The render command types with `--type <id>=<text>` (it replaces the text) and presses keys with `--key`
(after `--unfocus`).

<a id="forms-pitfalls"></a>
## Pitfalls

- A button's text is `label`, not `text`; its colours are in `style`, not `decoration`.
- A hugging button is only as wide as its label, without padding.
- An input does nothing with its value until a `changed` reaction stores it, or its value prop is bound.
- `${result}` in a `changed` chain is the new value until an action that gives a value replaces it; `setVariable`
  does not.
- Every action key is written flat in the action; a misspelled one is dropped (`unknown_action_key`).
- The `validator` prop is not applied: validate with variables.
- An outlined border without `contentPadding` puts the text on the border.

<a id="forms-see-also"></a>
## See also

[State](#page-state) (variables, computed variables) · [reactions](#interaction-reactions) · [lists](#page-lists)
(an editable list) · [data](#page-data) (`submitForm`, storage).

<a id="page-lists"></a>
# Lists, grids, tables and repeated data

<a id="lists-when-to-use"></a>
## When to use

Anything repeated from data: lists and grids from one item template, nested lists (`item`, `index`, `parent`),
equal-height card grids, tables, carousels (`pageView`), list tiles, pagination, pull to refresh, swipe actions and
reordering.

<a id="lists-minimal-example"></a>
## Minimal example

A `listView` repeats its first child once per item of its `data` binding; inside, `${item}` is the item and
`${index}` its position:

```json
{
  "schema": 3,
  "roots": ["faq"],
  "nodes": {
    "faq": {
      "type": "canvas",
      "slots": {"body": "col"},
      "layout": {"width": 390, "height": 600},
      "decoration": {"fills": [{"color": "#FFFFFFFF"}]}
    },
    "col": {
      "type": "column",
      "children": ["heading", "items"],
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 390}, "height": {"fill": 600}, "padding": 24},
      "props": {"spacing": 12, "crossAxisAlignment": "start", "scrollable": true}
    },
    "heading": {
      "type": "text",
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 342}, "height": {"hug": 30}},
      "props": {"text": "Questions", "style": {"fontSize": 24, "fontWeight": 700, "color": "#FF111827"}}
    },
    "items": {
      "type": "listView",
      "children": ["item"],
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 342}, "height": {"hug": 300}},
      "props": {"scrollable": false, "spacing": 8},
      "bind": {"data": "${questions}"}
    },
    "item": {
      "type": "column",
      "children": ["q", "a"],
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 342}, "height": {"hug": 60}, "padding": 12},
      "props": {"crossAxisAlignment": "start", "spacing": 4},
      "decoration": {"fills": [{"color": "#FFF3F4F6"}], "radius": 8},
      "actions": [
        {
          "trigger": {"type": "click"},
          "actions": [{"type": "setVariable", "variable": "open", "value": "${= open == index ? -1 : index}"}]
        }
      ]
    },
    "q": {
      "type": "text",
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 318}, "height": {"hug": 20}},
      "props": {"text": "${item.q}", "style": {"fontSize": 16, "fontWeight": 600, "color": "#FF111827"}}
    },
    "a": {
      "type": "text",
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 318}, "height": {"hug": 20}},
      "props": {"text": "${item.a}", "style": {"fontSize": 14, "height": 1.4, "color": "#FF4B5563"}},
      "bind": {"visible": "${= open == index}"}
    }
  },
  "variables": {
    "faq": [
      {"name": "open", "type": "integer", "value": -1},
      {
        "name": "questions",
        "type": "list",
        "value": [
          {"q": "Can I cancel any time?", "a": "Yes. Your plan stays active until the end of the period."},
          {"q": "Do you offer refunds?", "a": "Within 14 days of purchase, no questions asked."},
          {"q": "Is there a free trial?", "a": "Every plan starts with 30 days free."}
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

<a id="lists-reference"></a>
## Reference

<a id="node-listView"></a>
### `listView`

Flutter `ListView`; the first child is the item.

Flutter `ListView`: its first child repeated per item.

- Children: `children` and slots: `loading`, `error`, `end`, `sectionHeader`, `reorderPlaceholder`.
- Decoration: none: only blur effects in `decoration.effects` apply.

| Key | Type | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `scrollDirection` | [Axis](#enum-Axis) | `"vertical"` | `horizontal`, `vertical` | The axis it scrolls along. |
| `reverse` | bool | `false` |  |  |
| `physics` | [ScrollPhysicsType](#enum-ScrollPhysicsType) | `"platform"` | `platform`, `bouncing`, `clamping`, `never`, `rangeMaintaining` |  |
| `alwaysScroll` | bool | `true` |  | Scrolls even when the content fits (`AlwaysScrollableScrollPhysics`). |
| `primary` | bool | `false` |  |  |
| `keyboardDismissBehavior` | [KeyboardDismissBehavior](#enum-KeyboardDismissBehavior) | `"manual"` | `manual`, `onDrag` |  |
| `clipBehavior` | [Clip](#enum-Clip) | `"hardEdge"` | `none`, `hardEdge`, `antiAlias`, `antiAliasWithSaveLayer` |  |
| `itemCount` | int | unset |  | The number of items; null repeats the item without end (or one per value of the bound `data`). |
| `cacheExtent` | double | unset | ≥ 0 |  |
| `query` | Object | `{}` |  | Where the items come from in a running app: a cloud query (`{"collectionPath", "limit", "whereFilters", "orderByFilters", "paging", "loadRelated", "statusVariable"}`). Runtime only. |
| `scrollable` | bool | `true` |  | False builds every item without a viewport when the count is known and the list hugs its items (or stretches them across a cross axis it hugs). |
| `itemExtent` | double | unset | ≥ 0 | Each item's extent along the scroll direction. |
| `separator` | [ListSeparator](#enum-ListSeparator) | `"none"` | `none`, `space`, `divider` |  |
| `spacing` | double | `0` |  | The separator's extent; negative overlaps the items. Without a `separator` it is empty space (as a row's or column's spacing). |
| `dividerThickness` | double | `1` | ≥ 0 |  |
| `dividerColor` | [Color](#type-Color) | `"#FF000000"` |  |  |
| `dividerIndent` | double | `0` |  |  |
| `dividerEndIndent` | double | `0` |  |  |
| `layout` | [ListLayout](#enum-ListLayout) | `"list"` | `list`, `stack`, `deck` |  |
| `reversePaintOrder` | bool | `false` |  | Paints a layered list's items in the opposite order. |
| `itemPosition` | [Offset](#type-Offset) | unset |  | A `ListLayout.stack` list: where the item sits in the padded box when its x/y aren't bound. |
| `wrap` | bool | `false` |  | Lays every item out in runs, as Flutter `Wrap`, each item at its own size. The runs go along `scrollDirection`: with the default `vertical` the items flow top to bottom and wrap into columns; for items side by side that wrap onto new rows set `"scrollDirection": "horizontal"`. For cards in equal columns from data, a `gridView` with `minCrossAxisExtent` is usually what is wanted. |
| `wrapSpacing` | double | `0` | ≥ 0 |  |

| `wrapCrossAlignment` | [WrapCrossAlignment](#enum-WrapCrossAlignment) | `"start"` | `start`, `end`, `center` |  |
| `stretchItems` | bool | `false` |  | Every item as thick across the list as the thickest beside it. |

Taps reach the page on top first. |

<a id="node-tableView"></a>
### `tableView`

Flutter `TableView`; its slots are the cell templates.

Flutter's `TableView` (two_dimensional_scrollables): a table that scrolls on both axes, with a header row and column that stay pinned. Rows are the bound `data` (or `rowCount`); columns are `columns` (or bound `props.columns`). Its slots are templates built per cell with `${item}`: `cell` (`{value, row, column, rowIndex, columnIndex}`), `columnHeader` (`{label, column, columnIndex}`), `rowHeader` (`{row, rowIndex}`) and `corner`.

- Children: slots: `cell`, `columnHeader`, `rowHeader`, `corner`.
- Decoration: box decoration (fills, strokes, radius, shadows, clip).

| Key | Type | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `columns` | List<[TableColumn](#type-TableColumn)> | `[]` |  |  |
| `rowCount` | int | unset |  | The rows when no data is bound. |
| `rowHeight` | double | `40` | ≥ 0 |  |
| `rowHeightKey` | String | `""` |  | The field of a row (a map) that holds its own height, for rows that aren't all as tall (a summary row that grows with its content); rows without a number there are `rowHeight` tall. Empty: every row is. |
| `headerHeight` | double | `44` | ≥ 0 |  |
| `columnWidth` | double | `120` | ≥ 0 | A column's width unless it sets its own. |
| `rowHeaderWidth` | double | `120` | ≥ 0 |  |
| `fillWidth` | bool | `false` |  | Body columns grow to share the width the table has beyond all its columns' widths (equally), so a week fills a wide screen and still scrolls on a narrow one; no column is ever narrower than its width. |
| `pinHeaderRow` | bool | `true` |  |  |
| `pinHeaderColumn` | bool | `true` |  |  |
| `gridLineColor` | [Color](#type-Color) | `"#FFE0E2E8"` |  | The lines between cells; transparent for none. |
| `gridLineWidth` | double | `1` | ≥ 0 |  |
| `stripeColor` | [Color](#type-Color) | unset |  | Every other body row's background. |
| `headerColor` | [Color](#type-Color) | unset |  | The header row's and column's background. |
| `cacheExtent` | double | unset | ≥ 0 |  |
| `clipBehavior` | [Clip](#enum-Clip) | `"hardEdge"` | `none`, `hardEdge`, `antiAlias`, `antiAliasWithSaveLayer` |  |
| `horizontalPadding` | double | `0` | ≥ 0 | Space before the first column and after the last. |
| `headerBorderColor` | [Color](#type-Color) | unset |  | A line under the header row only. |
| `headerBorderWidth` | double | `1` | ≥ 0 |  |
| `rowHoverColor` | [Color](#type-Color) | unset |  | A body row's background while the pointer is over it. |
| `selectedRow` | int | `-1` |  | The selected body row (bind it), -1 for none: drawn in `selectedRowColor` with a `selectedRowEdgeWidth` edge at its start in `selectedRowEdgeColor`. |
| `selectedRowColor` | [Color](#type-Color) | unset |  |  |
| `selectedRowEdgeColor` | [Color](#type-Color) | unset |  |  |
| `selectedRowEdgeWidth` | double | `4` | ≥ 0 |  |
| `stretchLastColumn` | bool | `false` |  | The last column takes the width the columns leave over, so the ruled rows run to the table's edge. |

<a id="node-pagination"></a>
### `pagination`

Page controls for a list's pagination.

Page controls for a list's pagination (found by its name, `controller`): first, previous, page numbers with ellipses (1 … 4 5 6 … 16), next, last, a page size select and a summary. Choosing a page fires the node's `changed` reactions with the page as `${result}`.

- Children: none.
- Decoration: none: only blur effects in `decoration.effects` apply.

| `showPageNumbers` | bool | `true` |  |  |

<a id="behavior-reorderHandle"></a>
### `reorderHandle` (behavior)

A node key (beside `layout` and `props`). Type: bool. Default: `false`.

A reorderable list row's drag handle (`ReorderableDragStartListener`).

<a id="lists-triggers"></a>
### Triggers

Written as `"trigger": {"type": "<trigger>", ...}` in a reaction ([trigger fields](#interaction-trigger-fields)).

| Trigger | When it fires |
|---|---|
| <a id="trigger-reorder"></a>`reorder` | A data list row was dragged to a new place by this node, its reorder handle (`${result.from}`, `${result.to}`). A list with a `reorder` fires it too, with `${result.item}`, `${result.fromList}`, `${result.toList}`. |
| <a id="trigger-refresh"></a>`refresh` | A list or grid was pulled past its start to refresh (its `pullToRefresh`, or its pagination's); its pagination reloads its first page too. A list with this reaction can always be pulled. |
| <a id="trigger-swipeAction"></a>`swipeAction` | A swipe action of a list item ran (the list's `swipeActions`): `${result.action}`, `${result.label}`, `${result.item}`, `${result.index}`. |
| <a id="trigger-rowTap"></a>`rowTap` | A table view's body row was tapped: `${result.row}` (the row's data), `${result.rowIndex}`, `${result.column}` (the tapped column's key), `${result.columnIndex}`. |

| `page` | String | `"1"` |  | For goTo: a number or an expression. |
| `pageSize` | String | `"20"` |  | For setPageSize. |

<a id="type-Pagination"></a>
### Pagination

A pagination controller: loads a list's items page by page and exposes its state as a map variable named `name` (`${name.items}`, `${name.page}`, `${name.pageCount}`, `${name.hasMore}`, `${name.isLoadingMore}`, `${name.error}`...). Paginate actions move it.

| Key | Type | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | String | `""` |  | The map variable that holds the state, unique on its page. |
| `mode` | [PaginationMode](#enum-PaginationMode) | `"infinite"` | `pages`, `infinite`, `bidirectional` |  |
| `source` | [PaginationSource](#enum-PaginationSource) | `"data"` | `data`, `cloud`, `api` |  |
| `pageSize` | int | `20` | ≥ 1 |  |
| `pageSizeOptions` | List<int> | `[10,20,50,100]` |  | The page sizes a pagination node offers; empty offers none. |
| `strategy` | [PaginationStrategy](#enum-PaginationStrategy) | `"offset"` | `offset`, `page`, `cursor` |  |
| `keyPath` | String | `"id"` |  | The path in an item of the value that identifies it; items with the same value show once. Empty keeps every item. |
| `initialPage` | int | `1` | ≥ 1 | The page shown first, from 1. |
| `thresholdItems` | int | `5` | ≥ 0 | How many items from the end (or start) the next page starts loading. |
| `thresholdPixels` | double | `0` | ≥ 0 | The same in pixels of scroll left; 0 uses `thresholdItems` alone. |
| `cachePages` | bool | `true` |  | Loaded pages are kept to show again until a refresh. |
| `apiId` | String | unset |  | The API (`PaginationSource.api`). |
| `parameters` | Object | `{}` |  | The API call's parameters (`${page.page}`...). |
| `itemsPath` | String | `""` |  | Where in an API response the page's items, the total count and the next cursor are (empty: the response itself, unknown, none). |
| `totalPath` | String | `""` |  |  |
| `cursorPath` | String | `""` |  |  |
| `pullToRefresh` | bool | `false` |  | Pull to refresh (`RefreshIndicator`): the list's `refresh` reactions. |
| `refreshColor` | [Color](#type-Color) | unset |  |  |
| `refreshBackgroundColor` | [Color](#type-Color) | unset |  |  |
| `refreshDisplacement` | double | `40` | ≥ 0 |  |

### ListSections

Groups a data list's consecutive items with the same `groupBy` value into sections, each under the list's `sectionHeader` slot.

| Key | Type | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|

| `indexStyle` | [TextStyle](#type-TextStyle) | `{}` |  | The index's text (font, size, weight, color). |

### ListReorder

Dragging a list's items to a new place, within the list and, with a `group`, into other lists of the group (a Kanban board). A drop runs the list's `reorder` reactions with `${result.from}`, `${result.to}`, `${result.item}`, `${result.fromList}` and `${result.toList}`.

<a id="type-SwipeActions"></a>
### SwipeActions

Swipe actions on a list's items (`Dismissible`): toward the start reveals `endActions`, toward the end `startActions`; past `threshold` the first of the side runs. Running one fires the list's `swipeAction` reactions with `${result.action}`, `${result.item}`, `${result.index}`.

| Key | Type | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | bool | `true` |  |  |
| `startActions` | List<[SwipeAction](#type-SwipeAction)> | `[]` |  |  |
| `endActions` | List<[SwipeAction](#type-SwipeAction)> | `[]` |  |  |
| `threshold` | double | `0.4` | ≥ 0, ≤ 1 | The fraction of the item's width a swipe passes to run the first action. |
| `undo` | bool | `true` |  | An action that removes the item shows an Undo bar first. |
| `undoMs` | int | `4000` | ≥ 0 |  |
| `undoMessage` | String | `"${result.label}"` |  | `${result.label}` reads the action's label. |
| `apply` | [ListApply](#enum-ListApply) | `"none"` | `none`, `variable`, `cloud` |  |
| `radius` | [BorderRadius](#type-BorderRadius) | `0` |  | The revealed actions' corners (round them to match the item's). |
| `armedScale` | double | `1` | ≥ 0 | The action's label grows to this scale once a release would run it. |
| `armHaptic` | bool | `false` |  | A selection click when a swipe passes the threshold either way. |

<a id="type-TableColumn"></a>
### TableColumn

One column of a table view: the row field its cells show (`key`, read as `${item.value}`), its header text (`label`, `${item.label}`) and its width (null: the table's `columnWidth`).

| Key | Type | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `key` | String | `""` |  |  |
| `label` | String | `""` |  |  |
| `width` | double | unset | ≥ 0 |  |
| `flex` | double | `0` | ≥ 0 | The column's share of the room left when the table is wider than its columns (its width is then the least it takes); 0: fixed. |

<a id="lists-patterns"></a>
## Patterns

<a id="lists-one-template-from-data"></a>
### One template from data

A `listView` (or `gridView`, `pageView`) repeats its **first child** once per item of its `data` binding:
`"bind": {"data": "${questions}"}`. Inside the repeated child, `${item}` is the item (`${item.title}`) and
`${index}` its position from 0. A list in a scrolling page sets `"scrollable": false` so it lays out every item at
its full height; `spacing` separates items. Items fill the list's width. The item template can carry reactions: a
click on an item runs with that item's `item` and `index`. When the item is more than about five nodes, or appears
elsewhere too, make it one call of a [component](#page-components) (`"bind": {"props.plan": "${item}"}`).

<a id="lists-a-grid-of-cards"></a>
### A grid of cards

For cards in columns from one list inside a scrolling page, use a `gridView` with `minCrossAxisExtent` (CSS
`repeat(auto-fit, minmax(280px, 1fr))`: as many equal columns as fit), `"shrinkWrapRows": true` and
`"physics": "never"` (it lays out every item and the page scrolls). A fixed number of columns: `crossAxisCount`. A
`listView` with `"wrap": true` lays its items out at their own sizes in runs along its `scrollDirection`: set
`"scrollDirection": "horizontal"` for chips or nav links side by side. In wrap mode the gap between items is
`wrapSpacing` and between runs `runSpacing`; `spacing` does not apply.

<a id="lists-equal-height-cards"></a>
### Equal-height cards

In a `gridView` with `"shrinkWrapRows": true` (CSS grid's auto rows) each row is as tall as its tallest item, and
every item is stretched to it, whether it hugs or fills its height. Make the item the card (the box with the
decoration): a card *inside* a hugging item column keeps its own height, and a card that fills the item's height
there takes its design number (`fill_fallback`). A banner above one card goes inside the card, with a top margin on
the others to line them up. A card's button pinned to its bottom: a `spacer` (or a `fill` height child) between the
content and the button inside the stretched card. `shrinkWrapRows` wins over `mainAxisExtent` (`prop_ignored`); for
rows at least n tall, give the item `"constraints": {"minHeight": n}`.

<a id="lists-nested-lists"></a>
### Nested lists

A list inside a list's item repeats per item of its own `data`, usually a field of the outer item. Inside the inner
template `item` and `index` are the innermost list's; `parent` is the item around it (`${parent.item}`,
`${parent.index}`, and its fields directly: `${parent.name}`). Two levels:

```json
"sections": {"type": "listView", "children": ["section"], "bind": {"data": "${= groupBy(dishes, 'section')}"},
             "props": {"scrollable": false, "spacing": 24}, "layout": {"width": {"fill": 600}, "height": {"hug": 400}}},
"section":  {"type": "column", "children": ["sectionTitle", "dishList"], "props": {"crossAxisAlignment": "start"},
             "layout": {"width": {"fill": 600}, "height": {"hug": 200}}},
"sectionTitle": {"type": "text", "props": {"text": "${item.key} (${item.count})", "style": {"fontSize": 20, "color": "#FF111827"}},
             "layout": {"width": {"hug": 200}, "height": {"hug": 24}}},
"dishList": {"type": "listView", "children": ["dish"], "bind": {"data": "${item.items}"}, "props": {"scrollable": false},
             "layout": {"width": {"fill": 600}, "height": {"hug": 120}}},
"dish":     {"type": "text", "props": {"text": "${parent.key} ${parent.index}: ${item.name} (#${index})", "style": {"color": "#FF374151"}},
             "layout": {"width": {"fill": 600}, "height": {"hug": 20}}}
```

A third level reads the second's item as `parent`; to reach further out, carry the value down in the data.

<a id="lists-a-table-from-one-template"></a>
### A table from one template

A `listView` of rows bound to the records, each row a label and a `gridView` of cells bound to `${item.values}` with
`crossAxisCount` the number of columns: one cell node for every column (the example in
[a capped band](#layout-a-capped-band)). Four columns written by hand, or four lists side by side, are the same
table written four times. For a column that stays while the others scroll sideways, keep the label column a
`listView` of its own beside one horizontally scrolling block of the cell grids, rows the same height in both. A
`tableView` is a data table with columns declared once (sorting, row taps).

<a id="lists-a-weekly-grid"></a>
### A weekly grid

Seven columns of days from data: a `gridView` with `"crossAxisCount": 7` bound to the days (`${= range(7)}`, or a
computed list of `{day, done}` records), each cell a box whose fill is bound to the item. Rows of habits × days: a
`listView` of habits whose item holds a label and that 7-column grid bound to `${item.days}`; in a cell, `${parent}`
is the habit and `${index}` the day. A grid sizes its cells: set the cell height with `mainAxisExtent` and give
the cell `fill` on both axes (a fixed size is `fit_not_allowed`).

A tap on a day flips it in the habit's record (`setAt` and `set` build the new list); the label counts the checks:

```json
{
  "schema": 3,
  "roots": ["home"],
  "nodes": {
    "home": {
      "type": "canvas",
      "slots": {"body": "col"},
      "layout": {"width": 390, "height": 400},
      "decoration": {"fills": [{"color": "#FFFFFFFF"}]}
    },
    "col": {
      "type": "column",
      "children": ["habitList"],
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 390}, "height": {"fill": 400}, "padding": 24}
    },
    "habitList": {
      "type": "listView",
      "children": ["habit"],
      "bind": {"data": "${habits}"},
      "props": {"scrollable": false, "spacing": 12},
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 342}, "height": {"hug": 200}}
    },
    "habit": {
      "type": "column",
      "children": ["name", "week"],
      "props": {"crossAxisAlignment": "start", "spacing": 6},
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 342}, "height": {"hug": 70}}
    },
    "name": {
      "type": "text",
      "props": {"text": "${item.name}: ${= count(item.days, d => d)}", "style": {"fontSize": 15, "color": "#FF111827"}},
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 342}, "height": {"hug": 20}}
    },
    "week": {
      "type": "gridView",
      "children": ["day"],
      "bind": {"data": "${item.days}"},
      "props": {"crossAxisCount": 7, "mainAxisExtent": 40, "crossAxisSpacing": 6, "physics": "never"},
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 342}, "height": {"hug": 40}}
    },
    "day": {
      "type": "box",
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 40}, "height": {"fill": 40}},
      "decoration": {"fills": [{"color": "#FFE5E7EB"}], "radius": 20},
      "bind": {"decoration.fills[0].color": "${= item ? '#FF16A34A' : '#FFE5E7EB'}"},
      "actions": [
        {
          "trigger": {"type": "click"},
          "actions": [
            {
              "type": "setVariable",
              "variable": "habits",
              "value": "${= setAt(habits, parent.index, set(parent.item, 'days', setAt(parent.item.days, index, !item)))}"
            }
          ]
        }
      ]
    }
  },
  "variables": {
    "home": [
      {
        "name": "habits",
        "type": "list",
        "value": [
          {"name": "Water", "days": [true, true, false, false, false, false, false]},
          {"name": "Read", "days": [false, true, false, false, false, false, false]}
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

<a id="lists-a-carousel-pages-and-pagination"></a>
### A carousel, pages and pagination

A `pageView` shows one item (or child) per page and swipes between them (`viewportFraction` below 1 shows the
neighbours' edges; `initialPage`). Long lists that load in pages: the list's `pagination` settings, with a
`pagination` control or the `paginate` action to move between pages.

<a id="lists-pitfalls"></a>
## Pitfalls

- Only the first child is the template; other children are ignored.
- `item` and `index` are the innermost list's; the outer one is `parent`.
- A list inside a scrolling page needs `"scrollable": false` (or `"physics": "never"`, which a `gridView` needs:
  it has no `scrollable`), or it takes its design height and scrolls inside itself.
- A wrapping `listView` runs along its `scrollDirection`: with the default `vertical` it flows top to bottom into
  columns (`vertical_wrap`).
- Decoration on a `listView` or `gridView` is ignored (`decoration_ignored`): put the list inside a column that has
  it.
- A `fill` height inside a hugging grid item is its design number (`fill_fallback`).
- A slot inside a list of a component shows what the call passes in every item, built in the caller's scope: it
  reads the caller's variables, not the item.

<a id="lists-see-also"></a>
## See also

[State](#page-state) (list formulas: `filter`, `groupBy`, `sortBy`, `append`) · [forms](#forms-add-and-remove-items-a-list-editor)
(add and remove items) · [components](#page-components) · [responsive layout](#layout-cards-that-wrap).

<a id="page-navigation"></a>
# Screens, navigation, modals and toasts

<a id="navigation-when-to-use"></a>
## When to use

Several screens and moving between them, a page's URL path, passing values to a screen, dialogs, bottom sheets
and popovers, confirmations and toasts, app bars, navigation bars, tabs and disclosure (accordions).

<a id="navigation-minimal-example"></a>
## Minimal example

Two screens: a list that opens a detail screen with a parameter, a modal, and a toast:

```json

  "schema": 3,
  "roots": ["home", "about", "signup"],
  "nodes": {
    "home": {
      "type": "canvas",

      "layout": {"width": 390, "height": 844},
```

<a id="navigation-triggers"></a>
### Triggers

Written as `"trigger": {"type": "<trigger>", ...}` in a reaction ([trigger fields](#interaction-trigger-fields)).

| Trigger | When it fires |
|---|---|
| <a id="trigger-load"></a>`load` | A screen appeared (set on its canvas). |
| <a id="trigger-backPressed"></a>`backPressed` | On a screen (its canvas): the user tried to leave it (the system or browser back button, a back gesture, Escape on a dialog) while the canvas's `blockBack` holds (`props.blockBack`, usually bound: `${= dirty}`). The screen stays and these actions run instead, e.g. a "Discard changes?" confirm that leaves with a navigate pop, which the block doesn't stop. While `blockBack` is false, back leaves as usual and this doesn't fire. |

<a id="action-navigate"></a>
### `navigate` (action): Navigate

Goes to another screen. JSON: `{"type": "navigate", "mode": "push", "to": "canvas-b", "params": {"id": "${item.id}"}}`. The destination reads `params` as `${route.<name>}`.

| Key | Type | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `mode` | [NavigationMode](#enum-NavigationMode) | `"push"` | `push`, `pop`, `replace`, `reset` |  |
| `to` | String | `""` |  | A screen (canvas) or layout id. |
| `params` | Object | unset |  | Values the destination reads as ${route.<name>}. |
| `base` | String | `""` |  | `NavigationMode.reset`: a screen to put under the destination, so going back from it lands there. |
| `baseParams` | Object | unset |  |  |
| `transition` | [PageTransition](#enum-PageTransition) | `"platform"` | `platform`, `none`, `fade`, `fadeUp`, `slideUp`, `slideLeft`, `scale` |  |
| `transitionMs` | int | unset |  |  |
| `reverseTransitionMs` | int | unset |  |  |
| `routeTransition` | [RouteTransition](#type-RouteTransition) | unset |  | A custom transition; replaces transition and its times. |

Shows a screen (canvas) as a modal: a dialog, a sheet, a popover. The `CloseModalAction` that closes it gives the chain that opened it its `${result}`. JSON: `{"type": "openModal", "to": "canvas-d", "presentation": "bottomSheet"}`.

|---|---|---|---|---|

| `params` | Object | unset |  | Values the modal reads as ${route.<name>}. |
| `presentation` | [ModalPresentation](#enum-ModalPresentation) | `"dialog"` | `dialog`, `bottomSheet`, `adaptive`, `sideSheet`, `fullScreen`, `popover`, `banner` |  |
| `barrierDismissible` | bool | `true` |  |  |
| `barrierColor` | [Color](#type-Color) | unset |  | Null: the default scrim. |

| `placement` | [PopoverPlacement](#enum-PopoverPlacement) | `"belowStart"` |  |  |

Shows a short message (a snackbar). Its button (`actionLabel`) runs `actions` on the chain that showed it. Cosmetics beyond the fields below (colors, radius, shadows, text styles, offsets per breakpoint) are in `style`, JSON.

| Key | Type | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `label` | String | `""` |  |  |
| `icon` | [IconData](#type-IconData) | `{}` |  |  |
| `iconColor` | [Color](#type-Color) | unset |  |  |
| `selectedIcon` | [IconData](#type-IconData) | unset |  |  |
| `selectedIconColor` | [Color](#type-Color) | unset |  |  |
| `tooltip` | String | unset |  |  |
| `backgroundColor` | [Color](#type-Color) | unset |  | `BottomNavigationBarItem.backgroundColor` (shifting bars). |
| `actions` | List<Reaction> | `[]` |  |  |

<a id="type-RouteTransition"></a>
### RouteTransition

A composable route transition. `enter` is where the incoming screen starts, `exit` where the covered one ends; closing plays them in reverse unless `popEnter` (where the screen revealed by the pop starts) or `popExit` (where the closing screen goes) are given. A `preset` fills in what's left null. JSON: an object, or a bare preset name.

| Key | Type | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `preset` | [RouteTransitionPreset](#enum-RouteTransitionPreset) | unset | `sharedAxisX`, `sharedAxisY`, `sharedAxisZ`, `fadeThrough`, `iosPush`, `iosModal`, `circularReveal`, `zoom`, `coverVertical`, `cube`, `flip` | A ready-made transition; the sides given override its own. |
| `enter` | [TransitionSide](#type-TransitionSide) | unset |  | Where the incoming screen starts. |
| `exit` | [TransitionSide](#type-TransitionSide) | unset |  | Where the covered screen ends. |
| `popEnter` | [TransitionSide](#type-TransitionSide) | unset |  | Null: exit reversed. |
| `popExit` | [TransitionSide](#type-TransitionSide) | unset |  | Null: enter reversed. |
| `durationMs` | int | unset |  | Null: the preset's (300). |
| `reverseDurationMs` | int | unset |  | Null: `durationMs`. |
| `barrierColor` | [Color](#type-Color) | unset |  | Drawn behind a modal (or a see-through page) while it's open. Null: none on pages, the dialog's own on modals. |
| `opaque` | bool | unset |  | Whether the screen hides the one below once open. Null: the preset's (true without one). |
| `swipeBack` | [RouteSwipeBack](#enum-RouteSwipeBack) | unset | `platform`, `always`, `never` | Null: the preset's (`RouteSwipeBack.platform` without one). |
| `dismiss` | [RouteDismiss](#type-RouteDismiss) | unset |  | A drag that closes the screen. |

<a id="type-RouteDismiss"></a>
### RouteDismiss

A drag anywhere on a screen that closes it interactively: the drag runs the transition backwards, and on release the pop completes or cancels with `spring`.

| Key | Type | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `direction` | [DragDirection](#enum-DragDirection) | `"down"` | `left`, `right`, `up`, `down` | The way the screen is dragged to close it. |
| `distance` | double | `0.25` |  | The share of the screen's size along `direction` a slow drag must pass. |
| `velocity` | double | `700` |  | A fling faster than this (px/s) toward `direction` closes it. |
| `spring` | [Spring](#type-Spring) | `{}` |  |  |

<a id="navigation-patterns"></a>
## Patterns

<a id="navigation-screens"></a>
### Screens

Each canvas in `roots` is a screen, unless canvases are grouped: canvases with the same `props.screen` are one
screen, one canvas per breakpoint ([a canvas per breakpoint](#layout-a-canvas-per-breakpoint)). A canvas is the
`Scaffold` of its screen: put the page content in its `body` slot, usually a column filling it. Its
`decoration.fills` is the page background; its `layout` is its design size (on a device the canvas takes the
screen's size).

A site's pages may be separate documents (one file per page, checked and rendered together); `navigate` then names a
canvas id of another document. Give a canvas a `"path"` (`"pricing"`, a top-level key of the canvas node, not a
prop) for its URL; without one it gets a path from its name. The first screen of the first document is the entry
screen.

<a id="navigation-going-to-a-screen-and-back"></a>
### Going to a screen and back

`{"type": "navigate", "to": "<canvas id>"}` pushes the screen; `"mode": "pop"` goes back; `"replace"` and `"reset"`
replace the history. For a screen with a canvas per breakpoint, name any of them. `"params": {"id": "${item.id}"}`
passes values the destination reads as `${route.id}`. A link to the screen's path with a query string passes the same
(`trip?id=coast`), and so does the render command's `--navigate trip?id=coast`. A screen opened without the param
reads it as empty: give the page a default (`coalesce(find(trips, 'id', route.id), first(trips))`).
`transition` picks the animation (`fade`, `slideUp`...).

<a id="navigation-modals-and-toasts"></a>
### Modals and toasts

`{"type": "openModal", "to": "<canvas id>"}` shows another canvas over the screen, at its design size
(`presentation`: `dialog`, `bottomSheet`, `fullScreen`, a popover anchored to a node...). Inside it,
`{"type": "closeModal"}` closes it, and its value becomes the opener's `${result}`. The modal canvas is a root like
any screen; give it the size of the dialog. `{"type": "showToast", "message": "Saved", "style": "success"}` shows a
short message; `confirm` asks yes or no and runs `actions` or `cancelActions`.

<a id="navigation-a-mobile-menu-drawer"></a>
### A mobile menu (drawer)

A menu button that toggles a `menuOpen` variable, and the menu a node bound `"visible": "${menuOpen}"`. As an
overlay over the page: the canvas body is a `stack` filling it, the page's scrolling column first and the menu
panel last (fill width, placed at `"y": 64`), hidden unless open; or open it as a modal (`"presentation":
"fullScreen"` or a sheet). A link in the menu closes it (`setVariable menuOpen false`) and navigates. The render
command captures the open state with `--tap menuButton`; an overlay sized to the window is drawn in the first
window of a `--full-page` capture.

<a id="navigation-tabs-and-an-accordion-faq"></a>
### Tabs and an accordion (FAQ)

Tabs from a variable: a row of tab labels whose `selected` binds to `${= tab == 'lunch'}` with a click that sets
`tab`, and the panels bound `visible` on `tab` (the `tabs` and `tabBar` node types do the same with Material's
look). An FAQ where several items may be open: a list variable of open indices; an item's click sets
`${= contains(open, index) ? without(open, index) : append(open, index)}`, its answer is visible while
`${= contains(open, index)}`, and its icon turns (`motion.rotate`) with a transition.

<a id="navigation-app-bars-and-navigation-bars"></a>
### App bars and navigation bars

A canvas's `appBar` slot spans the top at its own height and `bottomNavigationBar` the bottom; the body sits
between, and `floatingActionButton` sits 16 px from the right above the bottom bar. `navigationBar` and
`bottomNavigationBar` take destinations (icon, label) and report the chosen index through `changed`.

<a id="navigation-pitfalls"></a>
## Pitfalls

- `to` names a canvas id; a screen that is not a root cannot be shown.
- A modal shows its canvas at its design size: give the modal canvas the dialog's size, not the screen's.
- `${route.<param>}` exists only on the screen navigated to with `params`.
- A canvas's `path` is a top-level key of the canvas node, not a prop.
- Menus hidden behind `hovered` never open on touch screens.

<a id="navigation-see-also"></a>
## See also

[State](#page-state) (variables kept across screens: `page_variables`) · [interaction](#page-interaction) (keys,
hover) · [responsive layout](#page-layout) (a canvas per breakpoint) · [animation](#page-animation) (route
transitions).

<a id="page-state"></a>
# State and logic

<a id="state-when-to-use"></a>
## When to use

Variables and where they live, computed and function variables, expressions and every binding path with the value
it expects, conditions, the formula functions (grouped: text, numbers, money, lists, objects, dates, colours), the
actions that change state, and sandboxed scripts.

<a id="state-minimal-example"></a>
## Minimal example

A counter: a variable, two buttons that change it, and a text and a colour bound to it.

```json
{
  "schema": 3,
  "roots": ["counter"],
  "nodes": {
    "counter": {
      "type": "canvas",
      "slots": {"body": "col"},
      "layout": {"width": 390, "height": 400},
      "decoration": {"fills": [{"color": "#FFFFFFFF"}]}
    },
    "col": {
      "type": "column",
      "children": ["label", "total", "add"],
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 390}, "height": {"fill": 400}, "padding": 24},
      "props": {"spacing": 12, "mainAxisAlignment": "center"}
    },
    "label": {
      "type": "text",
      "layout": {"width": {"hug": 120}, "height": {"hug": 24}},
      "props": {"text": "Clicked ${count} times", "style": {"fontSize": 18, "color": "#FF111827"}}
    },
    "total": {
      "type": "text",
      "layout": {"width": {"hug": 120}, "height": {"hug": 20}},
      "props": {"text": "", "style": {"fontSize": 14, "color": "#FF6B7280"}},
      "bind": {"props.text": "${= 'Total: ' + money(count * price, '$')}"}
    },
    "add": {
      "type": "box",
      "layout": {"width": 160, "height": 44},
      "decoration": {"fills": [{"color": "#FF2563EB"}], "radius": 8},
      "actions": [
        {
          "trigger": {"type": "click"},
          "actions": [{"type": "setVariable", "variable": "count", "op": "add", "value": "1"}]
        }
      ]
    }
  },
  "variables": {
    "counter": [{"name": "count", "type": "integer", "value": 0}, {"name": "price", "type": "decimal", "value": 2.5}]
  }
}
```

<a id="state-reference"></a>
## Reference

<a id="state-variables"></a>
### Variables

Declare them in the document's `variables`, under a canvas id (that canvas only) or under `"page_variables"` (every
canvas of the document, kept while the user moves between them). A site's `site.json` adds project variables, read
by bare name in every page and component. A variable's keys:

| Key | Example | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | `"v1"` |  |
| `name` | `"count"` | Unique in its scope; what expressions read (`${name}`). |
| `type` | `"integer"` |  |
| `value` | `3` | The default value, as `type` holds it (see `VariableType.coerce`); null when unset. |
| `formula` | `"a + 1"` | The expression (what goes in `${= ...}`) that computes the value of a computed variable; empty for a plain one. A computed variable is read-only: it changes when what its formula reads changes. |
| `parameters` | `["a"]` | A computed variable with parameters is a function: formulas call it by name (`clamp01(x)`), and its `formula` reads the arguments by these names. |
| `options` | `["a"]` | The options of a `VariableType.choice` variable. |
| `persist` | `true` | Whether the app keeps the value on the device: it starts from the value it had last time (not `value`) and every change is saved. A draft, a list the user builds up. A computed variable can't persist (`persists`). |

Types:

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `integer` | A whole number (`int`). |
| `text` | Text (`String`). |
| `decimal` | A number with decimals (`double`). |
| `boolean` | `true` or `false`. |
| `color` | A color, `#AARRGGBB`. |
| `list` | A JSON list. |
| `map` | A JSON object. |
| `image` | An image URL. |
| `choice` | One of `Variable.options`, stored as the option's value. |

<a id="state-expressions"></a>
### Expressions

`${name}` or `${path}` reads a value: `${count}`, `${user.name}`, `${items[0].price}`, `${pal[item.kind]}`.
`${= formula}` computes one: arithmetic (`+ - * / %`), comparisons (`== != < <= > >=`), `&&`, `||`, `!`,
`cond ? a : b`, literals (`'text'`, `3.5`, `true`, `null`, lists `[1, 2]`), and lambdas for list functions
(`x => x.price`). A text that is exactly one expression gives its value with its type; inside other text a number is
printed without trailing zeros. Names an expression may start with, besides the variables: `data`, `route`, `storage`, `screen`, `theme`, `item`, `index`, `parent`, `result`, `loop`, `auth`, `drag`, `perf`, `track`, `dismiss`, `pan`, `transform`, `flip`, `tilt`, `view`, `sticky`, `script`, `speech`, `pageOffset`.

<a id="state-binding-paths"></a>
### Binding paths

What each path of `bind` expects. A formula gives the value as the field is written in JSON: a number, `true` /
`false`, a name for an enum, a list or an object for the fields written that way. A value of another shape is not
read and the field keeps its value. Values are read loosely: `"12"` is a number, `1` and `"true"` are true.

| Path | Type | A formula gives |
|---|---|---|
| `visible` | `bool` | `true` or `false` |
| `opacity` | `double` | a number |
| `selected` | `bool` | `true` or `false` |
| `disabled` | `bool` | `true` or `false` |
| `data` | `List` | a list |
| `layout.width` | `AxisSize` | a number (fixed) or {"fill"\|"flexible"\|"hug"\|"fixed": number} |
| `layout.height` | `AxisSize` | a number (fixed) or {"fill"\|"flexible"\|"hug"\|"fixed": number} |
| `layout.constraints` | `BoxConstraints` | {"minWidth", "maxWidth", "minHeight", "maxHeight"} (each optional, numbers >= 0) |
| `layout.margin` | `EdgeInsets` | a number (all sides) or [left, top, right, bottom] |
| `layout.padding` | `EdgeInsets` | a number (all sides) or [left, top, right, bottom] |
| `layout.aspectRatio` | `double` | a number |
| `layout.flex` | `int` | a whole number |
| `layout.squeezable` | `bool` | `true` or `false` |
| `layout.x` | `AxisPosition` | a number (distance from the start) or {"start": d}, {"end": d}, {"start": a, "end": b}, {"align": -1..1}, {"relative": d} |
| `layout.y` | `AxisPosition` | a number (distance from the start) or {"start": d}, {"end": d}, {"start": a, "end": b}, {"align": -1..1}, {"relative": d} |
| `layout.align` | `Alignment` | [x, y] from -1 to 1, or a name: topLeft, topCenter, topRight, centerLeft, center, centerRight, bottomLeft, bottomCenter, bottomRight |
| `layout.order` | `int` | a whole number |
| `layout.basis` | `double` | a number |
| `decoration.fills` | `List<Paint>` | a list of Paint objects |
| `decoration.strokes` | `List<Paint>` | a list of Paint objects |
| `decoration.strokeWidth` | `double` | a number |
| `decoration.strokeAlign` | `StrokeAlign` | one of its names ([StrokeAlign](#enum-StrokeAlign)) |
| `decoration.strokeSides` | `StrokeSides` | one of its names ([StrokeSides](#enum-StrokeSides)) |
| `decoration.strokeCap` | `StrokeCap` | one of its names ([StrokeCap](#enum-StrokeCap)) |
| `decoration.dashPattern` | `List<double>` | a list of double objects |
| `decoration.radius` | `BorderRadius` | a number (every corner), [x, y] (every corner elliptical) or [topLeft, topRight, bottomRight, bottomLeft] (each a number or [x, y]) |
| `decoration.effects` | `List<Effect>` | a list of Effect objects |
| `decoration.clip` | `Clip` | one of its names ([Clip](#enum-Clip)) |
| `decoration.blendMode` | `BlendMode` | one of its names ([BlendMode](#enum-BlendMode)) |
| `decoration.foregroundFills` | `List<Paint>` | a list of Paint objects |
| `decoration.shape` | `DecorationShape` | one of its names ([DecorationShape](#enum-DecorationShape)) |

`props.<prop>` takes what the prop's type is written as: `"${= open ? 'vertical' : 'horizontal'}"` for
`props.direction`, a TextStyle object or a theme style's name for `props.style`. Every bindable field:

- `layout.<field>`: `width`, `height`, `constraints`, `margin`, `padding`, `aspectRatio`, `flex`, `squeezable`, `x`, `y`, `align`, `order`, `basis`, and `widthFactor`, `heightFactor`.
- `decoration.<field>`: `fills`, `strokes`, `strokeWidth`, `strokeAlign`, `strokeSides`, `strokeCap`, `dashPattern`, `radius`, `effects`, `clip`, `blendMode`, `foregroundFills`, `shape`. Inside `fills`, `strokes`, `foregroundFills` and `effects`, select an item by `[index]`, by its `id`, or every item by `*`, then a field of [Paint](#type-Paint) or [Effect](#type-Effect) (`decoration.fills[0].color`, `decoration.effects.*.color`, `.offset.dx`).
- `props.<prop>`: any prop of the node's type, and `props.<prop>.<field>` for a field of a model prop.
- `<behavior>` and `<behavior>.<field>`: [`motion`](#behavior-motion), [`animations`](#behavior-animations), [`transitions`](#behavior-transitions), [`shimmer`](#behavior-shimmer), [`inkWell`](#behavior-inkWell), [`states`](#behavior-states), [`tooltip`](#behavior-tooltip), [`ignorePointer`](#behavior-ignorePointer), [`floating`](#behavior-floating), [`hero`](#behavior-hero), [`draggable`](#behavior-draggable), [`dropTarget`](#behavior-dropTarget), [`track`](#behavior-track), [`dismissible`](#behavior-dismissible), [`pan`](#behavior-pan), [`reorderHandle`](#behavior-reorderHandle), [`reveal`](#behavior-reveal), [`typewriter`](#behavior-typewriter), [`particles`](#behavior-particles), [`textDirection`](#behavior-textDirection), [`defaultTextStyle`](#behavior-defaultTextStyle), [`flip`](#behavior-flip), [`tilt`](#behavior-tilt), [`transformGesture`](#behavior-transformGesture), [`sticky`](#behavior-sticky), [`viewProgress`](#behavior-viewProgress), [`measure`](#behavior-measure), [`customPaint`](#behavior-customPaint).

Named paths:

| Path | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `visible` |  |
| `opacity` |  |
| `selected` | Interaction states driven by data: true puts the node in `WidgetState.selected` / `WidgetState.disabled`, so its state styles (`states.selected`, `states.disabled`) patch it and its descendants, as hover and press do (`"selected": "${= item.id == selectedId}"`). |
| `disabled` |  |
| `data` | The items a repeating widget (list, grid, page view) builds one per. |
| `layout.width` |  |
| `layout.height` |  |
| `layout.flex` |  |
| `layout.margin` |  |
| `layout.padding` |  |
| `layout.x` |  |
| `layout.y` |  |
| `decoration.radius` |  |
| `decoration.strokeWidth` |  |
| `textDirection` |  |

<a id="state-conditions"></a>
### Conditions

An if / else-if / else rule. Its first branch whose test holds and that sets a property gives the property its value; when none does, the property keeps its binding's or its own value. JSON:

```json
{"id": "c1", "name": "Low stock", "branches": [
  {"when": {"left": "${stock}", "op": "lessThan", "right": "5"},
   "set": [{"node": "badge", "path": "visible", "value": true}]},
  {"set": [{"node": "badge", "path": "visible", "value": false}]}]}

```

- Branch: One branch: when `when` holds (always, for an `else`: null), the properties in `sets` take their values.
- Set entry: Sets property `path` (a binding path, DESIGN.md §5.1) of node `node` to `value`: a JSON value, where a string is an expression read like a binding's (`${= qty * 2}`, `#FF0000`, `Hello ${name}`).
- Comparison: `left op right` (the right side only for ops that `ConditionOp.takesRight`).
- Junction: All of `parts` (`and`) or any of them (`or`). Every part is evaluated. JSON: `{"and": [...]}` / `{"or": [...]}`.
- Operand: One side of a `Comparison`: an expression text whose `${...}` are read (`${count}`, `${= a + b}`, `3`, `done`), or, when `raw`, a literal taken as written. Both are then parsed loosely (`3` is a number, `true` a bool, `[1, 2]` a list). JSON: the text, or `{"raw": text}`.

| op | Reads right | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `equalsTo` | yes |  |
| `notEqualsTo` | yes |  |
| `greaterThan` | yes |  |
| `lessThan` | yes |  |
| `greaterThanOrEqualTo` | yes |  |
| `lessThanOrEqualTo` | yes |  |
| `isEmpty` | no | Null, or an empty text, list or map. |
| `isNotEmpty` | no |  |
| `contains` | yes | A list holds the right operand, a text contains it, a map has it as a key. |
| `isOdd` | no |  |
| `isEven` | no |  |
| `isNull` | no | Null, or the text `null`. |
| `isTrue` | no |  |
| `isFalse` | no |  |

<a id="state-scripts"></a>
### Scripts

A document's sandboxed JavaScript (`scripts`), run by `runScript` or called from a formula (`script.name(...)`).

| Key | Type | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | String | `""` |  |  |
| `name` | String | `""` |  | A JavaScript identifier: script.<name>(...). |
| `description` | String | `""` |  |  |
| `params` | Object | unset |  | [{"name", "description", "defaultValue"}]. |
| `source` | String | `""` |  | JavaScript. |
| `version` | int | `1` |  | Goes up each time the script is saved. |
| `capabilities` | List<String> | `[]` |  | What it may do: variables.read, variables.write, nodes.read, navigation, api, cloud, actions, clock. |
| `timeoutMs` | int | `1000` | ≥ 1 |  |
| `memoryLimitMb` | int | `32` | ≥ 1 | Enforced on devices; on the web only `timeoutMs` applies. |
| `pageId` | String | unset |  | Null: a project script. |
| `tests` | Object | unset |  | Sample runs: [{"name", "args", "vars", "nodes", "expect", "expectError"}]. |

<a id="state-formula-functions"></a>
### Formula functions

The functions a formula (`${= ...}`) can call, from the SDK's formula engine, grouped.

<a id="state-text"></a>
#### Text

| Function | Signature | Example |
|---|---|---|
| <a id="fn-left"></a>`left` | `left(text, count)` | `left("MX4821", 2) → MX` |
| <a id="fn-right"></a>`right` | `right(text, count)` | `right("1FUJGLDR5MX4821", 6) → MX4821` |
| <a id="fn-upper"></a>`upper` | `upper(text)` | `upper("hi") → HI` |
| <a id="fn-lower"></a>`lower` | `lower(text)` | `lower("Hi") → hi` |
| <a id="fn-trim"></a>`trim` | `trim(text)` | `trim("  hi ") → hi` |
| <a id="fn-contains"></a>`contains` | `contains(text or list, value)` | `contains(lower(title), lower(search)) → true` |
| <a id="fn-startsWith"></a>`startsWith` | `startsWith(text, prefix)` | `startsWith("Buy milk", "Buy") → true` |
| <a id="fn-endsWith"></a>`endsWith` | `endsWith(text, suffix)` | `endsWith("photo.png", ".png") → true` |
| <a id="fn-padLeft"></a>`padLeft` | `padLeft(value, width, char)` | `padLeft(4, 2) → 04 (numbers pad with 0, text with spaces)` |
| `padLeft` | `padLeft(text, width, char?)` | `padLeft(42, 5, "0") → 00042` |
| <a id="fn-padRight"></a>`padRight` | `padRight(value, width, char)` | `padRight("A", 3, ".") → A..` |
| `padRight` | `padRight(text, width, char?)` | `padRight("ab", 4, ".") → ab..` |
| <a id="fn-substring"></a>`substring` | `substring(text, start, end)` | `substring("Vinyl", 0, 3) → Vin` |
| `substring` | `substring(text, start, end?)` | `substring("EX-102", 3) → 102` |
| <a id="fn-replace"></a>`replace` | `replace(text, from, to)` | `replace("a-b-c", "-", " ") → a b c` |
| `replace` | `replace(text, from, to)` | `replace("1,402", ",", "") → 1402` |
| <a id="fn-regexReplace"></a>`regexReplace` | `regexReplace(text, pattern, to)` | `regexReplace("WILLOW PHARMACY 044", " [0-9]+$", "") → WILLOW PHARMACY; \$1 in to inserts a group` |
| <a id="fn-titleCase"></a>`titleCase` | `titleCase(text)` | `titleCase("SQ *KESTREL FLOWERS") → Sq *Kestrel Flowers` |
| <a id="fn-split"></a>`split` | `split(text, separator)` | `split("rock, jazz", ", ") → [rock, jazz]` |
| `split` | `split(text, separator?)` | `split("2481") → [2, 4, 8, 1]` |
| <a id="fn-matches"></a>`matches` | `matches(text, pattern)` | `matches(code, "^\d{4}$") → true` |
| <a id="fn-slug"></a>`slug` | `slug(text)` | `slug("Kind of Blue!") → kind-of-blue` |
| <a id="fn-charCode"></a>`charCode` | `charCode(text, index)` | `charCode("MX", 1) → 88` |
| <a id="fn-fromCharCode"></a>`fromCharCode` | `fromCharCode(code, …) or fromCharCode(list)` | `fromCharCode(65 + seat) → B` |
| <a id="fn-codeUnits"></a>`codeUnits` | `codeUnits(text)` | `sum(codeUnits(tag)) % 8 → a stable color index for tag` |
| <a id="fn-join"></a>`join` | `join(list, separator, field or item => value)` | `join(tags, " · ")` |
| <a id="fn-pad"></a>`pad` | `pad(value, width, fill)` | `pad(5, 2) → 05` |
| <a id="fn-text"></a>`text` | `text(value)` | `text(42) → "42"` |
