<a id="page-edit-ops"></a>
# Edit ops and streaming

<a id="edit-ops-when-to-use"></a>
## When to use

Building and changing a document with edit operations: what a model sends in a `ui_apply` tool call, what an app's
`UiSession` applies while the model streams, the retry protocol for rejected ops, the tools' schemas and the trust
profiles that limit what a model may use.

<a id="edit-ops-minimal-example"></a>
## Minimal example

The ops that build the base's smallest document, top-down, as a model streams them:

```json
{
  "ops": [
    {"op": "roots", "roots": ["home"]},
    {
      "op": "set",
      "id": "home",
      "node": {
        "type": "canvas",
        "name": "Home",
        "slots": {"body": "page"},
        "layout": {"width": 390, "height": 844},
        "decoration": {"fills": [{"color": "#FFFFFFFF"}]}
      }
    },
    {
      "op": "set",
      "id": "page",
      "node": {
        "type": "column",
        "children": ["title", "body"],
        "layout": {"width": {"fill": 390}, "height": {"fill": 844}, "padding": 24},
        "props": {"crossAxisAlignment": "start", "spacing": 12}
      }
    },
    {
      "op": "set",
      "id": "title",
      "node": {
        "type": "text",
        "layout": {"width": {"fill": 342}, "height": {"hug": 34}},
        "props": {"text": "Hello", "style": {"fontWeight": 700, "fontSize": 28, "color": "#FF111827"}}
      }
    },
    {
      "op": "set",
      "id": "body",
      "node": {
        "type": "text",
        "layout": {"width": {"fill": 342}, "height": {"hug": 40}},
        "props": {
          "text": "A column with two texts, filling the screen's width.",
          "style": {"fontSize": 15, "color": "#FF4B5563", "height": 1.4}
        }
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

<a id="edit-ops-reference"></a>
## Reference

<a id="edit-ops-the-ops"></a>
### The ops

A document is built and changed with six **edit operations**, each addressed by node id: what an agent sends in a
`ui_apply` tool call, what `codelessly apply` takes, and what an app's `UiSession` applies while a model streams
(`applyOps`, `decodeOps`, `OpStreamDecoder` in `package:codelessly_api/core.dart`). Generation is just the first
batch of ops; every change after it is a few more.

| Op | Fields | Means | Example |
|---|---|---|---|
| `set` | `id`, `node`, `nodes`, `parent`, `index`, `slot`, `placeholders` | Create node `id` (or replace it: the result says which), optionally placed under `parent` at `index` (default: last) or in `slot`. `node` is the node as the document holds it under "nodes": its `children` may list ids that arrive in later ops (pending until then). `nodes` sets several nodes at once (id → node), in order. `placeholders` gives a size (a layout fragment) to show for a pending child until it arrives. | `{"op":"set","id":"faqTitle","parent":"faqSec","index":0,"node":{"type":"text","layout":{"width":{"hug":120},"height":{"hug":28}},"props":{"text":"Questions","style":{"fontSize":22,"fontWeight":700,"color":"#FF111827"}}}}` |
| `patch` | `id` (required), `patch` (required) | Merge `patch` into node `id` (RFC 7396): objects merge, arrays and scalars replace, null deletes a key. Shaped like the node (`{"props": {"text": "Book a demo"}}`). It cannot change `children`, `slots` or `type`. | `{"op":"patch","id":"heroTitle","patch":{"props":{"text":"Book a demo","style":{"color":"#FF0F766E"}}}}` |
| `move` | `id` (required), `parent` (required), `index`, `slot` | Move node `id` (with its subtree) under `parent` at `index` (default: last), or into `slot`. Reorder: move within the same parent. | `{"op":"move","id":"faqSec","parent":"page","index":2}` |
| `remove` | `ids` (required) | Remove the nodes `ids` and everything under them; their parents stop listing them. | `{"op":"remove","ids":["promoBanner"]}` |
| `vars` | `scope` (required), `set`, `remove` | Variables of `scope` (a canvas id, or "page_variables"): `set` maps a name to its new value, or to a full variable object (`{"type": "boolean", "value": false}`) to declare it; `remove` lists names to remove. Bindings that read them update at once. | `{"op":"vars","scope":"pricing","set":{"annual":true}}` |
| `roots` | `roots` (required) | Set the document's canvases, in order. A root may name a canvas that arrives in a later op. | `{"op":"roots","roots":["home"]}` |
| `scripts` | `set`, `remove` | The document's scripts (sandboxed JavaScript, where allowed): `set` maps a name to {"source", "params", "capabilities", "timeoutMs"}; `remove` lists names. A reaction runs one ({"type": "runScript", "script": name}), a formula calls it (script.name(...)). | `{"op":"scripts","set":{"clamp":{"params":["v"],"source":"return Math.max(0, Math.min(9, v));"}}}` |

<a id="edit-ops-codes-of-the-edit-layer"></a>
### Codes of the edit layer

| Code | Rejects the op | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `invalid_op` | yes | An op that is not an object, or names no known "op" (set, patch, move, remove, vars, roots, scripts). |
| `missing_field` | yes | An op without a field it needs ("id", "node", "patch", "parent", "ids", "scope", "roots"). |
| `wrong_type` | yes | A field of an op with the wrong JSON type (an id that is not text, a node that is not an object). |
| `unknown_id` | yes | A patch, move or remove of a node the document does not have, or a set or move under a parent it does not have. |
| `structural_key_in_patch` | yes | A patch that changes "children" or "slots" (or "type"): child lists change only through set, move and remove; a type through set. |
| `stale_rev` | yes | The op changes a field another author changed after the batch's "baseRev": re-read the node (ui_read) and decide. |
| `would_orphan` | yes | A set that replaces a node and drops children it had: they would be left under no parent. Keep them in "children", move or remove them first, or use patch. |
| `multiple_parents` | yes | The op would list a node under a second parent (or twice in one): a node has one parent. Use move to change its parent. |
| `cycle` | yes | The op would put a node inside its own subtree. |
| `canvas_as_child` | yes | The op would place a canvas under a parent: canvases are only roots. |
| `invalid_parent` | yes | A set or move under a parent that takes no children there: a type without children, or a slot the type does not have. |
| `dangling_child` | yes | At the end of the stream, a child or slot id that names no node (it was pending and never arrived). |
| `unreachable_node` | no (a warning) | At the end of the stream, a node no root reaches (nothing lists it as a child or slot). |
| `pending_child` | no (a warning) | A child or slot id the op lists that has not arrived yet: accepted while streaming, an error (dangling_child) if it never comes. |
| `capability_not_allowed` | yes | The op uses a node type, action, script, link, image host or navigation target the session's trust profile does not allow. |
| `limit_exceeded` | yes | The op would exceed a limit of the trust profile (nodes, depth, text length, ops per call). |
| `truncated_op` | yes | The stream ended inside an op: what arrived of it was not applied. |
| `invalid_json` | yes | The tool input is not JSON where an op was expected. |
| `invalid_variable` | yes | A vars op that declares a variable without a name, or sets one with a value its type cannot hold. |
| `unknown_variable` | no (a warning) | A vars op that sets (or removes) a variable the scope does not declare: declare it with a full variable object. |
| `malformed_input` | no (a warning) | The tool input's JSON was not well formed at a character offset (a stray or missing brace or bracket, a trailing or missing comma, an op that began before the previous one closed): the decoder repaired it and read the ops around it. Write balanced JSON: one closing brace per opening brace. |
| `misplaced_field` | no (a warning) | A node field ("bind", "props", "actions"...) written on a set op instead of inside its "node": it was moved into the node. |
| `start_over` | yes | A batch that rebuilds a UI that already exists (new roots, a new canvas) instead of patching it: fix the existing document with patch, set (same ids) and remove; never start over. |
| `empty_button` | no (a warning) | A node that reacts to a tap but shows nothing (a box, row or column with no children): a button with no label. |
| `low_contrast` | no (a warning) | Text drawn in (nearly) the colour of the fill behind it, or with no colour (the default near-black) over a dark fill. |
| `missing_glyph` | no (a warning) | Text with characters the loaded fonts do not have (an arrow, a symbol): they draw as empty boxes. Use an icon node. Reported by a renderer that knows its fonts. |
| `no_size` | no (a warning) | A node that has content but was laid out with no width or no height, so nothing of it shows. Reported by a renderer. |
| `invalid_script` | yes | A scripts op whose script cannot be stored: a name or parameter that is not a JavaScript identifier, no source, limits out of range. |

<a id="edit-ops-the-tools"></a>
### The tools

`outline(document)` is one row per node, `[id, type, label, depth, {what is bound, states, triggers}]`, a sixth to
a seventh of the document's size (the two m05 pages: 6.7 KB for 147 nodes against 47.6 KB, 8.3 KB for 196 nodes
against 55.4 KB). `readUi` answers the `ui_read` tool: the outline, or whole nodes by id.

The two tools (`uiTools(catalog)`), their input schemas generated from the op declarations and the catalog's
node types (the agent profile over the core: [ui_tools.json](ui_tools.json)):

```json
[
  {
    "name": "ui_apply",
    "description": "Build or change the UI. The UI is one document: a flat map of nodes by id, each a Flutter-like widget (type, layout, decoration, props, children). Ops apply in order: set (create or replace a node, optionally placing it under a parent), patch (RFC 7396 merge patch on one node; null deletes a key), move, remove, vars (set or declare variables) and roots (the screens). Ids are the addresses: choose short readable ids. A node may list children that arrive in later ops. When building, write top-down: the roots op and the canvas first, then each container before its children, section by section, so the UI paints as it streams. To change an existing UI, send only the small ops the change needs (patch a prop instead of re-sending a node). The result lists the ops that were rejected with a code, a path and a suggestion: fix and resend only those.",
    "input_schema": "(see ui_tools.json)"
  },
  {
    "name": "ui_read",
    "description": "Read the current UI before changing it: the outline (one row per node: id, type, label, depth, what is bound), or full nodes by id. Read the outline first; ask for full nodes only for the ones you will change.",
    "input_schema": "(see ui_tools.json)"
  }
]
```

A schema that enumerates every node type and key is the wrong shape for a runtime tool: it costs tokens on every
call and still cannot say what a prop holds. `uiTools(catalog, compact: true)` gives the op envelope strictly (op
names, field names and kinds from the declarations; [ui_tools.compact.json](ui_tools.compact.json)) and leaves the
node's contents to the system prompt: the **base** in its runtime form, `runtimeStarter(catalog:, profile:, kind:)`
([RUNTIME_STARTER.md](RUNTIME_STARTER.md)). It is the same document as [STARTER.md](#page-base), assembled by
`baseDocument` from the same generated segments, with the runtime envelope (answering rules, the ops, two examples
that apply cleanly) in place of the file envelope (the render command, sites as files), and its tables restricted
to what the trust profile allows. `ui_read {"types": [...]}` describes any other allowed type on demand
(`describeTypes`), and validation does the rest.

The base ends with the index of the third tool, `ui_docs {"topic": ...}` (`uiTools(catalog, compact: true, docs:
true)`). `docsTopic` answers with these pages: a page's *When to use*, minimal example and pitfalls, and the list of
its sections; any section by its anchor (`ui_docs "forms-validation-and-an-error-state"`); any node type, action
type, trigger or behavior by name, generated from the declarations. A link `forms.md#x` in the files is
`ui_docs "x"` in the runtime form: the same map (`toRuntimeLinks`). The trust profile decides what may be *used*: a
topic outside it says it is not available here.

`TrustProfile.agentApps` is `agent` plus the document's own sandboxed scripts, for apps and games an agent builds:
the `scripts` op (name → `{"source", "params", "capabilities", "timeoutMs"}`, validated by `ScriptDef.validate()`,
`invalid_script`), `runScript` and `script.name(...)` in formulas, with capabilities limited to `variables.read`,
`variables.write` and `clock`. Everything else stays as `agent`'s.

<a id="edit-ops-the-trust-profile"></a>
### The trust profile

`TrustProfile` is what an edited document may use: node types and action types (a restricted catalog,
`profile.restrict(catalog)`), scripts, link and image hosts, navigation, and limits (nodes, depth, text length, ops
per call). `TrustProfile.agent`, the default for agent-written UI, allows the core's node types and its local
actions (variables, values, in-document navigation, modals, toasts, scrolling, animation, `componentEvent`): no
scripts, no links, no host functions, no feature library's types. A violation is `capability_not_allowed` or
`limit_exceeded`, with the op and the path.

`componentEvent` in a document that is not a component (an agent's UI) is the event to the document's host: the
session delivers it to the app, which sends it to the model.



<a id="edit-ops-patterns"></a>
## Patterns

<a id="edit-ops-a-follow-up-edit"></a>
### A follow-up edit

Then a follow-up instruction ("add a button under the title, drop the body text, make the title say Welcome") is
a few ops, not a new document:

```json
{"ops": [
  {"op": "set", "id": "cta", "parent": "page", "index": 1,
   "node": {"type": "row", "children": ["ctaText"], "layout": {"width": {"hug": 140}, "height": 44, "padding": [16, 0, 16, 0]},
            "decoration": {"fills": [{"color": "#FF2563EB"}], "radius": 10}}},
  {"op": "set", "id": "ctaText", "node": {"type": "text", "layout": {"width": {"hug": 100}, "height": {"hug": 20}},
            "props": {"text": "Get started", "style": {"fontSize": 15, "fontWeight": 600, "color": "#FFFFFFFF"}}}},
  {"op": "remove", "ids": ["body"]},
  {"op": "patch", "id": "title", "patch": {"props": {"text": "Welcome"}}},
  {"op": "vars", "scope": "home", "set": {"taps": {"type": "integer", "value": 0}}},
  {"op": "patch", "id": "cta", "patch": {"actions": [{"trigger": {"type": "click"},
            "actions": [{"type": "setVariable", "variable": "taps", "op": "add", "value": 1}]}]}},
  {"op": "move", "id": "cta", "parent": "page", "index": 0}
]}
```

A batch with a mistake: the second op misspells `fills`. It is rejected with a code, the path and a suggestion; the
first applies:

```json
{
  "ops": [
    {"op": "patch", "id": "title", "patch": {"props": {"text": "Welcome back"}}},
    {"op": "patch", "id": "title", "patch": {"decoration": {"fill": [{"color": "#FFF1F5F9"}]}}}
  ]
}
```

The result (`EditResult.toModelJson()`, the tool result):

```json
{
  "rev": 1,
  "applied": [0],
  "ids": {"patched": ["title"]},
  "rejected": [
    {
      "op": 1,
      "code": "unknown_decoration_key",
      "path": "/nodes/title/decoration/fill",
      "message": "decoration has no \"fill\": a fill is a list of paints: \"decoration\": {\"fills\": [{\"color\": \"#FF2563EB\"}]}.",
      "nodeId": "title",
      "expected": [
        "fills",
        "strokes",
        "strokeWidth",
        "strokeAlign",
        "strokeSides",
        "strokeCap",
        "dashPattern",
        "radius",
        "effects",
        "clip",
        "blendMode",
        "foregroundFills",
        "shape"
      ],
      "suggestion": "fills"
    }
  ],
  "warnings": [],
  "document": {"roots": ["home"], "nodes": 4},
  "next": "The UI exists as described (rev 1): fix it by patching it, in one ui_apply call. Resend only the rejected ops, corrected, with the same ids; patch fields of nodes that exist. Never start over: no new roots, no new canvas, no re-sending nodes that applied."
}
```

<a id="edit-ops-streaming"></a>
### Streaming

LLM APIs deliver a tool call's input as text deltas cut anywhere. `OpStreamDecoder` yields each op the moment its
closing brace arrives (inside a `set` with `nodes`, each node as its own brace closes), whatever the cuts; a stream
cut mid-op keeps every complete op and reports the tail (`truncated_op`).

**Malformed input.** With eager (fine-grained) tool input streaming a provider does not promise valid JSON, and
models do not always write it: a recorded live generation closed one brace too many three times in 24 ops. The
decoder works around op boundaries, not the enclosing JSON: it keeps a repaired copy of the text (a closer that
closes nothing is dropped, a missing one is inferred, trailing commas are removed, missing commas inserted), reads an
op object (`{"op": ...}`) at any depth outside another op (after an `ops` array closed early, in a wrapper of
another name, after text), and when an op begins before the previous one closed, closes that one where the next
began and reads what it can of it. Each repair is one `malformed_input` warning with the character offset; the ops
around it apply. A node field written beside `"node"` (what an early closing brace produces) is moved into the node
(`misplaced_field`). A single stray or missing brace, bracket or comma loses at most the op it is in
(`test/edit_stream_recovery_test.dart` checks this property on 2,000 random edits, and that every chunking yields the
same ops). `OpStreamEnd.repairs` and `.recovered` count the repairs and the ops read after the first one.

While a document streams in, it is incomplete by nature:

* **Order.** Root first, then top-down: the `roots` op, the canvas, its container, then each section complete before
  the next. Nothing breaks if a model does otherwise.
* **Forward references.** A child id listed before its node arrives is **pending**, not an error; a reference to a
  node, screen or variable that has not arrived yet (a state that patches it, a navigation to it) is a warning while
  the stream runs (`applyOps(..., incomplete: true)`). When the stream ends, `endOfStream` reports every id still
  dangling (`dangling_child`), so the model can send it.
* **Rendering** (the SDK's `UiSession`): nothing paints until a root canvas has content; a pending child takes no
  room (or the size a `set`'s `placeholders` gave it); a container none of whose children has arrived waits for
  its first, so no empty shells flash; text and values are never shown half-written (an op applies only whole).

<a id="edit-ops-the-retry-protocol"></a>
### The retry protocol

After a stream, the tool result (`EditResult.toModelJson()`) says exactly what the document holds and what to do:
`rev`, the ops that applied (by index, and the ids they set, patched, moved and removed), every rejected op with its
code, path, what was expected and a suggestion, warnings (at most 20), the pending ids, the document's roots and node
count, and, when anything was rejected or is pending, `next`: fix it by patching the document as it is (same ids),
never start over. A host sends it back and lets the model answer with one more `ui_apply`, a capped number of
times (the chat example: 2), stopping when nothing is rejected or pending. `applyOps(..., protectRoots: true)`
answers a batch that would replace the existing roots or create a new canvas with `start_over` (a live retry did
exactly that instead of fixing three ops). The diagnostics models hit carry the fix as JSON (`explainDiagnostic`): a
size written as a layout key (`"height": {"hug": 46}`), children on a type that takes none (the types that do, and a
row with a fill for a tag or button), a button's `text` (its `label`). `uiLints(document)` adds what no declaration
catches: `empty_button` (a tappable box that shows nothing) and `low_contrast` (text in its background's colour); a
renderer adds `missing_glyph` and `no_size` (the SDK's `UiSession.renderDiagnostics`).

<a id="edit-ops-pitfalls"></a>
## Pitfalls

* A `patch` is an RFC 7396 merge patch on one node, shaped like the node: objects merge, lists and values replace,
  `null` deletes a key. It never changes `children`, `slots` or `type` (`structural_key_in_patch`): child lists
  change only through `set` (with `parent`), `move` and `remove`.
* A `set` of an id that exists replaces the node (the result says which ids it created). Replacing a node that had
  children it no longer lists is `would_orphan`: keep them, move or remove them first, or patch instead.
* Each op is checked on its own, against what it touched: its structure (one parent, no cycle, no canvas as a child,
  a parent that takes children there), the trust profile, and the nodes' fields (the strict validator of
  [render](#page-render) on the nodes the op created or changed, their parents and children). A rejected op changes nothing; the others
  apply (with `"atomic": true`, all or none).
* A batch may carry `"baseRev"`, the revision the author read: a patch of a field, or a set of a node, that another
  author changed since is `stale_rev`, with the current value. Every applied batch has inverse ops: applied
  atomically, they restore the document (undo).

<a id="page-render"></a>
# The render command: checking your work

<a id="render-when-to-use"></a>
## When to use

Checking a document or a site before trusting it: strict validation, screenshots at each size, the states after
taps, typing and scrolling, and a diagnostic for every problem with a code, a JSON pointer and what to do. The
command lives in the SDK repository (`tool/render/render.sh`; its README has every option).

<a id="render-minimal-example"></a>
## Minimal example

The smallest document, and the command that checks it at three sizes:

```json
{
  "schema": 3,
  "roots": ["home"],
  "nodes": {
    "home": {
      "type": "canvas",
      "name": "Home",
      "slots": {"body": "page"},
      "layout": {"width": 390, "height": 844},
      "decoration": {"fills": [{"color": "#FFFFFFFF"}]}
    },
    "page": {
      "type": "column",
      "children": ["title", "body"],
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 390}, "height": {"fill": 844}, "padding": 24},
      "props": {"crossAxisAlignment": "start", "spacing": 12}
    },
    "title": {
      "type": "text",
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 342}, "height": {"hug": 34}},
      "props": {"text": "Hello", "style": {"fontSize": 28, "fontWeight": 700, "color": "#FF111827"}}
    },
    "body": {
      "type": "text",
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 342}, "height": {"hug": 40}},
      "props": {
        "text": "A column with two texts, filling the screen's width.",
        "style": {"fontSize": 15, "height": 1.4, "color": "#FF4B5563"}
      }
    }
  }
}
```

```sh
tool/render/render.sh home.json --out shots/ --sizes 390x844,834x1112,1440x900 --full-page
```

<a id="render-reference"></a>
## Reference

<a id="render-what-it-does"></a>
### What it does

Decoding is lenient: a misspelled key, a value of the wrong shape or an unknown enum value is silently ignored or
replaced by its default. Never trust a document that has not been checked. The command validates every document
strictly, renders each screen with the SDK at each size, writes `shots/<screen>@<w>x<h>.png` and
`shots/diagnostics.json`, and prints one line per problem with a code, the JSON pointer of the value
(`/nodes/hero-title/props/style/fontSize`) or the node, and what to do. It exits 1 when there are errors.

<a id="render-steps-before-the-capture"></a>
### Steps before the capture

In order: `--tap <id>` (`<id>#<n>` for the n-th copy of a list item; a node out of view or under an overlay is
scrolled to the middle first, and a tap that would land on another node is reported, not made), `--hover <id>`,
`--focus <id>`, `--unfocus`, `--type <id>=<text>`, `--key <key>`, `--set <variable>=<json>`, `--scroll <id or
screen>=<px>`, `--drag <id>=<dx>,<dy>` (or `=<other id>`: onto a node), `--navigate <screen>`, `--wait <ms>`. A step
may name a node by its `name` too. In a site, steps name nodes inside components by path (`--tap plans/card1/cta`)
and a node in a list's copy as `<template>#<n>/<node>` (`evCard#0/evReserve`, the same as `evReserve#0`). Ids are
per document, so a page, a component and an open modal may share one: a step naming an id two shown nodes have is
an error listing how to name each (`page/saved`, the page's own under its canvas id; `footer/saved`, the
component's). A step on a node hidden at one size (a media rule, another breakpoint's canvas) is skipped there with
a note; the others run. `--navigate` takes a canvas id, a screen name or a URL path, with a query string for the
params the screen reads as `${route.<name>}` (`--navigate speaker?id=ada`, `--navigate /project?id=7`); later steps
act on the screen navigated to. A `--set` holds: a timer or `load` reaction that writes the variable afterwards does
not change the capture (`set_overwritten` says it happened); `--now <ISO time>` pins `now()`. A tap, a drag or a
navigation first unfocuses a focused text field elsewhere, as a click outside it does. `--label <name>` keeps the screenshots and
`diagnostics-<name>.json` of each state apart. After each step the page settles before the next one and the capture
(about a second): an animation shorter than that is over when the screenshot is taken; to see one mid-flight,
lengthen its duration in a copy. `--key` presses a key for the screen's `keyDown` reactions; it does not submit a
focused text field (test `submitted` chains through a button). In nested lists `#n` counts the copies across the
whole repeat, outer item by outer item, from 0: with a 7-day grid per habit, `day#9` is the second habit's third
day. `--full-page` captures the whole page from its top, its own scroll
height, as a reader sees it: content fixed to the window and an open modal (with its dimmed backdrop) in the first
window, a sticky node once in its place, and after a navigation the page navigated to at its own height; without it
the capture is the window where the steps left the page. `--theme light|dark` starts the site in that theme mode
(PNG names end `-light`, `-dark`; a `--tap` on a `setThemeMode` switch then changes it). A site's declared fonts
(`site.json`'s `fonts`) and images named by a path relative to the site are read from its folder with no flag;
`--fonts <dir>` adds other font files (`--fonts system`: the system's). `--component <Type>` and
`--components-all` render components alone.

<a id="render-validation-codes"></a>
### Validation codes

From `package:codelessly_api/validate.dart`:

| Code | Severity | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `invalid_document` | error | The document is not a JSON object, or a top-level key has the wrong shape (nodes not an object, roots not a list). |
| `schema_version` | warning | The document has no "schema", or one this package does not read (it reads 2 and 3, and writes 3). |
| `schema_outdated` | info | A schema-2 document: it loads, migrated to schema 3 in memory (`migrate2to3`; `dart run tool/migrate.dart` rewrites the file). The other diagnostics are of the migrated document. |
| `legacy_value` | warning | A `legacy.<name>` key the migration kept: a value that had no current form and is no longer read. |
| `unknown_document_key` | error | A top-level key of the document that nothing reads. |
| `dangling_root` | error | A root id that names no node. |
| `root_not_canvas` | warning | A root that is not a canvas: it is never shown as a screen. |
| `no_roots` | error | The document has no roots, so nothing is shown. |
| `invalid_node` | error | A node that is not an object or has no "type": decoding drops it. |
| `unknown_node_type` | error | A node type no declaration knows: it renders as an empty box. |
| `unknown_node_key` | error | A key on a node that is neither a node field nor a behavior: it is kept but does nothing. |
| `unknown_prop` | error | A key in "props" that the node type does not declare: it does nothing. |
| `unknown_layout_key` | error | A key in "layout" that layout does not read. |
| `unknown_decoration_key` | error | A key in "decoration" that decoration does not read. |
| `unknown_field` | error | A key inside a value (a paint, a text style, a behavior model...) that its type does not read. |
| `wrong_type` | error | A value of the wrong JSON type or shape: decoding ignores it and uses the default. |
| `loose_value` | warning | A value of another JSON type that decoding converts (the text "12" for a number): write the type itself. |
| `invalid_enum` | error | A value that is not one of the allowed names: decoding uses the default. |
| `out_of_range` | error | A number outside its declared bounds: decoding clamps it. |
| `decoration_ignored` | warning | Fills, strokes, radius or shadows on a type without a box decoration: only blur effects are kept. |
| `dangling_child` | error | A child id that names no node. |
| `dangling_slot` | error | A slot whose id names no node. |
| `multiple_parents` | error | A node listed as a child (or slot) of more than one parent, or twice in one parent. |
| `cycle` | error | A node that contains itself. |
| `unreachable_node` | warning | A node no root reaches: it is never shown. |
| `unknown_slot` | error | A slot name the node type does not have. |
| `children_not_allowed` | error | A "children" list on a type that takes none (or takes slots only): they are never shown. |
| `slots_not_allowed` | error | A "slots" map on a type that has no slots. |
| `canvas_as_child` | error | A canvas used as the child of another node: canvases are screens, only roots. |
| `layout_field_ignored` | warning | A layout field the node's parent does not read (x/y outside a stack, flex/align outside a row or column). |
| `fit_not_allowed` | warning | A width or height mode the parent cannot honor (fill along a scrolling axis, flexible outside a row/column). |
| `zero_size` | warning | A fixed width or height of 0 (often a missing "width"/"height"): the node is invisible. |
| `vertical_wrap` | warning | A wrapping list that scrolls vertically: its items flow top to bottom and wrap into columns, not side by side. |
| `layout_clamped` | warning | A layout value that cannot take effect as written: a negative offset in a stack that hugs its children (clamped to 0), or a negative margin (Flutter has none: the box shrinks). |
| `prop_ignored` | warning | A prop that has no effect with another the node sets (a grid's mainAxisExtent while shrinkWrapRows sizes its rows): one of them is ignored. |
| `unknown_bind_path` | error | A "bind" key that names no bindable field of the node. |
| `reserved_bind_path` | warning | A binding path that is kept but not applied yet. |
| `expression_syntax` | error | A "${" that is not closed, or an empty ${}. |
| `unknown_name` | error | An expression reads a name that is neither a declared variable nor a scope the runtime provides. |
| `unknown_trigger` | error | A reaction whose trigger type is unknown or missing: the reaction is dropped. |
| `unknown_trigger_key` | error | A key of a trigger that triggers do not read. |
| `unknown_action_type` | error | An action type no declaration knows: the runtime skips it. |
| `unknown_action_key` | error | A key of an action that its type does not read. |
| `unknown_target_node` | error | An action or condition names a node id that is not in the document. |
| `unknown_screen` | error | A navigate or openModal names a screen (canvas or layout id) that does not exist. |
| `unknown_variable` | error | An action or trigger names a variable that is not declared. |
| `invalid_reaction` | error | A reaction or action that is not an object, or an action list that is not a list. |
| `invalid_variable` | error | A variable without a name, with an unknown type, or whose value its type cannot hold. |
| `duplicate_variable` | error | Two variables of the same name in one scope. |
| `unknown_scope` | error | Variables or conditions keyed by an id that is not a canvas of the document (nor page_variables). |
| `invalid_condition` | error | A condition, branch, predicate or set entry of the wrong shape. |
| `unknown_breakpoint` | error | A canvas, variant or media rule names a breakpoint the project does not define. |
| `invalid_media` | error | A "media" rule of the wrong shape: no condition (minWidth, maxWidth, orientation), a width that is neither px nor a breakpoint name, a minWidth above its maxWidth, or a patch key that cannot vary by screen size. |
| `media_overridden` | warning | A media rule patches a field the node also binds: the binding wins, so the patch never shows. |
| `unknown_theme_name` | error | A color or text style names a color or text style the project's theme (the site manifest's "theme") does not have: it would show transparent or unstyled. |
| `invalid_theme` | error | The site manifest's "theme" is not of the right shape: colors are "#AARRGGBB" (or another color's name), text styles are TextStyle objects, media rules patch colors and textStyles. |
| `invalid_fonts` | error | The site manifest's "fonts" is not of the right shape: a list of {"family": "Inter", "fonts": [{"asset": "fonts/Inter-Regular.ttf", "weight": 400, "style": "normal"}]} (a pubspec's fonts: section). |
| `font_format` | error | A declared font file is not .ttf, .otf or .woff: WOFF2 (Brotli-compressed) and font collections (.ttc) are not read. Use the .woff or .ttf of the same face. |
| `duplicate_breakpoint_canvas` | error | Two canvases of one screen are the design for the same breakpoint. |
| `screen_without_breakpoint` | warning | A canvas grouped into a screen (props.screen) that names no breakpoint: it shows only below the narrowest. |
| `duplicate_id` | warning | The same canvas id in two documents of one project: navigate and openModal name a screen by its canvas id, so a link reaches one of them. Other node ids are per document and may repeat. |
| `unknown_component` | error | A call names a component type (UpperCamelCase) that no definition of the project declares: it renders as an empty box of its size. |
| `duplicate_component` | error | Two definitions declare the same component type, or a component type is also a catalog type: there is no shadowing. |
| `component_cycle` | error | A component calls itself, directly or through other components: it can never finish rendering. |
| `component_id_mismatch` | error | A component document whose file name (or "id") is not its widget type: a file holds the component it is named after. |
| `invalid_component` | error | A component document of the wrong shape: a "widget" without a type, a type that is not UpperCamelCase, or not exactly one root. |
| `missing_prop` | error | A call does not set a parameter the component declares as required. |
| `unknown_event` | error | An event reaction (or a componentEvent action) names an event the component does not declare, or sits on a node that is not a component call. |
| `call_field_not_allowed` | error | A field on a call that belongs to the definition (decoration, layout.padding): the call gives size and placement only. |
| `slot_outside_component` | warning | A slot node in a document that is not a component: nothing fills it, its own children show. |
| `root_placement_bound` | warning | A component root binds its size or placement: the call sizes and places the root, so the binding is dropped. |
| `repeated_subtree` | info | A subtree written several times over, node for node (ids and names aside): a component, or a list template, would write it once. |

<a id="render-render-codes"></a>
### Render codes

The render step adds what only rendering shows: `render_exception` (naming the node), `action_error`,
`interaction_failed`, `tap_no_reaction`, `layout_overflow`, `offscreen`, `text_clipped`, `text_truncated`,
`text_no_color`, `missing_glyph`, `icon_not_drawn`, `expression_not_evaluated`, `path_overflow`, `font_fallback`,
`font_missing`, `fill_fallback`, `image_failed`, `image_network`, `empty_screen`, `invalid_json`,
`component_missing`, `set_overwritten`. Links to a screen that is missing are one `unknown_screen` per screen, with
how many links name it. Formulas are
parsed by the SDK's own parser there, so formula syntax errors and unknown names in formulas are reported only by
the render command.



<a id="render-patterns"></a>
## Patterns

<a id="render-a-loop-that-converges"></a>
### A loop that converges

Validate and render after each section, read the diagnostics, then look at the PNGs next to the target: validation
cannot tell you that a page is ugly. Fix by the JSON pointer each line gives. Capture each state with its own
`--label` so the files do not overwrite each other.

<a id="render-capturing-states"></a>
### Capturing states

The annual price: `--tap billingSwitch --label annual`. An open menu at phone width: `--sizes 390x844 --tap
menuButton --label menu`. An error state: `--type seats=0 --unfocus --label error`. A value set directly:
`--set annual=true`. A detail page with its parameter: `--navigate speaker?id=ada --full-page`. A reordered list or
a slider: `--drag handle#0=0,120`, `--drag volume=80,0`. A countdown before the event: `--now
2026-11-13T09:00:00Z`.

<a id="render-what-a-run-keeps"></a>
### What a run keeps

Storage, variables and the clipboard live in memory for one run: steps and `--navigate` see what earlier steps
wrote, and each size starts afresh, as does each run (nothing persists between runs, so a "restored on reload"
state is captured by writing it first: `--tap save --navigate home`). `downloadFile` saves its file under
`<out>/downloads/<capture>/` and `copyToClipboard` copies in memory; both are listed in the output and in the
diagnostics file (`downloads`, `clipboard`). `openLink` opens nothing.

<a id="render-comparing-with-a-reference"></a>
### Comparing with a reference

`--compare <dir>` picks, for each capture, the PNG of the same size whose name is the screen and the state exactly
(`section--saved--390x844.png` for `--label saved`, never `section--saved-empty`); with no `--label`, `default` or
no state. When the reference names a page otherwise, map it: `--compare-map home=index`.

<a id="render-pitfalls"></a>
## Pitfalls

- Every diagnostic is about the page as it renders at that size: its media rules applied, what scrolls there, what
  an ancestor clips away.
- The command does not fetch network images or fonts: put the files beside `site.json` and name them by their
  relative path.
- A `--tap` scrolls the target into view; a `--full-page` capture still starts at the top.
- Runs on one SDK checkout take turns (each waits for the one before): start several, and they finish one after
  another.

<a id="render-see-also"></a>
## See also

[The base](#page-base) · [responsive layout](#page-layout) · [components](#components-rendering-one-part).

<a id="page-values"></a>
# Value types, models and enums

<a id="values-when-to-use"></a>
## When to use

Looking up how one value is written: a value type (a colour, an alignment, insets), a model no feature page shows
(its fields) or an enum (its names). Link to one with `values.md#type-<Name>` or `values.md#enum-<Name>`. Models
that belong to a feature are on that feature's page (TextStyle on the theme page, InputDecoration on the forms
page...); the [A–Z](#index-a-z) finds any of them.

<a id="values-minimal-example"></a>
## Minimal example

Value types are written in a compact form of their own; models are objects; enums are names:

```json
{"color": "#FF2563EB", "padding": [16, 8, 16, 8], "alignment": [0, -1], "fit": "cover"}
```

<a id="values-reference"></a>
## Reference

Decoding is lenient and never fails: a value it cannot read becomes the field's default, which is why validation
reports it.

<a id="values-value-types"></a>
### Value types

<a id="type-Alignment"></a>
### Alignment

JSON: [x, y] from -1 to 1, or a name: topLeft, topCenter, topRight, centerLeft, center, centerRight, bottomLeft, bottomCenter, bottomRight.

Flutter's `Alignment`: -1 (start) to 1 (end) per axis. JSON: `[x, y]`.

<a id="type-AxisPosition"></a>
### AxisPosition

JSON: a number (distance from the start) or {"start": d}, {"end": d}, {"start": a, "end": b}, {"align": -1..1}, {"relative": d}.

Where a child of a freeform (stack) parent sits on one axis, as Flutter's `Positioned` or `Align`, in the parent's padded box:

* `{"start": d}`: d from the start edge;

* `{"end": d}`: d from the end edge;

* `{"start": a, "end": b}`: stretched between the two;

* `{"align": t}`: aligned like `Align`, -1 (start) to 1 (end), by its laid-out size;

* `{"relative": d}`: d from the start at design size, keeping its share of the free space (measured with the design sizes) as the parent resizes. A text that lays out wider than designed stays where it was put, which `align` wouldn't do.

<a id="type-AxisSize"></a>
### AxisSize

JSON: a number (fixed) or {"fill"|"flexible"|"hug"|"fixed": number}.

Sizing along one axis. `value` is the design size: the size for `SizeFit.fixed`, and the fallback whenever a mode can't apply. JSON: a number (fixed) or `{"fill"|"flexible"|"hug": value}`.

<a id="type-BorderRadius"></a>
### BorderRadius

JSON: a number (every corner), [x, y] (every corner elliptical) or [topLeft, topRight, bottomRight, bottomLeft] (each a number or [x, y]).

Flutter's `BorderRadius`: four corners, each circular or elliptical. JSON (sparse, see `fromJson`): `8`, `[16, 8]` or `[8, [16, 8], 0, 0]`.

<a id="type-BoxConstraints"></a>
### BoxConstraints

JSON: {"minWidth", "maxWidth", "minHeight", "maxHeight"} (each optional, numbers >= 0).

Flutter's `BoxConstraints`, where a missing bound means unconstrained.

<a id="type-Color"></a>
### Color

JSON: "#AARRGGBB" or "#RRGGBB" (hex, alpha first).

A 32-bit ARGB color, as Flutter's `Color`. JSON: `"#AARRGGBB"` (`"#RRGGBB"` and ints also read), or the name of one of the project's theme colors (`"ember"`: `ThemeTokens.colors`, resolved before the document renders; see `resolveThemeRefs`).

<a id="type-EdgeInsets"></a>
### EdgeInsets

JSON: a number (all sides) or [left, top, right, bottom].

Flutter's `EdgeInsets` (left, top, right, bottom). JSON: a number (all sides) or `[left, top, right, bottom]`.

<a id="type-FontFeature"></a>
### FontFeature

JSON: an OpenType tag ("tnum", "ss01") or "tag=value" ("liga=0").

<a id="type-FontWeight"></a>
### FontWeight

JSON: 100, 200 ... 900.

<a id="type-IconData"></a>
### IconData

JSON: a Material icon name ("check_circle", "lock_open_rounded"), an image URL, or {"type": "MATERIAL_ICON", "name", "style"}.

<a id="type-Offset"></a>
### Offset

JSON: [dx, dy].

An offset. JSON: `[dx, dy]`.

<a id="type-Rect"></a>
### Rect

JSON: [left, top, width, height].

<a id="type-Size"></a>
### Size

JSON: [width, height].


<a id="values-models"></a>
### Models

Objects with declared fields. Keys not listed are reported by validation (`unknown_field`).

<a id="type-AnimationRepeat"></a>
### AnimationRepeat

`controller.repeat(reverse:, count:)`. `count` 0 repeats forever; a count ends at the end of its last run. JSON: `{}` (forever), `{"reverse": true, "count": 3}`; `true` and a bare count read too.

| Key | Type | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `reverse` | bool | `false` |  |  |
| `count` | int | `0` | ≥ 0 | 0: forever. |

<a id="type-AnimationTrack"></a>
### AnimationTrack

One tween a `NodeAnimation` drives: a property at a binding `path` of a node, or a `variable`.

The value at the controller's value `v` (after the animation's curve): `u` is `v` inside `interval` (`Interval(begin, end)`), eased by `curve` (`CurveTween`); then `wave`s added to `from`, else the `keyframes` (`TweenSequence`), else `Tween(begin: from, end: to)` at `u`. A missing `from` or `to` is the property's own value (an entrance gives only `from`), or `blend`'s identity when the track adds or multiplies. Numbers interpolate and, as `Tween<double>` does, carry on past the ends on a curve that overshoots (`elasticOut`); colors interpolate; any other value switches at the end.

On a replacing track a wave's amplitude is a share of the way from `from` to `to` (the property's own value when `to` is omitted): `{"from": 0, "wave": [{}]}` swings a property between its own value and as far the other way, once a run (a pendulum). On an adding or multiplying track it is in the property's own units.

| Key | Type | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | String | `""` |  | Stable within its animation, so an edit can address it (`animations.enter.tracks.fade.from`). Optional. |
| `path` | String | `""` |  | A binding path (`motion.rotate`, `opacity`, `decoration.fills[0].color`). |
| `node` | String | `""` |  | The target node's id or key; empty: the node the animation is on. |
| `variable` | String | `""` |  | Instead of `path`: a number variable the value is written to. |
| `from` | Object | unset |  | A number, a color or an expression; empty: the property's own value. |
| `to` | Object | unset |  | `Tween(begin:, end:)`: numbers, colors, or `${...}` expressions read when a play starts. |
| `keyframes` | List<[Keyframe](#type-Keyframe)> | `[]` |  |  |
| `wave` | List<[Wave](#type-Wave)> | `[]` |  |  |
| `interval` | List<double> | `[0,1]` |  | `Interval(begin, end)`. |
| `curve` | [AnimationCurve](#enum-AnimationCurve) | `"linear"` |  |  |
| `blend` | [TrackBlend](#enum-TrackBlend) | `"replace"` | `replace`, `add`, `multiply` |  |
| `interpolation` | [KeyframeInterpolation](#enum-KeyframeInterpolation) | `"linear"` | `linear`, `monotoneCubic` | How `keyframes` are joined. |

<a id="type-Flight"></a>
### Flight

How a hero that flies in place (`HeroFlies.inPlace`) flies in from where the node with its tag was: on a spring by default (the node's `motion` transition's, when it has one with a spring), or, with a `duration`, along a curve that rises `lift` (or `liftShare` of the distance, the larger) above the higher end (as Flutter's `MaterialRectArcTween` bends a hero's path), swelling to `swell` at the middle and spinning `turns` times (toward the way it flies), trailing `trail` fading dots.

| Key | Type | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `duration` | int | `0` | ≥ 0 | 0: on the node's spring. |
| `curve` | [AnimationCurve](#enum-AnimationCurve) | `"easeInOut"` |  |  |
| `lift` | double | `0` |  | Rise of the path's control point above the higher end (px). |
| `liftShare` | double | `0` |  | The same as a share of the distance flown (the larger wins). |
| `swell` | double | `1` | ≥ 0 | Scale at the middle of the flight. |
| `turns` | double | `0` |  | Turns over the flight, clockwise when flying right. |
| `trail` | int | `0` | ≥ 0 | Fading dots left behind. |
| `trailColor` | [Color](#type-Color) | `"#FFFFC83D"` |  |  |

<a id="type-GesturePhysics"></a>
### GesturePhysics

How a node moves on its own once the pointer lets go, the same for a `DragMotion`, a `DragSource`'s return and a `TransformGesture`: a fling that slows by `friction` (Flutter's `FrictionSimulation`), a stretch of `overscroll` past the bounds, and a `spring` onto the `snap` target nearest to where the fling would stop.

| Key | Type | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `spring` | [Spring](#type-Spring) | `{}` |  | The spring it settles on. |
| `fling` | bool | `true` |  | Whether a release keeps the pointer's velocity and coasts. |
| `friction` | double | `0.865` | ≥ 0, ≤ 1 | The share of a fling's speed lost per second. |
| `minFlingVelocity` | double | `50` |  | Pixels per second: slower releases don't fling; the fastest start. |
| `maxFlingVelocity` | double | `8000` |  | Pixels per second: slower releases don't fling; the fastest start. |
| `overscroll` | double | `0.5` | ≥ 0, ≤ 1 | How far it stretches past its bounds (0 a hard stop, 1 free). |
| `snap` | [GestureSnap](#type-GestureSnap) | unset |  |  |

<a id="type-GestureSnap"></a>
### GestureSnap

The places a released node settles at (`GesturePhysics.snap`).

| Key | Type | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `kind` | [SnapKind](#enum-SnapKind) | `"points"` | `points`, `grid`, `edges` |  |
| `points` | List<[Offset](#type-Offset)> | `[]` |  | Offsets from rest. |
| `gridX` | double | `0` | ≥ 0 | For `SnapKind.grid`: the pitch per axis; 0 doesn't snap that axis. |
| `gridY` | double | `0` | ≥ 0 | For `SnapKind.grid`: the pitch per axis; 0 doesn't snap that axis. |

<a id="type-Keyframe"></a>
### Keyframe

One stop of a `TweenSequence`: the track's `value` at `at` (0–1 of the track's run), reached on `curve` from the stop before it.

| Key | Type | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `at` | double | `0` | ≥ 0, ≤ 1 |  |
| `value` | Object | unset |  |  |
| `curve` | [AnimationCurve](#enum-AnimationCurve) | `"linear"` |  |  |

<a id="type-PathFollow"></a>
### PathFollow

A place along an SVG path: `progress` (0–1) of the way along `path`'s length, turned with it as `orient` says. Shared by `motion.path` and a drag track's path.

Values of `progress` outside 0–1 wrap round a closed path (one that ends where it starts) and clamp to the ends of an open one.

JSON: `{"path": "M0 0 C 40 -60, 120 -60, 160 0", "progress": 0.5, "orient": "tangent"}`; a bare string reads as `path`.

| Key | Type | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | String | `""` |  | SVG path data. |
| `viewBox` | List<double> | `[]` |  | The path's coordinate space `[width, height]`, stretched over the node's parent; empty: pixels from the node's place. |
| `progress` | double | `0` |  | 0–1 of its length; wraps on a closed path. |
| `orient` | [PathOrient](#enum-PathOrient) | `"none"` | `none`, `tangent`, `upright` |  |

<a id="type-Pose"></a>
### Pose

A `Motion` drawn with a fade and a blur: the pose a page of a page view (`pageMotion`) or a side of a route transition is drawn at. Flutter: a `Transform` in an `Opacity` in an `ImageFiltered`. JSON: `motion`'s keys with `opacity` and `blur` beside them, flat (`{"shiftX": -1, "opacity": 0.5}`).

| Key | Type | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `translateX` | double | `0` |  | Pixels. |
| `translateY` | double | `0` |  | Pixels (`Transform.translate(offset:)`). |
| `shiftX` | double | `0` |  | Times the node's size (`FractionalTranslation`). |
| `shiftY` | double | `0` |  | Multiples of the node's own size (`FractionalTranslation`). |
| `scale` | double | `1` |  | The axis factors multiply `scale`. |
| `scaleX` | double | `1` |  | `Transform.scale(scale:, scaleX:, scaleY:)`: the axis factors multiply `scale`. |
| `scaleY` | double | `1` |  | `Transform.scale(scale:, scaleX:, scaleY:)`: the axis factors multiply `scale`. |
| `rotate` | double | `0` |  | Degrees, about z. |
| `rotateX` | double | `0` |  | Degrees, in 3D. |
| `rotateY` | double | `0` |  | Degrees. `rotate` turns about z (`Transform.rotate`); `rotateX` and `rotateY` turn in 3D, seen with `perspective` (0 flat). |
| `perspective` | double | `1` |  | How strongly a 3D rotation is seen in depth (0 flat). |
| `alignment` | [Alignment](#type-Alignment) | `[0,0]` |  |  |
| `backfaceHidden` | bool | `false` |  | Not painted while its back faces the viewer (through every transform above it too). |
| `path` | [PathFollow](#type-PathFollow) | unset |  |  |
| `opacity` | double | `1` | ≥ 0, ≤ 1 | 0–1. |
| `blur` | double | `0` | ≥ 0 | A layer blur's radius. |

<a id="type-Spring"></a>
### Spring

Flutter's `SpringDescription`: either the physical triple (`SpringDescription(mass:, stiffness:, damping:)`, when `stiffness` and `damping` are both given) or `SpringDescription.withDurationAndBounce` (`duration` ms, `bounce`). The one spring value of the model: transitions, animations, gestures, a flip card's settle and a route's dismiss all take it. JSON: `{"stiffness": 380, "damping": 36}` or `{"duration": 500, "bounce": 0.3}` (sparse; `{}` is `withDurationAndBounce()`'s defaults).

| Key | Type | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `stiffness` | double | unset |  | The physical spring's constants; both null: `duration` and `bounce`. |
| `damping` | double | unset |  | The physical spring's constants; both null: `duration` and `bounce`. |
| `mass` | double | `1` |  |  |
| `duration` | int | `500` | ≥ 1 | `withDurationAndBounce`: ms, and 0 (none) to 1. |
| `bounce` | double | `0` |  |  |

On-canvas handles that make a node an editable object (a sticker, a collage): corners scale it, edges stretch it, a knob rotates it.

| `rotateKnob` | bool | `true` |  |  |

<a id="type-TransitionReveal"></a>
### TransitionReveal

A clip that reveals a screen as a transition plays: a circle or rectangle growing from `origin` until it covers the screen.

<a id="type-TransitionSide"></a>
### TransitionSide

How one screen moves during a `RouteTransition`: an entering screen starts at `motion` and comes to rest; a leaving one starts at rest and ends at `motion` (a `Pose`: a transform, `shiftX`/`shiftY` in screen sizes, with an opacity and a blur); this side's `curve`, `delayMs` and `durationMs` time it inside the route's duration.

| Key | Type | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `motion` | [Pose](#type-Pose) | `{}` |  | The values it moves from (entering) or to (leaving). |
| `reveal` | [TransitionReveal](#type-TransitionReveal) | unset |  |  |
| `curve` | [AnimationCurve](#enum-AnimationCurve) | `"fastOutSlowIn"` |  |  |
| `delayMs` | int | `0` | ≥ 0 | Milliseconds into the transition this side starts. |
| `durationMs` | int | unset |  | Null: to the end. |

<a id="type-Wave"></a>
### Wave

A sine added to a track's value: `amplitude * sin(2π(cycles·t + phase))`, fading by `1 − decay·t` (a shake dies out with decay 1), folded to its absolute value with `rectify` (a ball's hops). Flutter has no counterpart; a list of them is a Fourier series: a wobble, a sway, a flame's flicker.

| Key | Type | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `cycles` | double | `1` |  |  |
| `amplitude` | double | `1` |  |  |
| `phase` | double | `0` |  |  |
| `decay` | double | `0` |  |  |
| `rectify` | bool | `false` |  |  |

| Value | Meaning |

| Value | Meaning |

| `centered` | How a series chart places its grid lines (and solid reference lines). `centered`: centred on the value's rounded y (the bottom line one pixel row up, inside the plot); a 1 px line there straddles two pixel rows. `crisp` (the default): whole pixel rows from the value's rounded y down (the bottom line's up, inside the plot), so a line of whole width is sharp; other widths stay centred on the value. `exact`: the rows just above the value's unrounded y, like a Flutter box of that height whose bottom edge sits at the value (sharp when that is a whole pixel, soft otherwise). |
| `crisp` | How a series chart places its grid lines (and solid reference lines). `centered`: centred on the value's rounded y (the bottom line one pixel row up, inside the plot); a 1 px line there straddles two pixel rows. `crisp` (the default): whole pixel rows from the value's rounded y down (the bottom line's up, inside the plot), so a line of whole width is sharp; other widths stay centred on the value. `exact`: the rows just above the value's unrounded y, like a Flutter box of that height whose bottom edge sits at the value (sharp when that is a whole pixel, soft otherwise). |
| `exact` | How a series chart places its grid lines (and solid reference lines). `centered`: centred on the value's rounded y (the bottom line one pixel row up, inside the plot); a 1 px line there straddles two pixel rows. `crisp` (the default): whole pixel rows from the value's rounded y down (the bottom line's up, inside the plot), so a line of whole width is sharp; other widths stay centred on the value. `exact`: the rows just above the value's unrounded y, like a Flutter box of that height whose bottom edge sits at the value (sharp when that is a whole pixel, soft otherwise). |

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `click` | A tap (a click with a mouse). `${result}` holds where it landed (`x`, `y` in the node, `globalX`, `globalY`) and the modifier keys held (`meta`, `shift`, `alt`). |
| `doubleTap` | Two taps in quick succession. A node with double tap reactions waits out the double tap timeout before its single taps run. |
| `longPress` | A long press. |
| `hold` | A press held for `Trigger.holdMs`; letting go early cancels it. |
| `secondaryClick` | A right click, or a two-finger tap on a trackpad (`${result.x}`, `${result.y}`: where, on screen). |
| `pointerDown` | A pointer went down on the node. |
| `pointerUp` | A pointer went up (or was canceled) on the node. |
| `hover` | The mouse cursor moved over the node (fires when it enters, too). |
| `cursorEnter` | The mouse cursor entered the node (once). |
| `cursorExit` | The mouse cursor left the node (once). |
| `swipeLeft` | A swipe (a fling) to the left, right, up or down. |
| `swipeRight` |  |
| `swipeUp` |  |
| `swipeDown` |  |
| `drag` | The node is dragged (every move); `dragEnd` when it's let go. |
| `dragEnd` |  |
| `wheel` | Wheel or trackpad scroll over the node; a pinch on it. |
| `pinch` |  |
| `changed` | An input's value changed (typed text, a toggled checkbox, a slider step, a picked item). `${result}` is the new value (a text field's: its text, word and selection). |
| `changeEnd` | A slider was let go, with its final value. |
| `submitted` | A text field was submitted from the keyboard. |
| `editingComplete` | A text field lost focus after editing. |
| `focusGained` | A text field gained or lost focus. |
| `focusLost` |  |
| `load` | A screen appeared (set on its canvas). |
| `imageLoading` | A node's image fill started loading, became ready, or failed. `${result.url}` identifies the image and `${result.status}` is `loading`, `loaded`, or `error`. Cached images can report loaded immediately without a loading event. |
| `imageLoaded` |  |
| `imageError` |  |
| `backPressed` | On a screen (its canvas): the user tried to leave it (the system or browser back button, a back gesture, Escape on a dialog) while the canvas's `blockBack` holds (`props.blockBack`, usually bound: `${= dirty}`). The screen stays and these actions run instead, e.g. a "Discard changes?" confirm that leaves with a navigate pop, which the block doesn't stop. While `blockBack` is false, back leaves as usual and this doesn't fire. |
| `valueChanged` | Variable `Trigger.variable` changed while the screen shows. |
| `timer` | Every `Trigger.intervalMs` while the screen shows (`Timer.periodic`) and `Trigger.when` holds; `${result.tick}` counts. |
| `frame` | Every frame while the node is on stage and `Trigger.when` holds (a `Ticker`): `${result.dt}` (ms since the tick this chain last got), `${result.elapsed}` (ms since it started), `${result.frame}`. A frame that comes while the chain still runs is skipped; its time goes to the next `dt`. A design canvas never ticks. |
| `keyDown` | A key went down (or up) while the screen shows; `Trigger.key` limits it to one key or combination, `Trigger.when` to while a formula holds. `${result.key}`, `${result.shift}`, `${result.alt}`, `${result.meta}`. |
| `keyUp` |  |
| `scroll` | The node (a scrolling row, column or canvas) scrolled (`${result.offset}`, `${result.max}`, `${result.fraction}`), or came near its end (load the next page). |
| `scrollEnd` |  |
| `enterViewport` | At least `Trigger.visibleFraction` of the node became visible (and stayed so for `Trigger.visibleMs`), or it fell below that after being visible. With `Trigger.onceKey` (`${item.id}`), an impression: once per item per app session. |
| `exitViewport` |  |
| `dragStart` | Drag and drop: on a draggable (start, cancel, completed) and on a drop target (drop, enter, exit, rejected). `${result}` and `${drag}` hold the drag. A list with a `reorder` fires `dragStart` when a row is picked up and `dragCompleted` when it is let go (moved or not), with `${result.index}` and `${result.item}`: a list can change while a row is lifted (fold its rows into tiles). On a node with a `drag` reaction (and no drag and drop), `dragStart` is the start of that one-finger drag, where the finger went down (`${drag.x}`, `${drag.y}`): begin a stroke there rather than on `pointerDown`, which fires for every finger of a pinch. |
| `dragCancel` |  |
| `dragCompleted` |  |
| `drop` |  |
| `dragEnter` |  |
| `dragExit` |  |
| `dropRejected` |  |
| `reorder` | A data list row was dragged to a new place by this node, its reorder handle (`${result.from}`, `${result.to}`). A list with a `reorder` fires it too, with `${result.item}`, `${result.fromList}`, `${result.toList}`. |
| `refresh` | A list or grid was pulled past its start to refresh (its `pullToRefresh`, or its pagination's); its pagination reloads its first page too. A list with this reaction can always be pulled. |
| `swipeAction` | A swipe action of a list item ran (the list's `swipeActions`): `${result.action}`, `${result.label}`, `${result.item}`, `${result.index}`. |
| `rowTap` | A table view's body row was tapped: `${result.row}` (the row's data), `${result.rowIndex}`, `${result.column}` (the tapped column's key), `${result.columnIndex}`. |
| `actionError` | On the current canvas: a failed action chain or cloud subscription. `${result.error}` is `{type, message, action, nodeId}` (no stack or raw service objects). A failure in this reaction reports to the host without recursively firing another actionError reaction. |
| `event` | On a component call: the component fired its event `Trigger.event` (a `componentEvent` action inside its definition); `${result}` is the event's payload. Flutter: the callback passed to a widget's `onChanged`-style parameter. The handler runs in the caller's scope. |

| `pass` | A line at `ViewProgress.from` of the viewport passes over the node, from its leading edge (0) to its trailing edge (1). |

<a id="enum-WriteOp"></a>
### WriteOp

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `set` | Replaces the value with `ValueWrite.value`. |
| `toggle` | Flips a boolean. |
| `add` | A number: adds; a list: appends (each item of a list value); a map: merges in a map value. |
| `subtract` | A number: subtracts. |
| `insert` | A list: inserts the value at `ValueWrite.index`. |
| `insertAll` | A list: inserts each item of a list value at `ValueWrite.index`. |
| `removeAt` | A list: removes the item at `ValueWrite.index`. |
| `remove` | A list: removes the items equal to the value; a map: removes key `ValueWrite.mapKey`. |
| `update` | A list: sets the item at `ValueWrite.index` (appends at the length); a map: sets key `ValueWrite.mapKey`. |

<a id="enum-WidgetState"></a>
### WidgetState

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `hovered` | A pointer is over the node. |
| `focused` | The node, or an input in it, has keyboard focus. |
| `pressed` | A pointer is pressing the node. |

| `disabled` | Its `disabled` binding is true; a disabled node runs no actions. |

<a id="enum-Join"></a>
### Join

`and`, `or`


<a id="values-patterns"></a>
## Patterns

<a id="values-colours-and-alignments"></a>
### Colours and alignments

A colour is `"#AARRGGBB"`, `"#RRGGBB"` or a theme colour's name. An alignment is `[x, y]` from -1 to 1 or a name
(`"topCenter"`, `"centerRight"`).

<a id="values-pitfalls"></a>
## Pitfalls

- Padding and margin are a number or four numbers; a list of two is not read.
- An enum value is case sensitive.
